contenido: Can. 1 . The canons of this Code refer to all and only the Eastern Catholic Churches, unless, with regard to relations with the Latin Church, something else is expressly established.
Can. 2 . The canons of the Code, in which the ancient law of the Eastern Churches is generally received or adapted, must be evaluated primarily on the basis of that law.

Can. 3 . The code, although it often refers to the provisions of the liturgical books, does not generally decide on liturgical questions; Therefore, these provisions must be diligently observed, unless they are contrary to the canons of the Code.

Can. 4 . The canons of the Code do not abrogate or repeal the agreements entered into or approved by the Holy See with nations or other political associations; Therefore, it will continue to be in force as at present, without prejudice to the contrary provisions of the Code.

Can. 5 . The claimed rights and privileges, which have been granted by the Apostolic See to natural or legal persons up to this time and have not been revoked, remain intact, unless expressly revoked by the canons of the Code.

Can. 6 . With the entry into force of the Code: 1° all laws of common law or private law that are contrary to the canons of the Code, or that refer to the matter fully regulated in the Code, are repealed; 2. All customs condemned by the canons of the Code or contrary to them and that are not centuries old or forgotten are remembered. TITLE I. CHRISTIANS AND THE RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF ALL THEIR

Can. 7 . § 1 . The faithful are those who, having been incorporated into Christ through baptism, have been constituted as the people of God, and in this way participate in their own way in the priestly, prophetic and royal role of Christ. § 2 . This Church exists in this world as a society established and organized in the Catholic Church governed by the successor of Peter and the Bishops in communion with him.

Can. 8 . Those baptized in full communion with the Catholic Church in these lands are those who, in their visible framework, are united to Christ by the bonds of the profession of faith, the sacraments and the ecclesiastical government.

Can. 9 . § 1 . In a special way, the catechumens are linked to the Church, who, moved by the Holy Spirit, seek with an explicit will to join it, and therefore, by this same will and by the life of faith, hope and charity that they practice, they are linked to the Church, which already welcomes them as its own. § 2 . The Church has a special concern for catechumens, who, while inviting them to lead an evangelical life and introducing them to participation in the divine liturgy, sacraments and divine praise, already grants them the various prerogatives proper to Christians.

Can. 10 . Adhering to the Word of God and the living and authentic teaching of the Church, the Christian faithful are obliged to keep the faith intact, guarded and transmitted at an immense price by their elders, and to profess it openly, as well as to understand it more by practicing it and to make it fruitful in works of charity.

Can. 11 . Among all the Christian faithful, since their regeneration in Christ, a true equality of dignity and action prevails, by which all work together according to their respective condition and role for the building up of the Body of Christ.

Can. 12 . § 1 . The Christian faithful are bound by the obligation of their individual conduct to always maintain communion with the Church. § 2 . They fulfill with great diligence the obligations imposed on them towards the entire Church and towards their own autonomous Church.

Can. 13 . All Christians, according to their individual circumstances, must contribute their energies to leading a holy life and promoting the growth of the Church and the sanctification of its ranks.
Can. 14 . All Christians have the right and obligation to work so that the divine message of salvation reaches more and more to all men of all times and to the entire world.

Can. 15 . § 1 . What the Pastors of the Church, representatives of Christ, declare as teachers of the faith, or establish as leaders of the Church, the Christian faithful are obliged to pursue Christian obedience, aware of their own responsibility. § 2 . It is integral to the Christian faithful, such as their needs, especially spiritual, and their desires. Let them make it clear to the pastors of the church. § 3 . Because of the knowledge, competence and excellence with which they are powerful, it is their right, even, and sometimes their obligation, to express their opinion on things that pertain to the good of the Church to the Pastors of the Church and, with integrity of faith and morals and reverence for the Pastors themselves and attention to the common good and the dignity of the people, to make it known to the rest of the Christian faithful.
Can. 16 . It is the right of the Christian faithful to receive from the Pastors of the Church the help of the spiritual goods of the Church, especially the word of God and the sacraments.

Can. 17 . It is the right of the Christian faithful to perform divine worship according to the prescriptions of their own independent Church and to follow their own way of spiritual life in accordance with the doctrine of the Church.

Can. 18 . It is characteristic of the Christian faithful to freely establish and moderate associations for purposes of charity or piety, or for the promotion of the Christian vocation in the world, and to hold meetings for the common achievement of the same goals.

Can. 19 . All Christian faithful, by participating in the mission of the Church, have the right to promote or support apostolic activity with their own initiatives, according to their individual status and condition; However, no company may claim the Catholic name for itself, unless the consent of the competent ecclesiastical authority has been obtained.

Can. 20 . The faithful, called by baptism to lead a life consistent with the doctrine of the Gospel, have the right to a Christian education, through which they can continue the maturity of the human person and at the same time be adequately instructed to know and live the mystery of salvation.

Can. 21 . Those who dedicate themselves to the sacred sciences enjoy fair freedom to investigate and to prudently open their minds to those in which they have experience, observing due obedience to the teachings of the Church.
Can. 22 . All Christians have the right to be free from any coercion when choosing a state of life.
Can. 23 . No one may illegitimately damage the good reputation enjoyed by anyone or violate the right of any person to protect their privacy.

Can. 24 . § 1 . It is the duty of the Christian faithful to legitimately claim and defend the rights they have in the Church in a competent ecclesiastical forum in accordance with the law. § 2 . It is also the right of Christians, if they are called to trial by competent authority, to be judged by observing the provisions of the law and applying them equitably. § 3 . It is the right of the Christian faithful not to be punished with canonical penalties but in accordance with the law.

Can. 25 . § 1 . The Christian faithful are obliged to attend to the needs of the Church, so that those necessary for their own purposes are at its disposal, especially for divine worship, for works of apostolate and charity, and for the adequate support of ministers. § 2 . They also have the obligation to promote social justice, as well as to help the poor with their own income, remembering the commandments of the Lord.

Can. 26 . § 1 . In the exercise of their rights, the Christian faithful, both individually and united in associations, must take into account the common good of the Church, as well as the rights of others and their obligations towards others. § 2 . It is the duty of the ecclesiastical authority to regulate, with a view to good, the common exercise of the rights of the Christian faithful. TITLE II OF THE CHURCHES OF THEIR LAW AND THE RITE

Can. 27 . In this Code, an independent Church is called a group of Christians united by a hierarchy to the rule of law, who expressly or tacitly are recognized as independent by the supreme authority of the Church.

Can. 28 . §1 . The rite is a liturgical, theological, spiritual and disciplinary heritage distinct from the culture and circumstances of the history of the people, which is expressed in the way of living the faith of each independent Church. § 2 . The rites discussed in the Code are, unless otherwise indicated, those that have their origin in the Alexandrian, Antiochene, Armenian, Chaldean and Constantinopolitan traditions. CHAPTER I. OF THE SUBSCRIPTION OF A CHURCH OF ITS RIGHT

Can. 29 . § 1 . A child who has not yet reached fourteen years of age is enrolled by baptism in the independent Church to which his Catholic father is enrolled; but if only the mother is Catholic, or if both parents request it with the consent of their will, it is registered in the independent Church to which the mother belongs, except for a particular law established by the Apostolic See. § 2 . However, if the child, who has not yet reached fourteen years of age, is: 1. born of an unmarried mother, is enrolled in the Church in his own right, to which the mother belongs; 2° of unknown parents, is assigned by right to the Church, to which those to whose care it is legally entrusted are attributed; but if it is the father and mother who adopt, § 1 applies; 3rd of unbaptized parents, is enrolled in the Church by his own right, to which he who received his education in the Catholic faith belongs.

Can. 30 . Anyone who is to be baptized, who has reached the age of fourteen, may freely choose any independent Church to which he or she is registered through baptism, except for a special law established by the Apostolic See.
Can. 31 . No one should seek in any way to induce any Christian to move to another independent Church.

Can. 32 . § 1 . No one can validly transfer to another independent Church without the consent of the Apostolic See. § 2 . But if it is an eparchy faithful to Christ of an independent Church that requests the transfer to another independent Church that has its own eparchy in the same territory, this consent of the Apostolic See is presumed, provided that the eparchial bishops of both eparchies agree in writing to the transition.

Can. 33 . It is fair that a woman go to Church independently of her husband when celebrating her marriage or during it; but once the marriage is dissolved, he can freely return to the old independent Church.

Can. 34 . If the parents or a Catholic spouse in a mixed marriage move to another independent Church, children under fourteen years of age are automatically enrolled in the same Church; However, if in a marriage between Catholics only one of the parents passes to another independent Church, the children only pass if both parents consent; but after fourteen years of age the children can return to the old independent Church.

Can. 35 . Non-Catholic baptized people who are suitable for full communion with the Catholic Church must preserve their own rite throughout the world and worship and observe it according to their strength, so they must register in the Church independent of the same rite, with the exception of the right to go to the Apostolic See in special cases of individuals, communities or regions.

Can. 36 . Any transition to another Church is autonomous from the moment of the declaration made before the local Hierarch of the same Church or the pastor itself or a priest delegated by any of them and two witnesses, unless a written declaration from the Apostolic See indicates otherwise.

Can. 37 . Any subscription to any independent church or transition to another independent church will be noted in the baptism book of the parish, including, if applicable, of the Latin church where the baptism was celebrated; If this is not possible, preserving it in another document in the parish archive of the parish priest of the independent Church to which the registration was made.

Can. 38 . The Christian faithful of the Eastern Churches, although entrusted to the care of a Hierarch or a parish priest of another independent Church, continue to be permanently enrolled in their own independent Church. CHAPTER II OF THE OBSERVANCE OF THE RITE

Can. 39 . The rites of the Eastern Churches, as the heritage of the entire Church of Christ, in which tradition shines from the Apostles to the Fathers, and which affirms the divine unity of the Catholic faith in diversity, must be observed and promoted religiously.

Can. 40 . § 1 . The hierarchs who preside over the independent Churches, and all other hierarchs, will ensure with the greatest fervor the faithful custody and exact observance of their own rite, and will not admit changes in it except by reason of their organic progress, keeping in mind, however, the mutual benevolence and unity of Christians. § 2 . All other clerics and members of institutes of consecrated life are obliged to faithfully observe their own rite and to acquire from day to day greater knowledge and more perfect use. § 3 . The other Christian faithful must also foster knowledge and appreciation of their own rites, and are obliged to observe them everywhere, unless something is prohibited by law.

Can. 41 . The faithful of any independent Church, including the Latin Church, who by virtue of their office, ministry or function have frequent relations with the faithful of another independent Church, must be instructed in the knowledge and worship of the rites of the same Church exactly according to the gravity of the office, ministry or function they perform. TITLE III OF THE SUPREME AUTHORITY OF THE CHURCH

Can. 42 . As by decree of the Lord Saint Peter and the other Apostles constitute a single College, the Roman Pontiff, successor of Peter, and the Bishops, successors of the Apostles, are united with each other in the same way. CHAPTER I OF THE ROMAN PONTIFICAL

Can. 43 . The Bishop of the Roman Church, in which the office of the Lord was singularly granted to Peter, the first of the Apostles, and which is to be transmitted to his successors, is the head of the Episcopal College, the Vicar of Christ and the Pastor of the entire Church in these lands, who enjoys, therefore, the supreme, full, immediate and universal power of his office in the Church, which he may always exercise freely.

Can. 44 . § 1 . The Roman Pontiff obtains supreme and full power in the Church through a legitimate election accepted by him together with an episcopal ordination; so he obtains the same power from the moment of acceptance, when he is elected to the supreme pontificate, which is distinguished by its episcopal character; but if the chosen one lacks episcopal character, he is immediately ordained bishop. § 2 . If it happens that the Roman Pontiff resigns his position, for its validity it is required that the resignation be made freely and duly manifest, but not that it be accepted by anyone.

Can. 45 . § 1 . The Roman Pontiff, by virtue of his office, not only enjoys power over the entire Church, but also has authority over all the eparchies and their ordinary power groups, thereby at the same time strengthening and vindicating the proper, ordinary and immediate power that the bishops have entrusted to the eparchies in their care. § 2 . The Roman Pontiff, in his office as Supreme Pastor of the entire Church, is always united with the other Bishops and the entire Church, in full communion; They themselves have the right to determine, according to the needs of the Church, whether this function should be exercised personally or collegially. § 3 . There is no appeal or appeal against the decision or decree of the Roman Pontiff.

Can. 46 . § 1 . In carrying out his function, the Roman Pontiff has bishops available, who can provide him with a cooperative effort in various ways, among which is the Synod of Bishops; In addition, he is assisted by the cardinal fathers, the Roman court, the papal legates, as well as other people and also various institutions according to the needs of the times; that all people and institutions, in its name and authority, fulfill the task that has been entrusted to them for the good of all the Churches, according to the norms established by the Roman Pontiff himself. § 2 . The participation of the Patriarchs and other Hierarchs who preside over the independent Churches in the Synod of Bishops is governed by special norms established by the Roman Pontiff himself.
Can. 47 . With the Roman See vacant or completely obstructed, nothing is new in the government of the entire Church; but the special laws issued for the same circumstances will be observed.

Can. 48 . The name of Apostolic See or Holy See in this Code includes not only the Roman Pontiff, but also, unless otherwise provided by law or determined by the nature of the matter, the departments and other institutions of the Roman Curia. CHAPTER II OF THE COLLEGE OF BISHOPS

Can. 49 . The Episcopal College, whose head is the Roman Pontiff, and whose members are Bishops by virtue of sacramental ordination and hierarchical communion with the head and members of the College and in which the apostolic body continues continually, exists together with its head and never without him, being also the subject of supreme and full power over the entire Church.

Can. 50 . § 1 . The Episcopal College exercises power over the entire Church in a solemn manner in the Ecumenical Council. § 2 . The same power is exercised by the College of Bishops through the united action of the Bishops dispersed throughout the world, which has been directed as such by the Roman Pontiff or has been received freely, so that a true collegial act is carried out. § 3 . According to the needs of the Roman Pontiff, it is appropriate to select and promote the methods by which the Episcopal College exercises its function collegially throughout the Church.

Can. 51 . § 1 . Only the Roman Pontiff has the power to convene an Ecumenical Council, to preside over it by himself or through others, to transfer, suspend or dissolve the Council and to confirm its decrees. § 2 . It is up to the Roman Pontiff himself to determine the matters to be discussed in the Ecumenical Council and to establish the order that must be observed in the same Council; To the questions proposed by the Roman Pontiff, the Fathers of the Ecumenical Council can add others that will be approved by the Roman Pontiff himself.

Can. 52 . § 1 . It is the right and obligation of all and only of the Bishops who are members of the Episcopal College to participate in the Ecumenical Council with a deliberative vote. § 2 . Furthermore, to the Ecumenical Council some who are not distinguished by episcopal dignity may be called by the supreme authority of the Church, which is responsible for determining their parts in the Council.

Can. 53 . If it happens that the Apostolic See becomes vacant during the celebration of the Ecumenical Council, it is automatically interrupted until the new Roman Pontiff orders the continuation of the Ecumenical Council or dissolves it.

Can. 54 . § 1 . The decrees of the Ecumenical Council have no binding force, unless they have been approved by the Roman Pontiff together with the Fathers of the Council, confirmed by him and promulgated by order of the same. § 2 . With this confirmation and promulgation, to have binding force, they also need the decrees carried by the Episcopal College, when it establishes the properly collegial action according to another method dictated by the Roman Pontiff or freely received. TITLE IV OF THE PATRIARCHAL CHURCHES

Can. 55 . According to the oldest tradition of the Church, already recognized by the first Ecumenical Councils, the patriarchal institution prevails in the Church; Therefore, the Patriarchs of the Eastern Churches, who preside as father and head of their respective Patriarchal Church, must be persecuted with singular honor.

Can. 56 . The patriarch is the bishop, who has power over all the bishops, without exception of the metropolitans and the rest of the faithful of the Church, over whom he presides, in accordance with the law approved by the supreme authority of the Church.

Can. 57 . § 1 . The establishment, restoration, alteration and suppression of patriarchal Churches is reserved to the supreme authority of the Church. § 2 . A title legitimately recognized or granted to each of the patriarchal churches can only be modified by the supreme authority of the church. § 3 . A patriarchal church within the limits of its own territory must have a fixed seat of residence of the Patriarch in the princely state, from which the Patriarch takes his title, if possible, established; This seat cannot be transferred except for the most serious reason, with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church and the assent of the Roman Pontiff.
Can. 58 . The Patriarchs of the Eastern Churches throughout the world precede all Bishops of any rank, subject to special rules of precedence established by the Roman Pontiff.

Can. 59 . § 1 . The patriarchs of the Eastern Churches, although some are later than others in time, are all equal in dignity to the patriarchs, except for their precedence of honor among them. § 2 . The order of precedence among the ancient Patriarchal Sees of the Eastern Churches is that first comes the See of Constantinople, then that of Alexandria, then that of Antioch and finally that of Jerusalem. § 3 . Among the other Patriarchs of the Eastern Churches, precedence is ordered according to the seniority of the Patriarchal See. § 4 . Among the Patriarchs of the Eastern Churches, who have the same title, but preside over different Patriarchal Churches, the one who was first promoted to the patriarchal dignity has priority.

Can. 60 . § 1 . The Patriarch in the churches intended for the faithful of the Church over which he presides, and in the liturgical celebrations of the Church itself, precedes the other Patriarchs, even if they are superior in title to the See or superior in promotion. § 2 . The patriarch who actually holds patriarchal power precedes those who still hold the title of the patriarchal seat he once held.
Can. 61 . The Patriarch may have a representative before the Apostolic See appointed by him with the prior consent of the Roman Pontiff.

Can. 62 . The patriarch who has resigned from office retains his title and honors, especially in liturgical celebrations, and also has the right to be assigned a suitable place of residence with his consent and to be provided with the means of the property of the Patriarchal Church, which are provided for his support in accordance with his own title, with a signature on the precedence Can. 60 , § 2 . CHAPTER I OF THE ELECTION OF THE PATRIARCHS
Can. 63 . The Patriarch is canonically elected at the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church.
Can. 64 . By particular right, those things that are required are listed for one to be considered fit for patriarchal dignity, always saving those that are prescribed in Can. 180.

Can. 65 . § 1 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church must meet at the patriarchal residence or at another place designated by the Administrator of the Patriarchal Church with the consent of the permanent Synod. § 2 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church must meet within the month following the vacancy of the Patriarchal See, a longer period being established by firm law, but not exceeding two months. Can. 66 n - § 1 . In the election of the Patriarch, all and only the members of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church have an active voice. § 2 . It is prohibited to participate in the election of the Patriarch at the court to anyone other than the members of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, except for those clerics who, according to the norm Can. 71 , § 1 , are assumed as tellers or actuaries of the Synod. § 3 . No one can interfere in any way either before the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or during the election of the Patriarch.
Can. 67 . In the election of the Patriarchs, the cann. 947 - 957 rejected contrary to custom must be observed, unless otherwise provided by common law.

Can. 68 . § 1 . All legitimately convened Bishops have the serious obligation to participate in the election. § 2 . If any bishop believes that he is detained by a just impediment, he must present his reasons in writing to the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church; The legitimacy of the impediment must be decided by the bishops present at the designated place at the beginning of the Synod sessions.

Can. 69 . In a canonically made convocation, if two of the three parts of the bishops who are obliged to attend the synod of bishops of the patriarchal church, except those who are detained by legitimate impediment, are present at the designated place, the synod is declared canonical and the election may proceed.

Can. 70 . Unless the particular law establishes otherwise, the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church presides over the election of the Patriarch, who is chosen from among those present at the first session; Meanwhile, the presidency is reserved for the administrator of the patriarchal Church.

Can. 71 . § 1 . Tellers and actuaries may also be appointed among the priests and deacons, according to the norm of particular law. § 2 . Regarding those issues that are directly or indirectly related to the elections, all those who participate in the Synod have a serious obligation to maintain secrecy.

Can. 72 . § 1 . The person who has obtained two-thirds of the votes will be elected, unless it is established by special law that after an adequate number of ballots, at least three, an absolutely significant part of the votes is sufficient and the election is completed in accordance with the rules of Can. 183 , §§ 3 and 4. § 2 . If the election does not take place within fifteen days after the beginning of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, the matter passes to the Roman Pontiff.

Can. 73 . The election, if at least one legitimately proclaimed bishop has been elected, is announced immediately by the president or, if the president is elected, by the bishop by principal episcopal ordination of the entire synod of bishops of the Patriarchal Church in the name of the formula and only after having been received into his own Patriarchal Church. but if the chosen one has not yet been legitimately proclaimed bishop, preserving the secret of all those who know in any way the result of the election, including with respect to the elected ones, the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church is suspended and notification is made, if everything required by the canons for episcopal proclamation has been fulfilled.

Can. 74 . The elected person must declare within two business days from the date of notification whether he or she accepts the election; but if he does not accept, or if he does not respond within two days, he loses all the right he had obtained from the election.

Can. 75 . If he has accepted the election and is ordained a bishop, the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church will proceed according to the provisions of the liturgical books to proclaim and enthrone him as Patriarch; but if the chosen one has not yet been ordained bishop, the enthronement cannot take place before the chosen one has received episcopal ordination.

Can. 76 . § 1 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church will inform the Roman Pontiff as soon as possible, by synodal letters, of the canonical election and enthronement and of the profession of faith and the promise to faithfully fulfill his duty issued by the new Patriarch before the Synod according to approved formulas; The synodal letters about the finalized election are also sent to the patriarchs of the other Eastern Churches. § 2 . The new Patriarch must request ecclesiastical communion from the Roman Pontiff as soon as possible by means of a letter signed in his own handwriting.

Can. 77 . § 1 . A canonically elected patriarch exercises his office validly only upon his enthronement, so he obtains the office by full right. § 2 . The Patriarch, before receiving ecclesiastical communion from the Roman Pontiff, must not convene a Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or ordain bishops. CHAPTER II OF THE RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF THE PATRICIANS

Can. 78 . § 1 . The power that the Patriarch, according to the norm of legitimate canons and customs, has over the Bishops and the other faithful of the Church over which he presides, is ordinary and proper, but so personal that he cannot establish a Vicar for the entire Patriarchal Church or delegate his power to someone for all cases. § 2 . The power of the Patriarch can only be validly exercised within the territory of the Patriarchal Church, unless the nature of the matter or the common or particular law approved by the Roman Pontiff determines otherwise.
Can. 79 . In all legal matters of the Patriarchal Church, the Patriarch leads the person of the Church.

Can. 80 . It is the duty of the Patriarch: 1° to exercise the rights and fulfill the obligations of the Metropolitan in all places where provinces have not been established; 2° make up for the negligence of the metropolitans by law; 3° exercise the rights and fulfill the obligations of the Metropolitan in the vacant metropolitan seat throughout the province; 4° Reprimand the Metropolitan, who has not designated the financial person responsible according to the Can. 262, § 1 standard; warning in case of bankruptcy to appoint the financier himself.

Can. 81 . The acts of the Roman Pontiff relating to the Patriarchal Church will be made known to the eparchial Bishops or other persons to whom they belong, through the Patriarch, unless the Apostolic See has directly decided in the case.

Can. 82 . § 1 . The patriarch may in his own right: 1° issue decrees within the scope of his competence, by means of which the methods of observance of the applicable law are determined with greater precision or the observance of the laws is enforced; 2° give instructions to the faithful of the entire Church, regarding those under their charge, expound sound doctrine, encourage piety, correct abuses and approve and recommend practices that promote the spiritual good of the faithful; 3° give encyclical letters to the entire Church, for which it is responsible, on issues related to the Church itself and the rite. § 2 . The Patriarch may order bishops and other clerics, as well as members of the institutes of consecrated life of the entire Church over which he presides, that his decrees, instructions and encyclical letters be read and displayed publicly in their own churches or homes. § 3 . In all matters concerning the entire Church over which he has charge, or more serious matters, the Patriarch must not fail to listen to the Permanent Synod, or the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, or even the Patriarchal Assembly.

Can. 83 . § 1 . In addition to the right and obligation of the eparchial bishop to canonically visit his own eparchy, the Patriarch has the right and obligation to carry out the pastoral visit in the same eparchy at the times established by particular law. § 2 . The patriarch may, for grave cause and with the consent of the permanent Synod, visit any church, city or eparchy by himself or through another bishop and, at the time of this visit, carry out everything that is proper to the eparchial bishop in a canonical visit.

Can. 84 . § 1 . The Patriarch will take great care that he or the eparchial bishops of the church over which he presides, in connivance with the councils, especially in the meetings provided for by law, with the patriarchs and eparchial bishops of other independent churches that exercise their power in the same territory, promote unity of action between themselves and the other Christian faithful of any independent church, and with united forces help the common works for the most expeditious promotion of the good of religion, for the more effective protection of ecclesiastical discipline and so that the unity of all Christians is fostered in harmony. § 2 . The Patriarch must also encourage frequent conferences between the Hierarchs and the other Christian faithful whom he considers prudent to convene, on pastoral matters and other matters that concern the entire Church under his responsibility, or any province or region.

Can. 85 . § 1 . For a serious reason, with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church and the consultation of the Apostolic See, the Patriarch may establish provinces and eparchies, delimit them in other ways, unite them, divide them, suppress them and change their hierarchical level and transfer the eparchial see. § 2 . The Patriarch, with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, has the right: 1° to give an eparchial bishop a coadjutor bishop or an auxiliary bishop, observing cann. 181 , § 1 , 182 - 187 and 212; 2° for serious reasons, transfer a Metropolitan or an eparchial or titular Bishop to another metropolitan, eparchial or titular see; If anyone refuses, the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church resolves the matter or refers it to the Roman Pontiff. § 3 . The Patriarch may, with the consent of the permanent Synod, erect, alter and suppress exarchies. § 4 . The Patriarch will inform the Apostolic See of these decisions as soon as possible.

Can. 86 . § 1 . It is the duty of the Patriarch: 1° to give patriarchal letters to the Metropolitan or the Bishop about the canonical provisions; 2° ordain the Metropolitan by himself or, if prevented, by other Bishops, as well as, if particular law so requires, also ordain all the Bishops; 3° Enthronement of the Metropolitan after episcopal ordination. § 2 . By right of the Patriarch, the Metropolitan and the other Bishops of the Church over which he presides have the power to ordain and enthrone those appointed by the Roman Pontiff outside the territory of the Church itself, unless otherwise expressly established in a special case. § 3 . Episcopal ordination and enthronement must take place within the limits established by law, while patriarchal letters relating to canonical provisions must be delivered within ten days following the proclamation of the election; of episcopal ordination and the enthronement of the Apostolic See as soon as possible.

Can. 87 . The Patriarch may ensure that in the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, according to the norms cann. 181 , §1 and 182 - 187, provided they are provided with adequate support, some Bishops of the patriarchal court are included, but not more than three, on whom he confers the office with residence in the patriarchal court, and he may ordain them after they have fulfilled all the requirements for episcopal proclamation.

Can. 88 . §1 . The bishops of the patriarchal church must show honor and respect to the patriarch and render him due obedience; The patriarch, however, must pursue those same bishops with equal reverence and embrace them with brotherly love. § 2 . The Patriarch will ensure that any controversies that may arise between the Bishops are resolved, with the firm right to refer them at any time to the Roman Pontiff.

Can. 89 . § 1 . It is the right and obligation of the patriarch to watch over all clergy in accordance with the law; If anyone seems to deserve punishment, let him warn the Hierarch, to whom the clergyman is immediately subject, and with the reprimand made against the clergyman himself proceed according to the law. § 2 . The Patriarch may entrust the management of matters that concern the entire Patriarchal Church to any clergyman consulted by his eparchial Bishop or, if he is a member of a religious institution or of a society of common life analogous to the religious one, to his Major Superior, unless the particular law of the Patriarchal Church requires such consent; You can also subdue this cleric directly to yourself during the function. § 3 . The patriarch may confer the dignity received in his own patriarchal church on any firm cleric Can. 430 , provided that he obtains the written consent of the eparchial bishop to whom the cleric is subject, or, if he is a member of a religious institution or of a society of common life analogous to the religious one, of his major superior.

Can. 90 . For serious reasons, the patriarch, after consultation with the eparchial bishop and with the consent of the permanent Synod, may exempt from the power of the eparchial bishop a place or a legal person, which does not belong to a religious institute, in the same act of erection, and immediately submit to it, regarding the administration of temporal goods, as well as the persons attached to the same place or legal person in all of them, which relate to their office or duty.

Can. 91 . The Patriarch must be mentioned in the Divine Liturgy and in the divine praises after the Roman Pontiff by all Bishops and other clerics, according to the provisions of the liturgical books.

Can. 92 . § 1 . The Patriarch will manifest his hierarchical communion with the Roman Pontiff, successor of Saint Peter, through the fidelity, veneration and obedience that are due to the supreme Pastor of the entire Church. § 2 . The patriarch must commemorate the Roman Pontiff as a sign of full communion with him in the Divine Liturgy and in the divine praises as provided in the liturgical books and ensure that it is done faithfully by all the bishops and other clerics of the Church over whom he is in charge. § 3 . It is a frequent custom of the Patriarch to meet with the Roman Pontiff, and according to specially established norms, to present to him a report on the state of the Church over which he presides, and within a year of his election, he then makes several visits to the City during his official visit, venerating the thresholds of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, and setting himself up as the successor of Saint Peter in primacy over the entire Church.
Can. 93 . That the patriarch resides in the seat of his residence, from which he may not be absent except for canonical cause.
Can. 94 . The Patriarch must celebrate the Divine Liturgy for the people of the entire Church over which he presides, on the festivals established by particular law.

Can. 95 . § 1 . The obligations of eparchial bishops, mentioned in Can. 196, also firmly bind the Patriarch to the other obligations of individual bishops. § 2 . The patriarch will ensure that the eparchial bishops faithfully fulfill their pastoral duties and reside in the eparchies they govern; will awaken your jealousy; If they have seriously offended in any matter, consult with them, unless the danger lies in delay, so as not to fail to warn the permanent Synod, and, if the warnings do not have the desired effect, refer the matter to the Roman Pontiff.
Can. 96 . Regarding prayers and exercises of piety, as long as they conform to the proper rite, the Patriarch in the entire Church over which he presides has the same power as the local Hierarch.

Can. 97 . The patriarch must carefully ensure the correct administration of all ecclesiastical property, a primary and firm commitment of each of the eparchial bishops, about which in Can. 1022 , § 1 .

Can. 98 . The Patriarch, with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church and with the prior consent of the Roman Pontiff, may enter into legal conventions established by the Apostolic See that do not conflict with civil authority; But the Patriarch cannot carry out the same agreements without having obtained the approval of the Roman Pontiff.

Can. 99 . § 1 . The patriarch will ensure that the personal statutes in the regions in which they are in force are observed by everyone. § 2 . If several Patriarchs in the same place use the power recognized or conferred in their Personal Statutes, it is in their best interest to act on matters of greater importance with a concerted plan.

Can. 100 . Matters that concern several eparchies and affect civil authority can be called by the Patriarch; but he cannot decide on them except after consulting the interested eparchial bishops, and with the consent of the permanent Synod; If the situation is urgent and there is not enough time to gather the members of the bishops of the permanent Synod, the bishops of the patriarchal court, if available, take turns in the case, otherwise the two eparchial bishops with the greatest seniority in episcopal ordination.

Can. 101 . The patriarch in his own eparchy, in the Stauropegian monasteries and also in places where neither the eparchy nor the exarchy has been established, has the same rights and obligations as the eparchial bishop. CHAPTER III OF THE SYNOD OF BISHOPS OF THE PATRIARCHAL CHURCH

Can. 102 . § 1 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church must be summoned all and only the ordained Bishops of the same Church, wherever they are appointed, excluding those mentioned in Can. 953, § 1, or those who have been punished with canonical penalties, as mentioned in cann. 1433 y 1434. § 2 . As regards eparchial bishops established outside the territory of the Patriarchal Church and titular bishops, their particular right may restrict their deliberative vote by the firm canons on the election of the Patriarch, bishops and candidates for office, as mentioned in Can. 149. § 3 . To expedite specific matters of the Patriarch in accordance with a particular law or with the consent of the current Synod, others, especially non-Bishop Hierarchs and experts, may be invited to express their opinions to the Bishops assembled in the Synod under the signature Can. 66, § 2.

Can. 103 . It is up to the Patriarch to convene and preside over the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church. Can. 104 n - § 1 . All bishops legitimately called to the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church are bound by grave obligation to attend the same Synod, except those who have already resigned their office. § 2 . If any bishop believes that he is detained by a just impediment, he must present his reasons in writing to the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church; The legitimacy of the impediment must be decided by the bishops present at the designated place at the beginning of the Synod sessions. § 3 . With the exception of the eparchial Patriarchs and Bishops still in office, at the end of the year eighty, the Bishops lose their deliberative vote in the Synod of Bishops and also in the election of Patriarchs and Bishops candidates for the positions mentioned in Can. 149. § 4 . In order for certain matters to be expedited by the Patriarch in accordance with a particular law or with the consent of the current Synod, others may be invited, especially non-Bishop Hierarchs and experts, to express their opinions to the Bishops assembled in the Synod under the signature Can. 66, § 2.
Can. 105 . For the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, none of the members of the same Synod can send a representative in his place, and none has more votes.

Can. 106 . § 1 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church must be convened whenever: 1° they must process matters that are the exclusive competence of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or for whose execution the consent of the same Synod is required; 2° The Patriarch deems it necessary with the consent of the permanent Synod; 3. It is required by at least one third of the partners of a given business, always preserving the rights of Patriarchs, Bishops and other people established by common law. § 2 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church must also be convened, if particular law so requires, on specific dates, even every year.

Can. 107 . § 1 . Unless a particular law requires a greater presence and the signature cann. 69, 149 et 183 , § 1 , each session of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church is canonical and each vote is valid if the majority of the Bishops who are obliged to participate in the same Synod are present. § 2 . The signatures cann. 72, 149 et 183, §§ 3 and 4 are members of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church to establish, through established norms, how many votes and scrutiny are required, so that synodal decisions obtain the force of law; otherwise, Can. 924 should be saved.

Can. 108 . § 1 . It is up to the Patriarch to open the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, as well as to transfer it, extend it, suspend it and dissolve it with the consent of the same Synod. § 2 . It is also the duty of the patriarch to prepare in advance the order to be observed by the members of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church in examining matters, and to submit it to the approval of the Synod at the beginning of the sessions. § 3 . During the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, each Bishop may add others to the proposed questions, if at least one third of the members participating in the Synod agree.
Can. 109 . Once the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church has begun, none of the Bishops may withdraw from the sessions of the Synod except for just cause approved by the Synod.

Can. 110 . § 1 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church is exclusively competent to approve laws for the entire Patriarchal Church, which gain force according to the norms Can. 150, §§ 2 and 3. § 2. The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church is the court for the Can. 1062 norm. § 3 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church carries out the election of the Patriarch, Bishops and candidates for the offices mentioned in Can. 149. § 4 . Administrative acts are not the responsibility of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, unless the Patriarch establishes otherwise for certain acts, or unless by common law some acts are reserved to the same Synod and to firm canons that require the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church.

Can. 111 . § 1 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church determines the form and timing of the promulgation of laws and the publication of decisions. § 2 . Likewise, the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church must decide on the preservation of secrecy regarding the acts and businesses debated in the cases established by common law. § 3 . The minutes of the laws and decisions are sent as soon as possible to the Roman Pontiff; Certain acts, or even all, will be shared with the other Patriarchs of the Eastern Churches regarding the judgment of the same Synod.

Can. 112 . § 1 . The promulgation of laws and the publication of decisions of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church are the responsibility of the Patriarch. § 2 . The authentic interpretation of the laws of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church until the future Synod of Patriarchs is consulted by the Permanent Synod.

Can. 113 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church will draw up its own statutes, which will provide for the secretariat of the Synod, for the preparatory commissions, for the order of procedure and for other means that consult more effectively to achieve the goal. CHAPTER IV OF THE PATRIARCHAL COURT

Can. 114 . § 1 . The patriarch must have a patriarchal court next to his seat, distinct from the court of the patriarch's eparchy, which consists of the permanent synod, the bishops of the patriarchal court, the ordinary court of the patriarchal church, the patriarchal financier, the patriarchal chancellor, the commission for liturgical affairs as well as other commissions that are attached to the patriarchal court by law. § 2 . The people belonging to the patriarchal tribunal may be chosen by the patriarch from among the clerics of the entire Church over which he presides, after consultation with his eparchial bishop or, if they are members of a religious institution or a society of common life analogous to the religious one, by his major superior. § 3 . The offices of both patriarchal courts, as far as possible, should not be accumulated in the same persons.

Can. 115 . § 1 . The permanent synod is made up of the patriarch and four bishops appointed for five years. § 2 . Three of these bishops are elected by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, among whom at least two must be from the eparchial bishops, while one is appointed by the Patriarch. § 3 . At the same time and in the same manner, as far as possible, four Bishops will be appointed, who will alternatively replace the disabled members of the permanent Synod in the order determined by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church.

Can. 116 . § 1 . It is the duty of the patriarch to convene a permanent synod and preside over it. § 2 . If the Patriarch cannot participate in the current Synod, the Bishop presides over the sessions of the Synod with the major episcopal ordination among the members of the Synod, redistributed in number of five according to the norm Can. 115 , § 3 . § 3 . If the permanent Synod must decide on a matter that affects the person of a bishop member of the same Synod, or his eparchy or office, he must be heard here, but in the Synod he must be replaced by another Bishop according to the norm Can. 115, § 3.
Can. 117 . The president and all other members of the permanent Synod who attended the Synod must sign the minutes of the Synod.
Can. 118 . Voting in a permanent Synod must be secret, if it involves people; in other cases, however, if at least one of the members expressly requests it.

Can. 119 . If a matter falling within the competence of the Permanent Synod is to be determined, while the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church is being held, the decision on this matter is reserved to the Permanent Synod, unless the Patriarch, with the consent of the Permanent Synod, considers it appropriate to entrust the decision to the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church.

Can. 120 . The permanent Synod must be convened on fixed dates, at least twice a year, and whenever the Patriarch considers it appropriate, and whenever it is necessary to accelerate matters for which common law requires the consent or advice of the Synod itself.

Can. 121 . If a permanent Synod cannot be established for serious reasons in the opinion of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, the Apostolic See will be informed and the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church will elect two Bishops, one of whom must be an eparchial Bishop, who will take turns with the Patriarch during the duration of the Permanent Synod.

Can. 122 . § 1 . For the administration of the property of the Patriarchal Church, the Patriarch, with the consent of the permanent Synod, appoints a patriarchal treasurer, distinct from the treasurer of the Patriarch's eparchy, who is faithful to Christ, expert in financial matters and of excellent integrity, except those who are related to the Patriarch by blood or affinity up to and including the fourth degree. § 2 . The patriarchal financier is appointed for a period determined by the particular law; cannot be removed from the Patriarch during his office except with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or, if there is danger in delay, of the permanent Synod. § 3 . The patriarchal financier must report each year in writing to the Permanent Synod the account of the administration of the outgoing year as well as the budget of income and expenses of the year that begins; An account of the administration must also be rendered whenever requested by the permanent Synod. § 4 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church may request from the patriarchal financier the account of the administration as well as the budget of income and expenses and submit it to its own examination.

Can. 123 . §1 . In the patriarchal court, a priest or deacon is appointed by the patriarch, with all exceptions, who, as patriarchal chancellor, is in charge of the patriarchal chancery and the archive of the patriarchal court, taking turns, if necessary, assisted by the person appointed by the patriarch. § 2 . In addition to the chancellor and his successors, who are notaries by virtue of their office, the Patriarch may also appoint other notaries for the entire Church over which he presides, to whom cann. 253 y 254 shall apply to all; which journalists will also be able to freely remove from office. § 3 . Around the archives of the patriarchal court are preserved cann. 256 - 260 .

Can. 124 . The liturgical commission, which must be held in every patriarchal church, and the other commissions prescribed for autonomous churches are instituted by the patriarch, are composed of persons appointed by the patriarch and are governed by the norms established by him, unless otherwise provided by law.

Can. 125 . The expenses of the patriarchal court are paid with the assets that the patriarch can use for this purpose; If these are not sufficient, the individual eparchies, as a measure to be determined by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, must contribute to the payment of the expenses. CHAPTER V. OF THE VACANT OR IMMEDIATE PATRIARCHAL SEE

Can. 126 . § 1 . The patriarchal seat becomes vacant due to the death or resignation of the Patriarch. § 2 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church is competent to accept the resignation of the Patriarch, in consultation with the Roman Pontiff, unless the Patriarch has addressed the Roman Pontiff directly.

Can. 127 . Unless a particular law provides otherwise, the Administrator of the Patriarchal Church when the Patriarchal See is vacant is the Bishop by episcopal ordination of greatest seniority among the Bishops of the Patriarchal Court or, if they are absent, among the Bishops who are members of the permanent Synod.

Can. 128 . It is the responsibility of the Administrator of the Patriarchal Church: 1. to immediately communicate the news of the vacancy of the Patriarchal See to the Roman Pontiff as well as to all the Bishops of the Patriarchal Church; 2° the special norms that, for the different situations in which the Patriarchal See has become vacant, the common or particular law or the instruction of the Roman Pontiff, if any, prescribe, to be exactly executed or to have others execute them; 3° to summon the bishops to the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church for the election of the Patriarch and to arrange all other things necessary for the same Synod.

Can. 129 . The Administrator of the Patriarchal Church in the eparchy of the Patriarch, in stauropegic monasteries and also in places where neither eparchy nor exarchy has been established, has the same rights and obligations as the Administrator of a vacant eparchy.

Can. 130 . § 1 . The ordinary power of the Patriarch passes to the Administrator of the Patriarchal Church, excluding all those who can only act with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church. § 2 . The Administrator of the Patriarchal Church cannot remove the Protosincellus or the Syncellus of the Patriarch's Eparchy from office, nor can he innovate anything by leaving the Patriarchal See vacant. § 3 . Although he lacks the prerogatives of the Patriarch, the Administrator of the Patriarchal Church precedes all the Bishops of the same Church, but not in the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, in the election of the Patriarch.
Can. 131 . The administrator of the patriarchal Church must report his management to the new Patriarch as soon as possible.

Can. 132 . § 1 . If the patriarchal see is so obstructed for any reason that the patriarch cannot even communicate by letter with the eparchial bishops of the church over which he presides, the government of the patriarchal church corresponds, according to the Can. 130 norm, to the eparchial bishop within the territory of the same church by the major episcopal ordination, who in turn is not obstructed, unless the patriarch appoints another bishop or, in case of extreme necessity, even a priest. § 2 . The patriarch being so hindered that he cannot communicate even by letters with the faithful of his own eparchy, the government of the same eparchy is under Protosincellus; but if he himself is prevented, it depends on him whom the Patriarch has appointed, or on who governs the patriarchal Church in the meantime. § 3 . Whoever has assumed the government in the meantime must inform the Roman Pontiff as soon as possible of the impeded Patriarchal See and of the assumed government. CHAPTER VI OF THE METROPOLITAN PATRIARCHAL CHURCH

Can. 133 . § 1 . The Metropolitan, who presides over a province within the limits of the territory of the Patriarchal Church, in the eparchies of this province, in addition to others attributed to him by common law, is responsible for: 1. Ordaining and enthroning the bishops of the province within the time determined by law by signature Can. 86, § 1, n. 2; 2° convene the Metropolitan Synod at the times established by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, arrange the issues to be discussed at the time, preside over the Synod, move it, extend it, suspend it and dissolve it; 3° create a metropolitan court; 4° ensure that faith and ecclesiastical discipline are faithfully observed; 5° carry out the canonical visit, if the eparchial bishop has neglected it; 6° appoint or confirm the person who has been legitimately proposed or elected for the position, if the eparchial Bishop has not done so within the period established by law, not being prevented by just impediment, and also appoint the eparchial treasurer, if the eparchial Bishop has not appointed him after having been warned. § 2 . In all legal matters of the province, the Metropolitan is in charge of the province.

Can. 134 . § 1 . The dignity of the metropolitan was always related to the specific eparchial seat. § 2 . A metropolitan in his own eparchy has the same rights and obligations as an eparchial bishop in his own.
Can. 135 . The Metropolitan must be commemorated by all Bishops and other clerics in the Divine Liturgy and in divine praises as provided in the liturgical books.
Can. 136 . The Metropolitan, who presides over the province, precedes the titular Metropolitan everywhere.

Can. 137 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church will determine more precisely the rights and obligations of Metropolitans and Metropolitan Synods according to the legitimate customs of the Patriarchal Church, as well as the circumstances of times and places.

Can. 138 . The rights and obligations of the Metropolitan established outside the territory of the Patriarchal Church are the same as in Can. 133, § 1, nos. 2 - 6 and § 2 as well as in cann. 135, 136, 160 et 1084 , § 3 are prescribed; As for other rights and obligations, the Metropolitan observes the special norms proposed by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church and approved by the Apostolic See or established by this same See.

Can. 139 . The eparchial bishop who exercises his authority outside the territorial limits of the patriarchal Church itself and does not belong to any province, may designate a Metropolitan with the consultation of the Patriarch and with the approval of the Apostolic See; This Metropolitan has the rights and obligations mentioned in Can. 133, § 1, nos. 3 - 6. CHAPTER VII OF THE PATRIARCHAL CONVENTION

Can. 140 . The Patriarchal Assembly is a consultative group of the entire Church, chaired by the Patriarch, which assists the Patriarch and the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church in the conduct of matters of greatest importance, especially for the forms and methods of the apostolate, as well as of ecclesiastical discipline, in accordance with the times and the common good of the Church itself, taking into account also the common good of the entire territory, where there are several independent Churches, to be properly compound.

Can. 141 . The Patriarchal Assembly must be convened at least every five years and with the consent of the Permanent Synod or the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, whenever the Patriarch considers it useful.

Can. 142 . § 1 . It is the duty of the patriarch to convene the patriarchal assembly, preside over it and move it, prorogue it, suspend it and dissolve it; The vice president, who presides over the assembly in the absence of the patriarch, will be appointed by the patriarch himself. § 2 . When the patriarchal seat becomes vacant, the patriarchal meeting is suspended by law, until the new Patriarch decides on the matter.

Can. 143 . § 1 . The following will be summoned to the patriarchal assembly: 1° The eparchial bishops and the other local hierarchs; 2nd titular bishops; 3° Presidents of monastic confederations, General Superiors of institutes of consecrated life and Superiors of independent monasteries; 4° the rectors of the universities of Catholic studies and of the universities of ecclesiastical studies, as well as the deans of the faculties of theology and canon law, who have their headquarters within the limits of the territory of the Church whose assembly is held; 5th directors of major seminaries; 6° of each eparchy at least one of the priests registered in the same eparchy, especially the parish priests, one of the religious or members of societies of common life analogous to the religious ones, as well as two lay people, unless the statutes determine a greater number, all of whom are designated in the manner determined by the eparchial bishop and, even, if they are members of a religious institution or of a society of common life analogous to the religious ones, with the consent of the competent Superior. § 2 . All those who are to be summoned to the patriarchal assembly must attend, unless they are detained due to just impediment, of which they are obliged to inform the patriarch; Eparchial bishops, however, may send a procurator in his place. § 3 . People from another independent Church may be invited to the patriarchal assembly and participate in it, in accordance with the statutes. § 4 . Various observers from non-Catholic churches or ecclesial communities may also be invited to the patriarchal meeting.

Can. 144 . § 1 . It is the firm right of every Christian to refer questions to the Hierarch, and only the Patriarch or the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church is responsible for determining the topics to be discussed in the Patriarchal Assembly. § 2 . It is the duty of the patriarchs to ensure, through appropriate preliminary consultations and commissions, that all questions are properly prepared and sent to the members of the assembly at the appropriate time.

Can. 145 . The Patriarchal Assembly will have its statutes approved by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, which will contain the necessary regulations for the purposes of the Assembly. CHAPTER VIII OF THE TERRITORY OF THE PATRIARCHAL CHURCH AND THE POWER OF THE PATRIARCH AND THE SYNODS OUTSIDE THIS TERRITORY

Can. 146 . § 1 . The territory of the Church, presided over by the Patriarch, extends to those regions in which the Church's own rites are observed and the Patriarch has the legitimately acquired right to erect provinces, eparchies and exarchies. § 2 . If doubt arises about the boundaries of the territory of the Patriarchal Church or if the change of the boundaries is discussed, it is the duty of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church to investigate the matter, after hearing the highest administrative authority of each independent Church that is interested, as well as the matter discussed in the Synod itself, to present a duly prepared petition regarding the resolution of the doubt or about the change of the boundaries to the Roman Pontiff, whose sole responsibility is to resolve the doubt authentically or to issue a decree on the change of boundaries. the limits.

Can. 147 . Within the limits of the territory of the Patriarchal Church, the power of the Patriarch and the Synods is exercised not only over all the Christian faithful enrolled in the same Church, but also over others who do not have a local Hierarch of their own independent Church established in the same territory and who, although permanently enrolled in their own Church, are entrusted with the care of the local Hierarchs of the same Patriarchal Church under the signature Can. 916 , § 5 .

Can. 148 . § 1 . It is the right and obligation of the patriarch, with respect to the faithful who reside outside the limits of the territory of the Church under his responsibility, to seek appropriate information also through the Visitor sent by him with the consent of the Apostolic See. § 2 . The visitor, before beginning his office, must go to the eparchial bishop of these Christians and present the letter of appointment. § 3 . Once the visit is over, the Visitor sends a report to the Patriarch, who, on the matter discussed in the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, can propose to the Apostolic See the appropriate means, so that the protection and growth of the spiritual good of the Christian Church that he is in charge of is provided throughout the world, also through the establishment of parishes and exarchies or eparchies of their own. Can. 149 n - The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, signed Can. 102 , § 3 , elects candidates, at least three, for the office of eparchial bishop, coadjutor bishop or auxiliary bishop outside the territory of the patriarchal church, and in accordance with the norms of the canons on the election of bishops, and proposes them for nomination through the Roman Patriarch Pontiff, held in secret of everyone who knows in some way the result of the elections, including the candidates.

Can. 149 . The candidates, at least three, to occupy the office of eparchial bishop, coadjutor bishop or auxiliary bishop outside the territory of the patriarchal church, are elected by the Synod of bishops of the patriarchal church in accordance with the canons on the election of bishops, and are proposed by the Roman Pontiff for nomination, kept secret from all who know in any way the result of the election, including the candidates.

Can. 150 . § 1 . Bishops appointed outside the territory of the Patriarchal Church have all the synodal rights and obligations of other Bishops of the same Church under the signature Can. 102 , § 2 . § 2 . The laws approved by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church and promulgated by the Patriarch, if they are liturgical laws, are valid throughout the world; but if they are disciplinary laws or if the other decisions of the Synod are in doubt, they have the force of law within the territory of the patriarchal Church. § 3 . The eparchial bishops outside the limits of the territory of the patriarchal Church, established by disciplinary laws and other synodal decisions that do not exceed their competence, wish to give force of law in their own eparchies; but if these laws or decisions have been approved by the Apostolic See, they have the force of law throughout the world. TITLE V. OF THE MAJOR ARCHBISHOPICAL CHURCHES

Can. 151 . An archbishop is a major Metropolitan of a See determined or recognized by the supreme authority of the Church, who presides over the whole of an independent Eastern Church not marked with the title of patriarch.

Can. 152 . What is said in common law about patriarchal churches or patriarchs is understood to be applicable to major archiepiscopal churches or major archbishops, unless expressly provided otherwise in common law or established by the nature of the matter.

Can. 153 . § 1 . A major archbishop is elected according to the cann. 63 - 74 norm. § 2 . After the acceptance of the elect, the Synod of Bishops of the major archiepiscopal Church must inform the Roman Pontiff of the canonically completed election by means of synodal letters; but the chosen one himself must request confirmation of his election from the Roman Pontiff by means of a signed letter in his own handwriting. § 3 . Once confirmation has been received, those elected must make before the Synod of Bishops of the major archbishopric a profession of faith and a promise to faithfully fulfill their duty, and then proceed to their proclamation and enthronement; but if the chosen one has not yet been ordained bishop, the enthronement cannot take place before the chosen one has received episcopal ordination. § 4 . But if confirmation is rejected, a new election must be held within the period set by the Roman Pontiff.

Can. 154 . Immediately after the patriarchs, the major archbishops have priority of honor according to the order of establishment of the church over which they preside, in a major archiepiscopal church. TITLE VI OF METROPOLITAN CHURCHES AND OTHER CHURCHES OF OWN RIGHT CHAPTER I OF METROPOLITAN CHURCHES OF OWN RIGHT

Can. 155 . § 1 . The autonomous Metropolitan Church is presided over by a Metropolitan of a specific see appointed by the Roman Pontiff and assisted by a Council of Hierarchs in accordance with law. § 2 . It is the exclusive authority of the Supreme Church to erect, alter and suppress independent metropolitan churches and to limit their territory to certain limits.

Can. 156 . § 1 . Within three months following episcopal ordination or, if he has already been ordained bishop, counting from the enthronement, the Metropolitan has the obligation to request the mantle from the Roman Pontiff, which is a sign of his metropolitan power and of the full communion of the independent metropolitan Church with the Roman Pontiff. § 2 . Before the imposition of the mantle, the Metropolitan cannot convene the Council of Hierarchs and ordain the Bishops.

Can. 157 . § 1 . The power that the Metropolitan has according to the law over the Bishops and other Christian faithful of the Metropolitan Church that he presides is ordinary and proper, but so personal that he cannot establish an independent Vicar for the entire Metropolitan Church or delegate his power to someone for all cases. § 2 . The power of the Metropolitan and the Council of Hierarchs is only validly exercised within the territorial limits of the independent metropolitan Church. § 3 . In all legal matters of the independent Metropolitan Church, the Metropolitan is the same person.

Can. 158 . § 1 . The autonomous seat of the Metropolitan Church is in the main city, from which the Metropolitan, who presides over the same Church, takes his title. § 2 . The metropolitan has the same rights and obligations in the eparchy that has been entrusted to him as the eparchial bishop in his own.

Can. 159 . In the independent metropolitan Church that he presides, the Metropolitan, in addition to those assigned to him by common law or the particular law established by the Roman Pontiff, has the right to: 1° ordain and enthrone the bishops of the same Church within the time determined by law; 2° Convene a Council of Hierarchs in accordance with the law, order the issues that must be treated in the same way, preside over it and transfer it, extend it, suspend it and dissolve it; 3° create a metropolitan court; 4° ensure that faith and ecclesiastical discipline are faithfully observed; 5° carry out a canonical visit in the eparchies, if the eparchial bishop has neglected it; 6° appoint the Administrator of the eparchy in the case referred to in Can. 221, n. 4; 7° appoint or confirm who has been legitimately proposed or elected for the position, if the eparchial Bishop has not done so within the period established by law, without there being a just impediment, and also appoint the eparchial treasurer, if the eparchial Bishop has not appointed him after having been warned. 8° Communicate the acts of the Roman Pontiff to the eparchial Bishops and others to whom they belong, unless the Apostolic See has directly ordered it, and ensure the faithful execution of the provisions contained in these acts.
Can. 160 . In cases of extraordinary or special difficulty, the eparchial bishops must not fail to listen to the metropolitan and the metropolitan eparchial bishops.

Can. 161 . The Metropolitan is to be commemorated after the Roman Pontiff by all bishops and other clerics in the Divine Liturgy and in divine praises in accordance with the provisions of the liturgical books.

Can. 162 . The Metropolitan must commemorate the Roman Pontiff as a sign of full communion with him in the Divine Liturgy and in the divine praises as provided in the liturgical books and ensure that it is done faithfully by all the Bishops and other clerics of the Metropolitan Church over those under his charge.

Can. 163 . It is a frequent custom of the Metropolitan to be with the Roman Pontiff; but the visit, which must be carried out every five years according to Can. 208 , § 2 , as far as possible, must be made together with all the bishops of the metropolitan church over which he has charge.

Can. 164 . § 1 . The Council of Hierarchs must be summoned all and only the ordained Bishops of the same independent Metropolitan Church wherever they are appointed, excluding those mentioned in Can. 953, § 1, or those who have been punished with canonical penalties, mentioned in cann. 1433 y 1434; Bishops of another independent Church may only be invited as guests if the majority of the members of the Council of Hierarchs agree. § 2 . The eparchial bishops and the assistant bishops have a deliberative vote in the Council of Hierarchs; but the other bishops of the independent metropolitan Church may have this vote, if it is expressly established in a particular law.

Can. 165 . § 1 . All bishops legitimately called to the Council of Hierarchs are bound by grave obligation to attend the same Council, except those who have already resigned from their position. § 2 . If any bishop believes that he is detained due to a just impediment, he must present his reasons in writing to the Council of Hierarchs; The legitimacy of the impediment must be decided by the Bishops, who have a deliberative vote and are present in the place designated at the beginning of the Council sessions. § 3 . None of the members of the Council of Hierarchs can send a proxy in their place and no one has more votes. § 4 . When the Council of Hierarchs has begun, none of those who must attend may leave except for just cause approved by the President of the Council.

Can. 166 . § 1 . Unless a particular right requires a larger presence, each canonical session of the Council of Hierarchs and each vote is valid if the majority of the bishops who are obliged to attend the Council of Hierarchs are present. § 2 . Hierarchical business plan. corresponds to the absolute majority of the voters who have a deliberative vote and are present.

Can. 167 . § 1 . According to the firm canons, which expressly discuss the power of the Council of Hierarchs to dictate laws and regulations, this Council can issue them even in those cases in which the common law differs from the particular law of the independent Church. § 2 . The Metropolitan informs the Apostolic See as soon as possible of the laws and regulations approved by the Council of Hierarchs, and the laws and regulations cannot be validly promulgated before the Metropolitan has received written notification from the Apostolic See of the receipt of the minutes of the Council; The Metropolitan also informs the Apostolic See of the rest of the work in the Council of Hierarchs. § 3 . It is up to the Metropolitan to ensure the promulgation of laws and the publication of the decisions of the Council of Hierarchs. § 4 . In the firm canons, which expressly deal with the administrative acts of the Metropolitan, who presides over the autonomous metropolitan Church, it is also his responsibility to prescribe those administrative acts that are committed by common law to the superior administrative authority of the autonomous Church, but with the consent of the Council of Hierarchs.

Can. 168 . Regarding the appointment of Metropolitans and Bishops, the Council of Hierarchs will prepare for each case a list of at least three most suitable candidates and will send it to the Apostolic See, also to the candidates; To compose the list, the members of the Council of Hierarchs, if they so decide, may request the opinion of certain priests or other Christian believers who are distinguished by their wisdom regarding the needs of the Church and the special gifts of the candidates for the episcopacy.

Can. 169 . The Council of Hierarchs will ensure that the pastoral needs of the faithful are met and may make decisions regarding them that appear appropriate to promote the growth of faith, encourage common pastoral action, regulate morals, maintain its own rites and maintain common ecclesiastical discipline.

Can. 170 . The Council of Hierarchs will meet at least once a year, and whenever special circumstances require it, or matters reserved to this Council by common law, or whose execution requires the consent of the Council itself, they must be accelerated.

Can. 171 . The Council of Hierarchs must prepare its own statutes, which will be transmitted to the Apostolic See, which will provide for the secretaries of the Council, the preparatory commissions, the order of procedures and other means that allow for more effective consultation to achieve the goal.

Can. 172 . In the independent metropolitan church, a meeting is held according to the cann. 140 - 145 rule and is convened at least every five years; What is said about the Patriarch, the Metropolitans are competent.

Can. 173 . § 1 . The metropolitan see is vacant in independent metropolitan churches: 1° The administrator of the autonomous metropolitan church is the eparchial bishop of the same church, of higher episcopal ordination, who informs the Roman Pontiff as soon as possible about the vacancy of the metropolitan see; 2° the ordinary power of the Metropolitan passes to the Administrator of the independent Metropolitan Church, excluding all of them, which can only be done with the consent of the Council of Hierarchs; 3. Since the metropolitan headquarters is vacant, nothing is new. § 2 . In these Churches, the things established in Can. 132, § 1, in Can. 132, § 1 must be observed with reference to the Patriarchal See. What is said about the Patriarch, the Metropolitans are competent. § 3 . cann. 221 - 233 is observed around the vacant or obstructed seat of the Metropolitan Eparchy. CHAPTER II OF THE OTHER CHURCHES OF THEIR RIGHT

Can. 174 . The independent Church, which is neither patriarchal nor archiepiscopal nor metropolitan, is entrusted to the Hierarch who presides over it according to the norms of common law and particular law established by the Roman Pontiff.
Can. 175 . These churches depend directly on the Apostolic See; but the rights and obligations, of which in Can. 159, nos. 3 - 8, the Hierarch is delegated by the Apostolic See.

Can. 176 . If common law refers something to particular law or to a higher administrative authority of an independent Church, the competent authority in these Churches is the Hierarch who presides according to law, with the consent of the Apostolic See, unless expressly established otherwise. TITLE VII OF THE EPARCHIES AND BISHOPS CHAPTER I OF THE BISHOPS

Can. 177 . § 1 . An eparchy is a portion of the people of God, which is entrusted to the bishop to feed it with the cooperation of the presbytery, so that, adhering to its Pastor and gathered by him through the Gospel and the Eucharist in the Holy Spirit, it establishes a particular Church, in which the Church of Christ truly exists and works, one, holy, catholic and apostolic. § 2 . Can. 85, § 1 must be observed in the establishment, alteration and suppression of eparchies within the territory of the Patriarchal Church; In other cases the establishment, alteration and suppression of eparchies is the exclusive responsibility of the Apostolic See.

Can. 178 .
