The eparchial bishop, who of course has been entrusted with the feeding of the eparchy in his own name, governs it as vicar and legate of Christ; the power with which he acts personally in the name of Christ is his own, ordinary and immediate, although the exercise of the same power is ultimately governed by the supreme authority of the Church and may be circumscribed within certain limits in view of the benefit of the Church or of the faithful.

Can. 179 . Bishops who have not been entrusted with the eparchy to govern in their own name, whatever other office they hold or have held in the Church, are called titular bishops. Art. I ON THE ELECTION OF BISHOPS

Can. 180 . For a person to be considered suitable for the episcopate, he or she is required to be: 1° firm in faith, in good morals, in piety, in the zeal of souls and in prudence; 2° enjoy a good reputation; 3° not bound by the marriage bond; 4° be at least thirty-five years of age; 5° established for at least five years in the order of the presbytery; 6° a licensed doctor or at least an expert in some sacred science.

Can. 181 . § 1 . Bishops within the boundaries of the territory of the Patriarchal Church to fill a vacant eparchial position or to fill another office are appointed by canonical election in accordance with the norm cann. 947 - 957, unless customary law provides otherwise. § 2 . The other bishops are appointed by the Roman Pontiff with the signature cann. 149 y 168.

Can. 182 . § 1 . Only the members of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church can propose suitable candidates for the episcopate, and it is also their responsibility, according to the norm of particular law, to collect the information and documents necessary to verify the suitability of the candidates, after hearing them, whether they lead appropriately, secretly and individually to some priests or even other Christians who stand out for their prudence and Christian life. § 2 . The Bishops will communicate the information to the Patriarch at the appropriate time before the convocation of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church; But the Patriarch sends the matter to all the members of the Synod with his own information, if he has the opportunity to do so. § 3 . Unless a particular law approved by the Roman Pontiff provides otherwise, the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church examines the names of the candidates and draws up a list of candidates by secret ballot, which is sent by the Patriarch to the Apostolic See to obtain the approval of the Roman Pontiff. § 4 . The approval of the Roman Pontiff, once granted to each candidate, is valid until it is explicitly revoked, in which case the candidate's name must be removed from the list. Can. 183 n - § 1 . By the signature Can. 102 , § 3 , call made canonically, if two of the three parties of Bishops who are obliged to attend the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, except those who are detained by legitimate impediment, are present at the designated place, the Synod is declared canonical and the election may proceed. § 2 . Bishops must freely choose those they consider worthy and suitable before the Lord. § 3 . An absolutely larger part of the votes of those present is required for an election; After three ineffective votes, in the fourth vote votes are cast only for two candidates who obtained the majority of votes in the third vote. § 4 . If in the third or fourth vote it is not decided who is the candidate for the new vote or who is elected by equal votes, the tie will be broken in favor of whoever is the greatest according to the presbyteral ordination; If none precedes the others in priestly ordination, the oldest.

Can. 183 . § 1 . In a canonically made convocation, if two of the three parts of the bishops who are obliged to attend the synod of bishops of the patriarchal church, except those who are detained by legitimate impediment, are present at the designated place, the synod is declared canonical and the election may proceed. © Copyright 1990 - Vatican Publishing Copyright © Department of Communication Holy See Holy See

Can. 184 . § 1 . If he is chosen from among those on the list of candidates, to which the Roman Pontiff has already given his consent, the election is carried out by the Patriarch in secret to inform the chosen one. § 2 . If the elected have accepted the election, the Patriarch will immediately inform the Apostolic See of the acceptance of the election and the day of the proclamation.

Can. 185 . § 1 . If he is not chosen from among those on the list of candidates, the Patriarch will immediately notify the Apostolic See of the election made to obtain the approval of the Roman Pontiff, keeping it secret from all who know in any way the result of the election, including those elected, until information about the approval reaches the Patriarch. § 2 . Having obtained the consent of the Roman Pontiff, the Patriarch secretly hints at the election of the chosen ones and acts in accordance with the norms of Can. 184 , § 2 .

Can. 186 . § 1 . If the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church cannot meet, the Patriarch, in consultation with the Apostolic See, will request the votes of the Bishops by letter; in which case the Patriarch must rely for the validity of the act on the work of two scrutinized Bishops, who will be appointed according to the norm of particular law or, if there is none, by the Patriarch with the consent of the permanent Synod. § 2 . The tellers must open the bishops' letters, count the votes and sign the written report of the scrutiny carried out together with the Patriarch. § 3 . If any of the candidates in this single vote obtained an absolutely greater share of the votes of the members of the Synod, he will be considered elected and the Patriarch will proceed according to the rule Can. 184 or 185; Otherwise, the Patriarch must refer the matter to the Apostolic See.

Can. 187 . § 1 . To be promoted to the episcopate, a canonical provision is necessary, by which the eparchial bishop of a specific eparchy is appointed or another specific function is entrusted to him in the Church. § 2 . Before episcopal ordination, the candidate makes a profession of faith as well as a promise of obedience to the Roman Pontiff and in the patriarchal Churches also a promise of obedience to the Patriarch in those in which he is subject to the Patriarch according to the law.

Can. 188 . § 1 . Unless detained for legitimate impediment, he must receive episcopal ordination within three months from the day of proclamation, if elected, or receipt of apostolic letters, if nominated, to be promoted to the episcopate. § 2 . The eparchial bishop must take canonical possession of the eparchy within four months of his election or appointment.

Can. 189 . § 1 . The canonical possession of the eparchy is taken by the eparchial bishop after having legitimately carried out his own enthronement, in which the apostolic or patriarchal letters of the canonical disposition are read publicly. § 2 . A document of the complete enthronement, signed by the chancellor and at least two witnesses, must be drawn up by the eparchial bishop himself and kept in the archives of the eparchial court. § 3 . Before his enthronement, the bishop did not interfere in the government of the eparchy either by himself or by others or by any title; but if he has any position in the eparchy, he can retain and exercise it. Art. 2 OF THE RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF THE EPARCHIAL BISHOPS
Can. 190 . In all legal matters of the eparchy, the eparchial bishop is the same person.

Can. 191 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop must govern the eparchy that has been entrusted with legislative, executive and judicial power. § 2 . The eparchial bishop exercises legislative power himself; exercises executive power either by himself or by Protosincellus or Syncellis; judicial power either by itself or by the judicial deputy and the judges.

Can. 192 . § 1 . In the exercise of his pastoral office, the eparchial bishop must show concern for all the faithful who are entrusted to his care, regardless of their age, condition, nation or independent church, as well as for those who live in the territory of the eparchy and move at the same time in the same area. § 2 . In a special way, the eparchial bishop ensures that all the faithful entrusted to his care foster unity among Christians according to the principles approved by the Church. § 3 . The eparchial bishop must have those who are not baptized entrusted to him in the Lord, and must ensure that the charity of Christ also shines for them through the witness of the faithful who live in the ecclesiastical communion. § 4 . The eparchial Bishop will take special care of the priests whom he listens to as assistants and advisors, he will protect their rights and ensure that they fulfill the obligations inherent to their condition and that the means and institutions they need to foster their spiritual and intellectual life are at their disposal. § 5 . The eparchial bishop will ensure that clerics and their families, if married, receive adequate support and adequate social and preventive security, as well as health care, in accordance with the law.

Can. 193 . § 1 . An eparchial bishop, to whose care the Christian faithful of another independent Church are entrusted, has the heavy obligation to provide everything so that these Christian faithful preserve the rite of their own Church and worship and observe it for their strength and foster relations with the higher authority of the same Church. § 2 . Let the eparchial bishop attend to the spiritual needs of these faithful, if possible, through the priests or pastors of the independent Church itself and the faithful, or even through the Syncellus designated for the care of these faithful. § 3 . The eparchial bishops who appoint such priests, pastors or sincelos to take care of the Christian patriarchal Churches, enter into relations with the Patriarchs concerned and act with their own authority, in accordance with them, as soon as the Apostolic See makes decisions; but if the Patriarchs do not agree for any reason, the matter will be referred to the Apostolic See.
Can. 194 . The eparchial bishop can confer dignities on the clerics subject to him, to the exclusion of others, according to the norms of the particular law of his own Church.
Can. 195 . The eparchial bishop must encourage as far as possible the vocations of priests, deacons, monks and other members of the institutes of consecrated and missionary life.

Can. 196 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop is obliged to propose and illustrate the truths of faith that are to be believed and applied to the Christian faithful through his frequent preaching; He also ensures that the provisions of the law relating to the ministry of the word of God, particularly the homily and catechesis, are diligently observed, so that all Christian doctrine may be transmitted to all. § 2 . May the eparchial bishop firmly protect the integrity and unity of the faith.

Can. 197 . The eparchial Bishop, taking into account that he is obliged to set an example of holiness in charity, humility and simplicity of life, must strive with all his help to promote the holiness of the faithful according to their vocation and, as prime minister of the mysteries of God, he must ensure that the faithful, entrusted to his care, grow in grace through the celebration of the sacraments and, especially, with the participation of the Divine Eucharist, and fully know the paschal mystery and Live in such a way that you form a single Body in the unity of the love of Christ.

Can. 198 . The eparchial bishop must frequently celebrate the Divine Liturgy for the people of the eparchy entrusted to him; but he must celebrate the days prescribed by the particular law of his own independent Church.

Can. 199 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop, as director, promoter and custodian of all liturgical life in the eparchy entrusted to him, ensures that it is promoted to the extent possible and organized according to the legitimate prescriptions and customs of the independent Church. § 2 . The eparchial bishop will see to it that at least a part of the divine praises are celebrated in his own cathedral church, even every day, according to the legitimate customs of his own independent church; Likewise, that in each parish for the saints divine praises be celebrated on Sundays and holidays and on the main solemnities and their vigils. § 3 . The eparchial bishop frequently presides over divine praise in the cathedral or other church, especially on holy days of obligation and other solemnities, in which a considerable part of the people participate.

Can. 200 . The eparchial bishop must celebrate sacred functions throughout the eparchy, which according to the provisions of the liturgical books must be solemnly performed by him using all the pontifical insignia, but not outside the limits of his own eparchy without the express or at least reasonably presumed consent of the eparchial bishop.

Can. 201 . § 1 . Since he must protect the unity of the universal Church, the eparchial bishop is obliged to promote common ecclesiastical discipline, as well as to enforce the observance of all ecclesiastical laws and legitimate customs. § 2 . Let the eparchial bishop ensure that abuses are not introduced into ecclesiastical discipline, especially with regard to the ministry of the word of God, the celebration of sacraments and sacramentals, the worship of God and the saints and the execution of pious wills.

Can. 202 . The eparchial bishops of several independent Churches exercising their power in the same territory will ensure that, through collective council in periodic meetings, they foster unity of action and collaborate with united forces in common works to more quickly promote the good of religion and more effectively maintain ecclesiastical discipline.

Can. 203 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop must promote the various forms of apostolate in the eparchy and ensure that, throughout the eparchy or in the particular districts of it, all the works of apostolate are coordinated under his supervision, keeping in mind the specificity of each of them. § 2 . The eparchial Bishop underlines the obligation by which the faithful are obliged to exercise the apostolate according to their own condition and aptitude, and encourage them to participate and help in the various works of apostolate according to the needs of the place and time. § 3 . The eparchial bishop must promote associations of the faithful that directly or indirectly pursue a spiritual goal, if appropriate, establishing them, approving them, praising them or entrusting them in accordance with the law.

Can. 204 . § 1 . An eparchial bishop, even if he has a coadjutor bishop or an auxiliary bishop, has the obligation to reside in his own eparchy. § 2 . Except for reasons of obligation that legitimately require the absence of his own eparchy, an eparchial bishop may be absent from the eparchy for just cause each year for no more than one continuous month or one interruption, provided it is ensured that the eparchy suffers no loss by his absence. § 3 . But on the days of the most important solemnities established by particular law according to the tradition of his own Church, the eparchial bishop must not be absent from his own eparchy except for serious reasons. § 4 . If an eparchial bishop, exercising his power within the territory of the patriarchal Church, is unlawfully absent from the eparchy entrusted to him for more than six months, the patriarch shall immediately refer the matter to the Roman Pontiff; In other cases, the Metropolitan must do so, or, if the Metropolitan himself is illegitimately absent, the eparchial Bishop, by episcopal ordination, must be subject to the Metropolitan himself.

Can. 205 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop is obliged to canonically visit the eparchy, in whole or in part, every year, so that at least every five years he canonically visits the entire eparchy by himself or, if legitimately prevented, by a coadjutor bishop or by an auxiliary bishop or by a Protosincellus or Syncellus or by another priest. § 2 . Persons, Catholic institutions, things and sacred places that are within the limits of the eparchy are subject to the canonical visitation of the eparchial bishop. § 3 . The eparchial bishop may visit members of religious institutions as well as societies of common life as religious of pontifical or patriarchal right and their houses only in the cases expressed by law.

Can. 206 . § 1 . An eparchial bishop who exercises his power within the territorial limits of the patriarchal church is obliged to submit a report to the patriarch every five years on the state of the eparchy entrusted to him according to the method established by the synod of bishops of the patriarchal church; The Bishop sends a copy of the report as soon as possible to the Apostolic See. § 2 . The other eparchial bishops must present the same report to the Apostolic See every five years and, if they are the bishops of a patriarchal church or an independent metropolitan church, they must send a copy of the report to the patriarch or metropolitan as soon as possible.

Can. 207 . The eparchial bishop of any autonomous Church, including the Latin Church, will inform the Apostolic See, on the occasion of the quinquennial report, on the state and needs of the Christian faithful who, even if others are registered in the autonomous Church, are entrusted to his care.

Can. 208 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop who exercises his authority within the territory of the Patriarchal Church, within five years following his enthronement, will make a visit to the city, if possible together with the Patriarch, will venerate the thresholds of the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and present himself as successor of Saint Peter in the primacy over the entire Church. § 2 . The other eparchial bishops must make a visit to the city every five years by themselves or, if they are legitimately prevented, by another. But if it is the Bishops of a patriarchal Church, it is desirable that the visit be made at least several times together with the Patriarch.

Can. 209 . § 1 . The commemoration of the Roman Pontiff, above all, as a sign of full communion with him in the Divine Liturgy and in the divine praises, as provided in the liturgical books, must be carried out by the eparchial bishop and ensure that it is done faithfully by the other clerics of the eparchy. § 2 . The eparchial bishop must be commemorated by all clerics in the Divine Liturgy and in divine praises as provided in the liturgical books.

Can. 210 . § 1 . An eparchial bishop who has attained seventy-five years of age, or who has become less fit to perform his duties due to illness or any other serious reason, is requested to tender his resignation from office. § 2 . The resignation of the office of eparchial bishop must be presented to the Patriarch, if it is an eparchial bishop who exercises his authority within the territory of the patriarchal Church; In other cases, the resignation must be presented to the Roman Pontiff and, furthermore, if the Bishop belongs to the Patriarchal Church, it must be notified to the Patriarchs as soon as possible. § 3 . To accept the resignation, the Patriarch needs the consent of the current Synod, unless the invitation to resign has been preceded by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church.

Can. 211 . § 1 . An eparchial bishop, whose resignation from office has been accepted, obtains the title of bishop emeritus of the eparchy he governs and may maintain his seat of residence in the eparchy itself, unless, in certain cases, due to special circumstances, the Apostolic See or, in the case of an eparchy situated within the territory of the patriarchal Church, the Patriarch with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the patriarchal Church provides otherwise. § 2 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or the Council of Hierarchs must ensure that the bishop emeritus is provided with adequate and worthy support, taking into account the primary obligation to which the eparchy he served is linked. Art. 3 ON ADJUTATION BISHOPS AND AUXILIARY BISHOPS

Can. 212 . § 1 . If the pastoral needs of the eparchy so advise, one or more auxiliary bishops will be appointed at the request of the eparchial bishop. § 2 . In more serious circumstances, even of a personal nature, a coadjutor bishop endowed with special powers with the right of succession may be appointed ex officio.

Can. 213 . § 1 . In addition to the rights and obligations established by common law, the auxiliary bishop also has those determined in the letters of canonical disposition. § 2 . The rights and obligations of the Coadjutor Bishop appointed by the Patriarch are determined by the Patriarch himself in consultation with the permanent Synod; However, if it is a question of instructing a coadjutor bishop in all the rights and obligations of an eparchial bishop, the consent of the synod of bishops of the Patriarchal Church is required. § 3 . The rights and obligations of the auxiliary bishop are those established by common law.

Can. 214 . § 1 . A coadjutor bishop and an auxiliary bishop, to take canonical possession of their office, must present the letter of canonical disposition to the eparchial bishop. § 2 . The auxiliary bishop must also present the letter of canonical disposition to the college of eparchial counselors. § 3 . However, if the eparchial bishop is totally prevented, it is enough for the coadjutor bishop and the auxiliary bishop to show the letter of canonical disposition to the college of eparchial counselors. § 4 . The chancellor must be present at the presentation of the letters relating to the canonical provision, who will record the matter in the minutes.

Can. 215 . § 1 . The assistant bishop takes the turn of the eparchial bishop when he is absent or incapacitated; He must be called Protosincellus, and the eparchial bishop must entrust to him above all those things that require a special mandate of the law. § 2 . The bishop of the eparchial signature § 1 appoints the auxiliary bishop Protosyncellus; However, if there are more, he calls one Protosincellus and the others Syncellus. § 3 . The eparchial bishop consults the auxiliary bishops before others when considering cases of greater importance, especially of a pastoral nature. § 4 . The assistant bishop and the auxiliary bishop, having been called to be part of the concern of the eparchial bishop, must perform their functions in such a way that they act unanimously with him in all matters.

Can. 216 . § 1 . The coadjutor bishop and the auxiliary bishop should not be held back by a just impediment when the eparchial bishop requires them to perform functions that the eparchial bishop himself must perform. § 2 . The episcopal rights and functions that the coadjutor bishop and the auxiliary bishop can and wish to exercise are not usually entrusted to others by the eparchial bishop.

Can. 217 . The coadjutor bishop and the auxiliary bishop are obliged to reside in the eparchy, from which, except to fulfill some function outside the eparchy or for reasons of vacation, which must not last longer than one month, they must not leave except for a short time.

Can. 218 . To resign from the position of assistant bishop or auxiliary bishop, apply cann. 210 y 211 , § 2 ; These bishops are granted the title of emeritus of the office they have previously held. Art. 4. ABOUT THE VACANT OR AVAILABLE PARQUILIAL POSITION
Can. 219 . The eparchial see becomes vacant due to the death, resignation, transfer and deprivation of the eparchial bishop.

Can. 220 . Regarding vacant eparchial sees within the limits of the territory of the Patriarchal Church, in addition to cann. 225 - 232 and firm cann. 222 y 223, the following must be observed: 1° The Patriarch will inform the Apostolic See as soon as possible of the vacancy of the eparchial see; 2° until the appointment of the Administrator of the eparchy, the ordinary power of the eparchial Bishop passes to the Patriarch, unless otherwise provided for in the particular law of the Patriarchal Church or of the Roman Pontiff; 3° The patriarch must appoint the administrator of the eparchy within one calendar month from the receipt of information about the vacancy of the eparchial see, in consultation with the bishops of the patriarchal court, if they are available, or otherwise in consultation with the permanent Synod; After a useless month, the appointment of the Administrator is transferred to the Apostolic See; 4° The administrator of the eparchy, sent before the Patriarch by profession of faith, obtains the power that he cannot exercise, however, unless he takes possession of the canonical office, which is done by showing the letter of his appointment to the college of eparchial counselors; 5° It is the duty of the patriarch to ensure that a worthy and suitable eparchial bishop is delivered to the vacant eparchial see as soon as possible and not beyond the limits established by common law.

Can. 221 . With the exception of vacant eparchial sees, mentioned in Can. 220, in all other cases of vacant eparchial see except cann. 225 - 232 and firm cann. 222 y 223, the following must be observed: 1° The Metropolitan, otherwise the one in charge of the college of eparchial consultants according to Can. 271, § 5, informs the Apostolic See and, if it concerns the eparchies of the Patriarchal Church, also the Patriarch, as soon as possible regarding the vacancy of the eparchial see, let him do so; 2° the government of the eparchy, unless otherwise provided by the Apostolic See, passes to the auxiliary bishop until the appointment of the administrator of the eparchy or, if there are more, to the major auxiliary bishop by episcopal ordination or, if there is no auxiliary bishop, to the college of eparchial counselors; the aforementioned govern the eparchy meanwhile by the power recognized by the common law of Protosyncello; 3° the college of eparchial councilors must elect the Administrator of the eparchy within eight days following receipt of information about the vacancy of the eparchial see, but for the validity of the election an absolute majority of the votes of the members of the same college is required; 4° if within eight days the Administrator of the eparchy is not elected or if the elected one lacks the conditions in Can. 227, § 2 for the validity of the election, the appointment of the Administrator of the eparchy is transferred to the Metropolitan or, if absent or prevented, to the Apostolic See; 5° The legitimately elected or appointed administrator of the eparchy immediately obtains power and does not need any confirmation; informs the Apostolic See as soon as possible of his election or appointment by the Metropolitan and, if he belongs to the Patriarchal Church, also by the Patriarch.

Can. 222 . A coadjutor bishop, provided he has already taken canonical possession of his office, when the eparchial see is vacant, automatically becomes administrator of the eparchy, until he is enthroned as eparchial bishop.

Can. 223 . In case of transfer to another eparchial see, the Bishop must take canonical possession of the new eparch within two months following notification of the transfer; Meanwhile, in the old eparchy: 1° The administrator of the eparchy has the rights and obligations; 2° preserves the honorary privileges of eparchial bishops; 3rd receives the entire income from his former position.

Can. 224 . § 1 . Protosincellus and Syncellus immediately cease to hold office when the eparchial see becomes vacant, unless they are: 1° ordained bishops; 2nd established in the eparchy of the Patriarch; 3° established in eparchies located within the territory of the patriarchal Church, until the Administrator of the eparchy took canonical possession of his position. § 2 . The things done by Protosincelus and Syncellus, who immediately cease in office when the eparchial see becomes vacant, are valid until they have received final notification of the vacancy of the eparchial see. § 3 . When the eparchial see is vacant, the auxiliary bishop retains the powers conferred by law and exercised under the authority of the administrator of the eparchy, which he had in a full eparchial see such as Protosincellus or Syncellus, unless the Apostolic See or the particular law of his own patriarchal Church establishes otherwise.

Can. 225 . § 1 . Only one is elected or appointed Administrator of the rejected eparchy contrary to custom. § 2 . If the eparchial treasurer becomes administrator of the eparchy, he will in the meantime elect another eparchial treasurer from the council of financial affairs.

Can. 226 . In appointing the administrator of the eparchy, neither the Patriarch nor the college of eparchial counselors can retain any part of his authority, nor can they determine the time or other restrictions on the performance of his functions.

Can. 227 . § 1 . The administrator of the eparchy must be distinguished by integrity, piety, sound doctrine and prudence. § 2 . Only a bishop or priest who is not bound by marriage, has reached thirty-five years of age, and has not been elected, nominated, or transferred to the same vacant eparchial seat, may be validly elected or nominated for the office of Administrator of the eparchy. If these conditions have been met, the acts of whoever has been elected or appointed Administrator of the eparchy are automatically null and void.

Can. 228 . § 1 . Nothing is new when the eparchial seat is vacant. § 2 . Those who in the meantime are engaged in the government of the eparchy are prohibited from doing anything that could harm the eparchy or episcopal rights; They and all others are specifically prohibited from removing, destroying or altering eparchial court documents, whether by themselves or another.
Can. 229 . The administrator of the eparchy has the same rights and obligations as the eparchial bishop, unless the law provides otherwise or the nature of the matter determines otherwise.

Can. 230 . Unless otherwise provided by law: 1° The administrator of the eparchy has the right to a fair remuneration established by the law of particular right or determined by legitimate custom, which must be taken from the assets of the eparchy; 2° the other emoluments corresponding to the eparchial bishop, while the eparchial see is vacant, will be reserved to the future eparchial bishop for the needs of the eparchy, observing the provisions of particular law, which determine the way in which the emoluments must be disbursed.

Can. 231 . § 1 . The report of the eparchy administrator must be presented to the patriarch, if he himself has appointed the administrator, otherwise to the council of eparchy councilors, in which case it does not need to be accepted to be valid. § 2 . The dismissal of the Administrator of the eparchy within the territory of the Patriarchal Church corresponds to the Patriarch with the consent of the permanent Synod; Otherwise it is reserved to the Apostolic See. § 3 . After the death, resignation or removal of the Administrator of the eparchy, a new one must be appointed by the same authority and in the same manner prescribed for the previous one. § 4 . The administrator of the eparchy ceases to be a canonical possession of the eparchy taken over by the new eparchial bishop; The new eparchial bishop may demand a system of administration.

Can. 232 . § 1 . The eparchial financier must perform his duties under the authority of the eparchial administrator when the eparchial see is vacant; The administration of ecclesiastical assets corresponds to the eparchial financier, who has no vacant administrator due to the eparchial see, unless the Patriarch or the college of eparchial counselors provide otherwise. § 2 . For the resignation or dismissal of the eparchial treasurer in the vacant eparchial seat, Can. 231, §§ 1 and 2. § 3 must be observed. If it is resolved in any way by right of the eparchial treasurer within the territorial limits of the Patriarchal Church, the election or appointment of a new treasurer corresponds to the Patriarch after consulting the Bishops of the patriarchal court, if any, otherwise after consulting the permanent Synod; In other cases, the financial person in charge is chosen by a college of eparchial advisors. § 4 . The eparchial treasurer must give an account of his administration to the new eparchial bishop, and if he is not confirmed by him in his position, he ceases to hold office.

Can. 233 . § 1 . If the eparchial see is so hindered by the capture, banishment, banishment or incapacity of the eparchial bishop, that he cannot even communicate by letter with the faithful entrusted to him, the government of the eparchy corresponds to the coadjutor bishop, unless the Patriarch provides otherwise with the consent of the permanent Synod in the eparchies situated within the limits of the territory of the Church over which he presides, or of the Apostolic See; but if any coadjutor bishop is missing or prevented, the Protosincellus, the Syncellus or another suitable priest appointed by the eparchial bishop, to whom the rights and obligations of the Protosyncellus belong by right; but the eparchial bishop may, at the time, designate several people who will succeed each other in office. § 2 . If they are absent or prevented from assuming the government of the eparchy, it is up to the college of eparchial counselors to elect a priest who will govern the eparchy. § 3 . Whoever has undertaken to govern an eparchy within the territory of the Patriarchal Church must, as soon as possible, inform the Patriarch of the impeded eparchial see and the position assumed; In other cases, he must inform the Apostolic See and, if it is the Patriarchal Church, also the Patriarch. Art. 5 OF THE APOSTOLIC ADMINISTRATORS

Can. 234 . § 1 . The Roman Pontiff entrusts the government of the Eparchy to the Apostolic Administrator, whether full or vacant, for serious and special reasons. § 2 . The rights, obligations and privileges of the Apostolic Administrator are taken from the letter of his appointment. CHAPTER II OF THE BODIES THAT HELP THE EPARCHIAL BISHOP IN THE GOVERNMENT OF THE EPARCHY Art. I ON THE EPARCHIAL CONVENTION
Can. 235 . The eparchial assembly provides assistance to the eparchial bishop in matters related to the needs or special interests of the eparchy.
Can. 236 . The eparchial assembly will be convened whenever the deputies recommend it by the judgment of the eparchial bishop and in consultation with the presbyteral council.

Can. 237 . § 1 . It is the duty of the eparchial bishop to convene the eparchial assembly, preside over it by himself or another, move it, prorogue it, suspend it and dissolve it. § 2 . When the eparchial see becomes vacant, the eparchial assembly is automatically suspended until the new eparchial bishop decides on the matter.

Can. 238 . § 1 . The following are summoned to the eparchial assembly and must attend: 1° the auxiliary bishop and the auxiliary bishops; 2° Protosincellus, Syncelli, judicial vicar and eparchial treasurer; 3rd eparchial counselors; 4th rector of the major eparchial seminary; 5th protopresbyter; 6° at least one priest from each district, elected by all those who have the care of souls there, with the protopresbyter presiding over the election; Likewise, another priest must be elected, who will take his place under the same conditions; 7° the members of the presbyteral council and some delegates of the pastoral council, if any, by the same council in the form and number established by the particular right to be elected; 8° some deacons elected according to the norm of particular law; 9° The superiors of independent monasteries and some superiors of other institutes of consecrated life that have their headquarters in the eparchy, in the form and number of elections established by particular law; 10° lay people elected by the pastoral council, if it exists, or determined by the eparchial bishop in such a way that the number of lay people does not exceed one third of the members of the eparchial assembly. § 2 . The eparchial bishop, if he considers it appropriate, can invite others to the eparchial assembly, without excluding people from other independent churches, to whom he can also grant the right to vote. § 3 . Some observers from non-Catholic Churches or Ecclesial Communities may also be invited to the eparchial meeting.

Can. 239 . Those who must attend the eparchial assembly cannot, even if they are detained due to legitimate impediment, send a representative to attend the eparchial assembly on their behalf, but they must inform the eparchial bishop of the impediment.

Can. 240 . § 1 . It is the firm right of any Christian to indicate the topics that will be discussed at the eparchial meeting, and only the eparchial bishop should decide the topics that will be discussed at this meeting. § 2 . The eparchial bishop will appoint, at the time, one or more commissions whose purpose is to prepare the topics to be discussed at the eparchial assembly. § 3 . The eparchial Bishop will also ensure that, at the time, all those summoned are given a plan of the topics to be discussed. § 4 . All proposed questions are subject to free discussion in the sessions of the eparchial assembly.

Can. 241 . The eparchial bishop is the only legislator in the eparchial assembly, the others having only an advisory vote; Only he subscribes to the decisions that were made at the eparchial meeting; which, if enacted at the same meeting, immediately become binding, unless expressly provided otherwise.

Can. 242 . The eparchial bishop communicates the text of the laws, declarations and decrees given in the eparchial assembly to the authority that determines the particular law of his own independent Church. Art. II ON THE EPARCHIAL TRIBUNAL

Can. 243 . § 1 . An eparchial bishop must have an eparchial tribunal next to his see, which entrusts him with the government of the eparchy that has been entrusted to him. § 2 . The eparchial court includes Protosincellus, Syncelli, judicial vicar, financier and eparchial financial advisor, chancellor, eparchial judges, promoter of justice and defender of the bond, notaries and other persons who are assumed by the eparchial bishop to properly fulfill the responsibilities of the eparchial court. § 3 . The eparchial bishop may also establish other positions in the eparchial tribunal as the needs or interests of the eparchy require.

Can. 244 . § 1 . The appointment and dismissal of those who exercise their functions in the eparchial tribunal corresponds to the eparchial bishop. § 2 . All those admitted to office in the eparchial tribunal must: 1. make a promise to faithfully fulfill the office according to the method determined by law or by the eparchial bishop; 2° keep the secret within the limits and according to the method determined by the law or by the eparchial bishop. 1. Of the Protosyncello and the Syncelli

Can. 245 . In each eparchy a Protosincellus will be appointed, who, endowed with ordinary vicarious powers according to the norm of common law, will assist the eparchial bishop in the government of the entire eparchy.

Can. 246 . Whenever the right of government of the eparchy requires it, one or more Syncelli may be appointed, who by right in a certain part of the eparchy, or in a certain type of business, or around the faithful of the Church, other independent groups of people enrolled in a certain group, have the same power that the common law gives to the Protosyncello.

Can. 247 . § 1 . Protosincellus and Syncelli are freely named by the eparchial bishop and can be freely removed by him with the signature Can. 215 , §§ 1 and 2. § 2 . Protosincellus and Syncellus must be celibate priests, unless the particular law of their own independent Church determines otherwise, as far as possible from among the registered clerics of the eparchy, of age not less than thirty years, doctors or graduates or at least experts in some sacred science, recommended by sound doctrine, honesty, prudence and experience in the conduct of affairs. § 3 . The office of Protosyncelli or Syncellus is not conferred on the relatives of the eparchial bishop up to and including the fourth degree. § 4 . An eparchial bishop may also assume a Protosincellus and Syncellus of another eparchy or another autonomous Church with the consent of his eparchial bishop.

Can. 248 . § 1 . Unless the common law expressly provides otherwise, the Protosyncello throughout the eparchy, and the Syncelli within the scope of the office assigned to him, are entitled to the same executive powers of government as the eparchial bishop, with the exception of those which the eparchial bishop has reserved for himself or for others, or which by law require his special mandate, without which the act for which such mandate is required is null and void. § 2 . Protosyncellos and Syncellis, within the scope of their competence, are also entitled to the usual faculties granted by the Apostolic See to the eparchial bishop, as well as to the execution of the mandates of the Apostolic See or the Patriarch, unless otherwise expressly provided or decided by the energy of the person of the eparchial bishop.
Can. 249 . Protosincellus and Syncellus must report to the eparchial bishop on major matters, conduct and actions and never act against his will and mind.
Can. 250 . The priests protosyncelli and Syncelli during their office have the privileges and insignia of the first post-episcopal dignity.

Can. 251 . § 1 . Protosincellus and Syncellus cease from their positions at the end of a given time, by resignation accepted by the eparchial bishop or by dismissal. § 2 . When the eparchial seat is vacant, the cirras of Protosyncellus and Syncellus Can. 224 will be preserved. § 3 . With the suspension of the office of eparchial bishop, the power of the Protosyncelli and the Syncelli is suspended, unless they are ordained bishops. 2° Of the chancellor and the other notaries and the archives of the eparchial court

Can. 252 . § 1 . In the eparchial court, a chancellor is appointed, who is a priest or a deacon, whose main obligation, unless otherwise provided in the particular law, is to ensure that the minutes of the court are taken, prepared and preserved in the archives of the eparchial court. § 2 . If deemed necessary, an assistant may be assigned to the chancellor, whose name will be vice-chancellor. § 3 . Both the chancellor and vice-chancellor are by right notaries of the eparchial court.

Can. 253 . § 1 . In addition to the chancellor, other notaries may be appointed whose signature gives public credit, either to any acts, to judicial acts in progress, or to acts of a certain cause or business only. § 2 . Journalists must have a perfect reputation and be above all suspicion; In cases where the reputation of the clergyman may be called into question, the notary must be a priest.

Can. 254 . Notaries are: 1° prepare minutes and documents related to decrees, provisions, obligations or other things that require their attention; 2° faithfully record in writing the things that are done, and sign the minutes of these things indicating the place, day, month and year; 3° present the minutes or documents whose preservation is legally requested and declare their copies in accordance with the original.
Can. 255 . The chancellor and other notaries may be removed from office freely by the eparchial bishop, but not by the eparchial administrator, except with the consent of the eparchial councilors.

Can. 256 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop will establish in a secure place the archive of the eparchial court, in which documents relating to the affairs of the eparch will be preserved. § 2 . With all care and concern, an inventory of the documents preserved in the archive of the eparchial court should be prepared, with a brief synopsis of them.

Can. 257 . § 1 . The archives of the eparchial court must be closed, and the eparchial bishop and chancellor must have the key; no one can enter without the permission of the eparchial bishop or the Protosyncelli together with the chancellor alone. § 2 . It is the right of those interested to receive an authentic copy of the documents, which are public in nature and which refer to the status of their person, personally or through a proxy.

Can. 258 . The eparchial court cannot extract documents from the archive except for a short time and with the permission of the eparchial bishop alone or of the Protosincell together with the chancellor.

Can. 259 . § 1 . There should also be a secret archive in the eparchial court, or at least in the eparchial court archive a secret cabinet completely closed and locked, which cannot be removed from the place where the documents are kept confidential. § 2 . Each year the minutes of the sentencing procedures regarding conduct whose life has elapsed or which have been terminated for ten years will be destroyed, preserving a brief summary of the fact and the text of the final sentence or decision.

Can. 260 . § 1 . Only the eparchial bishop should have the key to the secret archive or secret closet. § 2 . Leaving the eparchial seat vacant, the secret archive or the secret closet must not be opened except in case of true necessity on the part of the Administrator of the eparchy. § 3 . Do not remove documents from a secret file or secret cabinet.

Can. 261 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop will ensure that the records and documents of the archives of the cathedral churches, parishes and others existing within the limits of the territory of the eparchy are carefully kept and that two copies of the inventory of records and documents are made, one of which will be kept in his own archive and the other in the archive of the eparchial court. § 2 . For the inspection or extraction of the records and documents related to these archives, the norms established by the eparchial bishop must be observed. 3° Of eparchial finances and financial planning

Can. 262 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop, in consultation with the eparchial advisory council and the financial council, appoints an eparchial financier who is faithful to Christ, expert in financial matters, and of good integrity. § 2 . The eparchial financier is appointed for a period determined by the particular law; during his tenure he should not be removed unless there is a serious reason that must be evaluated by the eparchial bishop in consultation with the eparchial council of advisors and the financial council. § 3 . The eparchial treasurer is under the authority of the eparchial bishop, who more precisely determines his rights and relations with the financial council, administers the temporal goods of the eparchy, ensures the administration of ecclesiastical goods throughout the eparchy, ensures their conservation, protection and growth, makes up for the negligence of local administrators and administers himself ecclesiastical goods that lack an administrator designated by law. § 4 . The eparchial treasurer must report on the administration to the eparchial bishop every year and whenever the bishop himself requests it; The eparchial bishop, however, through the financial council, will examine the accounts presented by the eparchial financier. § 5 . Regarding the financial obligations of the eparchial see, Can. 232 must be observed in the vacant eparchial see.

Can. 263 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop establishes a financial council, which is composed of the president, who is the eparchial bishop himself, and of some persons qualified also by civil law, if possible, appointed by the eparchial bishop in consultation with a college of eparchial counselors, unless the particular law of his own independent Church has already provided for another equivalent means, always firm, so that those elected or nominated by others need the confirmation of the eparchial bishop. § 2 . The eparchial treasurer is automatically a member of the financial council. § 3 . Those who are related to the eparchial bishop up to and including the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity are excluded from the financial affairs of the council. § 4 . The eparchial bishop must not fail to listen to advice on financial matters in acts of greater importance in financial matters; and its members have only an advisory vote, unless their consent is required by common law in specially expressed cases or by the founding document. § 5 . In addition to other tasks entrusted to the council by common law, it is the responsibility of financial affairs to prepare each year an account of the income and disbursements expected for the entire government of the eparchy in the following year, as well as to approve the account of income and expenses for the outgoing year. Art. III OF THE PRESBYTERAL COUNCIL AND THE COLLEGE OF EPARCHIAL CONSULTANTS

Can. 264 . A presbyteral council must be established in the eparchy, that is, a group of priests representing the presbytery, who will assist the eparchial bishop with their advice in accordance with the law in them, which refers to the needs of the pastoral work and the good of the eparchy.
Can. 265 . The presbyteral council will have its own statutes approved by the eparchial bishop in accordance with the firm norms of common law and the particular law of its own independent Church.

Can. 266 . Regarding the constitution of the presbyteral council, the following must be observed: 1. An appropriate part of the members is elected by the priests themselves according to the norm of the particular law of the Church itself. 2° certain priests must be born members, according to the norms of the statutes, who belong to the council by virtue of the office required of them; 3. The eparchial bishop is free to appoint some members.

Can. 267 . § 1 . In the election of the members of the presbyteral council, the following have active and passive voice: 1° all the registered priests of the eparchy; 2° other priests who have a domicile or quasi-domicile in the eparchy and at the same time perform some function for the good of the same eparchy. § 2 . To the extent provided by the statutes, active and passive voice may also be conferred on other priests who have a domicile or quasi-domicile in the eparchy.

Can. 268 . The method of electing members of the presbyteral council must be determined by the statutes, so that, to the extent possible, the priests of the presbytery are represented, taking into account especially the different ministries and the different regions of the eparchy.

Can. 269 . § 1 . It is the responsibility of the eparchial bishop to convene the presbyteral council, preside over it and determine the issues that are to be discussed therein or accept proposals from the members. § 2 . The eparchial bishop must listen to the presbyteral council in matters of greater importance and consult in cases expressed by common law; and needs his consent only in cases expressly determined by the common law, and by the firm law of the Patriarch relative to the affairs of the eparchy which he governs, to consult the presbyteral council also in these cases only. § 3 . The presbyteral council can never act without the eparchial bishop, whose only concern is to publish what has been done in the council itself.

Can. 270 . § 1 . The members of the presbyteral council shall be appointed for a term to be determined in the statutes in such a way that the whole council or any part of it may be renewed within five years. § 2 . When the eparchial seat becomes vacant, the presbyteral council ceases and its functions are covered by a college of eparchial counselors; Within the year following the taking of canonical possession of the eparchy, the eparchial bishop must establish a new presbyteral council. § 3 . If the presbyteral council fails to fulfill the task entrusted to it for the good of the eparchy or is seriously abused by it, the eparchial bishop may dissolve it in consultation with the Metropolitan or, if it is the metropolitan see itself, in consultation with the eparchial bishop for major episcopal ordination under the same Metropolitan, but must establish a new presbyteral council within the year.

Can. 271 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop must establish a college of eparchial counselors, to whom correspond the functions determined by law. § 2 . The college of eparchial counselors is established for a period of five years, after which it continues to exercise its proper functions until a new college is established. § 3 . The members of the college of eparchial counselors must be no less than six and no more than twelve; If, for any reason, the minimum number of members of the college is not reached within a given period of five years, the eparchial bishop integrates the college as soon as possible by appointing a new member, otherwise the college will not be able to act validly. § 4 . The members of the college of eparchial counselors are freely appointed by the eparchial bishop from among those who are members of the presbyteral council at the time of their appointment. § 5 . The college of eparchial counselors is presided over by the eparchial bishop; the eparchial see being vacant or obstructed, the one who in the meantime holds the place of eparchial bishop, or, if he has not been appointed, a senior priest in the same college by sacred ordination. § 6 . Whenever the law determines that an eparchial bishop needs the consent of a college of eparchial counselors, it is sufficient for the patriarch, in the affairs of the eparchy he governs, to consult this college. Art. IV OF THE PASTORAL COUNCIL

Can. 272 . In the eparchy, if pastoral circumstances suggest it, a pastoral council should be established, under the direction of the eparchial bishop, to investigate, evaluate and propose practical conclusions on those things that concern the pastoral work in the eparchy.

Can. 273 . § 1 . The pastoral council, which is nothing more than a consultative group, is made up of clerics, religious or members of societies of common life analogous to religious ones and, especially, of lay people appointed in the manner determined by the eparchial bishop. § 2 . The pastoral council should be organized in such a way that, to the extent possible, the faithful of the eparchy are represented by different types of people, associations and other companies. § 3 . Along with these Christian faithful, the eparchial bishop may also invite others, even those from another independent Church, as appropriate to the pastoral plan. § 4 . No one should be appointed to the pastoral council except those who are faithful in their faith, who are excellent in good morals and prudence.

Can. 274 . § 1 . The pastoral council is constituted for a time according to the provisions of the statutes, which are given by the eparchial bishop. § 2 . When the eparchial see becomes vacant, the pastoral plan ceases.

Can. 275 . It is solely the responsibility of the eparchial bishop to convene the pastoral council according to the needs of the apostolate, to preside over it and to publish the things discussed therein. Art. 5 ABOUT THE PROTOPRESBYTERS

Can. 276 . § 1 . A protopresbyter is a priest who is in charge of a district made up of several parishes, in order to fulfill the eparchial functions determined by law in the name of the bishop. § 2 . It is up to the eparchial bishop, in consultation with the presbyteral council, to establish, change and suppress said districts according to the needs of pastoral activity.

Can. 277 . § 1 . For the office of protopresbyter, which, except by the particular right of his own independent Church, must not be stably combined with the office of parish priest of a given parish, the eparchial bishop appoints, after hearing, if appropriate, the parish priests and vicars of the parish district in question, a priest who stands out in doctrine and apostolic zeal, especially among the parish priests. § 2 . A protopresbyter is appointed for a period determined by a particular law. § 3 . The eparchial bishop may remove the protopresbyter from office only for justified cause.

Can. 278 . § 1 . In addition to the powers and capacities conferred on him by particular law, the Protopresbyter has the right and obligation to: 1. promote and coordinate common pastoral action; 2° ensure that clerics lead a life appropriate to their condition and diligently fulfill their obligations; 3° take care that the Divine Liturgy and the divine praises are celebrated according to the provisions of the liturgical books, that the beauty and luster of the churches and the sacred furniture are faithfully preserved, especially in the celebration of the Divine Liturgy and in the custody of the Divine Eucharist, that the parish books are correctly written and sealed, that the ecclesiastical property is diligently administered, finally, that the parish house is cared for with care. due diligence. § 2 . In the district entrusted to him, the protopresbyter: 1. Shall ensure that clerics attend such conferences as the local Hierarch deems appropriate to promote sacred knowledge and pastoral matters; 2° He will ensure that spiritual support is available to clerics, and will be especially concerned about those who face more difficult circumstances or are tormented by problems. § 3 . The protopresbyter must ensure that the parish priests he knows are seriously ill, and their relatives, if they are married, do not lack spiritual and material help, and that the funerals of the deceased are celebrated with dignity; Also ensure that books, documents, sacred objects and other things belonging to the Church are not lost or taken away on the occasion of illness or death. § 4 . The protopresbyter has the obligation to visit the parishes according to the determination made by the eparchial bishop. CHAPTER III OF THE PARISHES, OF THE PARISHES AND OF THE VICARS OF THE PARISHES
Can. 279 . A parish is a specific community of Christians established stably in an eparchy, whose pastoral care is entrusted to the parish priest.

Can. 280 . § 1 . As a general rule, the parish must be territorial, which of course must include all the faithful of a certain territory; but if it is convenient in the judgment of the eparchial bishop in consultation with the presbyteral council, personal parishes will be erected according to the nationality, language and membership of the faithful, and others of the Church in their own right, or even determined for some other defined reason. § 2 . It is the responsibility of the eparchial bishop to erect, change and abolish parishes in consultation with the presbyteral council. § 3 . A legally established parish is a legal entity in its own right.

Can. 281 . § 1 . A parish priest is a priest who, as the main collaborator of the eparchial bishop, as a pastor, is entrusted with the proper care of souls in a given parish under the authority of the same eparchial bishop. § 2 . A legal person cannot be a valid pastor.

Can. 282 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop, but not the Administrator of the eparchy, may, with the advice of the presbyteral council and with the consent of the superior of an important religious institution or society of common life, erect a parish similar to the religious ones in the church of the same institution or society under the signature Can. 480. § 2 . This erection must be made by written agreement between the eparchial bishop and the major superior of a religious institution or society of common life in the manner of the religious, by which it is determined precisely what the parish ministry must fulfill, how to add people to the parish, what economic matters, and what are the rights and obligations of the members of the same institution or society in that church and which priest.

Can. 283 . The eparchial bishop may not subjugate certain groups of people, buildings and places that are in the territory of the parish and that are not exempt by law from the care of the parish priest, in whole or in part, except for serious cause.

Can. 284 . § 1 . The right to appoint pastors belongs only to the eparchial bishop, who appoints them freely. § 2 . But in order for the parish of a member of a religious institution or of a society of common life to be entrusted in the likeness of the religious, the Major Superior proposes to the eparchial bishop the appointment of a suitable priest from his institution or society, subject to the agreements concluded with the eparchial bishop or other authority determined by the particular law of his own Church. § 3 . The parish priest is permanent in his position, so he should not be appointed for a specific period of time unless: 1. he is a member of a religious institution or a society of common life such as a religious one; 2° the candidate has accepted it in writing; 3° this is a special case, in which case the consent of the college of eparchial counselors is required; 4° the particular right of the independent Church allows it.

Can. 285 . § 1 . For a priest to be appointed parish priest, it is necessary that he be endowed with good morals, sound doctrine, zeal for souls, prudence and other virtues and gifts that are legally required to fill the parish ministry with praise. § 2 . If a priest is married, good conduct is required of both his wife and his children who live with him. § 3 . The eparchial Bishop will assign a vacant parish to the one he considers suitable to receive all people, having considered all the circumstances; so that he can judge the suitability, hear the protopresbyter and carry out appropriate investigations after the hearing, if necessary, also to other Christian faithful, especially the clergy.

Can. 286 . When the eparchial see is vacant or obstructed, the administrator of the eparchy or whoever governs the eparchy in the meantime is responsible: 1° to appoint a parish priest by the Major Superior according to the norm Can. 284, § 2; 2° appoint a parish priest from among other priests, if the eparchial see has been vacant or obstructed for at least one year.

Can. 287 . § 1 . The pastor of a parish should only have parish care; However, due to a shortage of priests or other circumstances, the same parish priest may be entrusted with the care of several neighboring parishes. § 2 . In the same parish there is only one priest; But if the particular law of an independent Church allows a parish to be entrusted to several priests, the same particular law will determine precisely what are the rights and obligations of the moderator, who directs the common action and is responsible for it before the eparchial bishop, and what are the rights and obligations of the other priests.

Can. 288 . The parish priest obtains from the canonical provision the care of souls, which, however, he is not permitted to exercise unless it is taken according to the norm of particular law by the canonical possession of the parish.

Can. 289 . § 1 . In the exercise of the task of teaching, the pastor has the duty to preach the word of God to all the faithful, so that they grow in faith, hope and charity, rooted in Christ, and the Christian community gives the testimony of charity that the Lord has recommended; as well as catechetical formation adapted to each era to lead the faithful to a full knowledge of the mystery of salvation; To impart this institution, it seeks the help not only of members of religious institutes or societies of common life such as religious, but also the cooperation of lay people. § 2 . In carrying out the task of sanctification, the parish priest must ensure that the celebration of the Divine Liturgy is the center and summit of the entire life of the Christian community; It must also work so that the Christian faithful are nourished with spiritual food through the devout and frequent reception of the sacraments and through conscious and active participation in divine praises. The priest also remembers to contribute as much as possible to the sacrament of penance to encourage Christian life; Therefore, he must facilitate those called to administer this sacrament, if necessary, also to other priests who master several languages. § 3 . In fulfilling the task of governing, the shepherd is above all concerned with knowing his own flock; and being a minister of all the sheep, foster the growth of Christian life both in individual Christian believers and in associations especially dedicated to the apostolate and in the entire parish community; He will, therefore, visit homes and schools, as his pastoral office demands; let him take a serious look at the young men and women; He will persecute the poor and the weak with paternal charity; Finally, take special care of the workers and work hard, so that they help the faithful in the works of apostolate.

Can. 290 . § 1 . In all legal matters of the parish, the pastor corresponds to the same person. § 2 . The most important sacred functions, such as the celebration of the sacraments of Christian initiation, the blessing of firm marriages, Can. 302 , § 2 , ecclesiastical funerals are referred to the pastor in such a way that parochial vicars are not permitted to perform them without at least the presumed permission of the pastor himself.

Can. 291 . All offerings, except those mentioned in cann. 715 - 717, which are received on the occasion of the completion of the pastoral service by the pastor and other clerics assigned to the parish, must be brought to the parish Mass, unless the contrary will of the offerer is established regarding completely voluntary offerings; The eparchial bishop, in consultation with the presbyteral council, has the right to establish the provisions by which the allocation of these offerings is provided, as well as the fair remuneration of the pastor and other parish clergy in accordance with the Can. 390 norm.

Can. 292 . § 1 . The parish priest has the obligation to reside in the parish house near the parish church; However, the local Hierarch may, for just cause, allow him to reside elsewhere, provided that the parish service does not suffer loss as a result. § 2 . Except for serious reasons, the parish priest may be absent from the parish every year, for vacation, for no more than one continuous month or a break; that the days during which once a year the pastor takes time off for spiritual retreat are not counted as holidays; and if the parish priest wishes to be absent from the parish for more than a week, he is obliged to notify the corresponding local Hierarch. § 3 . It is up to the eparchial bishop to establish the norms by which the absence of the parish priest during the care of the parish is expected to be covered by a priest endowed with the necessary faculties and abilities.

Can. 293 . The pastor remembers that he must, with his daily conduct and his concern for the baptized and the unbaptized, Catholics and non-Catholics, set an example of a truly priestly and pastoral ministry and bear witness to the truth and life to all, and as a good pastor he must also seek out those who, in fact, have been baptized in the Catholic Church, abstain from receiving the sacraments, or rather have failed in the faith.

Can. 294 . The priest must frequently celebrate the Divine Liturgy for the people of the parish entrusted to him, but he is obliged to celebrate it on the days prescribed by the particular law of his own independent Church.
Can. 295 . In the parish, according to the norm of the particular law of the independent Church, appropriate plans must be made for the management of pastoral and financial affairs.

Can. 296 . § 1 . The parish books must be kept in the parish, namely the book of baptisms, marriages, deaths and others, according to the norms of the particular law of the Church itself or, if they are lacking, those established by the eparchial bishop himself; The pastor must ensure that parish books are correctly recorded and kept according to the same rules. § 2 . In the baptism book, the registration of the baptized person of the determined independent Church is recorded according to the norm Can. 37, the ministry of the chrismation of the holy miracle, as well as those that correspond to the Christian faithful, except marriage, Can. 840, § 3, and also by reason of adoption and also by reason of sacred order or perpetual profession in a religious institution; These records are always called a baptismal certificate. § 3 . The testimonies given of the canonical status of the faithful, and all documents that may have legal importance, are signed by the parish priest himself or his delegate and sealed with the parish seal. § 4 . An archive will be maintained in the parish, in which the parish books are kept together with the letters of the Hierarchs and other documents of need or usefulness; all of which must be inspected by the eparchial bishop or his delegate at the canonical visitation or at another convenient time, and the parish priest must take care that they do not fall into the hands of strangers. § 5 . The oldest parish books are also kept in accordance with the rules of particular law.

Can. 297 . § 1 . The parish priest ceases to hold office by resignation accepted by the eparchial bishop, after a certain time has elapsed, by removal or transfer. § 2 . The parish priest, having reached seventy-five years of age, is asked to present his resignation from office to the eparchial bishop, who, having examined all the circumstances of the person and the place, decides whether to accept or postpone it; The eparchial bishop must provide adequate support and accommodation to the renunciant, taking into account the norms of the particular law of his own independent Church.

Can. 298 . If the parish is vacant or the pastor is prevented for any reason from exercising his pastoral duties in the parish, the eparchial bishop shall as soon as possible appoint a priest to be administrator of the parish.

Can. 299 . § 1 . The parish administrator has the same rights and obligations as the parish priest, unless otherwise determined by the eparchial bishop. § 2 . The parish administrator may not do anything that could harm the rights of the parish priest or harm parish property. § 3 . The parish administrator will report to the pastor upon completion of his duties.

Can. 300 . § 1 . When the parish is vacant and the parish priest is completely prevented from exercising his pastoral duties prior to the appointment of the parish administrator, the parochial vicar looks after the parish in the meantime and, indeed, if there are more, of its major presbyteral ordination or, if there are no vicars, of the nearest parish priest; But the eparchial bishop will determine in due course which parish will be considered closest to each one. § 2 . Whoever has assumed the government of the parish in the meantime must immediately inform the eparchial bishop of the matter.

Can. 301 . § 1 . If it is necessary or convenient to carry out the pastoral care of the parish, one or more parochial vicars may be added to the parish priest, who must be priests. § 2 . A parochial vicar may be appointed for the entire parish or for a specific part of it. § 3 . The parochial vicar is freely appointed by the eparchial bishop after hearing, unless he wisely decides otherwise, the parish priest and, if he is a member of a religious institution or a society of common life analogous to the religious one, observing Can. 284, § 2.

Can. 302 . § 1 . The rights and obligations of the parochial vicar are derived from common and particular law as well as from the letters of the eparchial bishop and must be exercised under the authority of the parish priest, but, unless expressly provided otherwise and except for the obligation mentioned in Can. 294, the parochial vicar must by reason of his office assist the pastor in all parish ministry and, if necessary, complement the pastor's shift. § 2 . But by reason of his office, the parochial vicar is not endowed with the power to bless marriages; However, in addition to the local Hierarch, also the parish priest within the limits of the parish can confer this power, even a general one; faculty which, if conferred upon him, the parochial vicar may also confer upon other priests in individual cases. § 3 . The parochial vicar, as a collaborator of the parish priest, must dedicate an excellent and active effort to pastoral work every day; between the pastor and the vicar of the parish there must be a fraternal conversation, mutual charity and respect must always prevail and the same plans, help and example help each other providing the care of the parish with harmonious will and common effort. § 4 . The parochial vicar has the obligation to reside in the parish according to the prescriptions of the eparchial bishop or legitimate customs; However, during vacation time, the parochial vicar has the same right as the parish priest.

Can. 303 . A parochial vicar may be removed by the eparchial bishop for just cause; If, however, the parochial vicar is a member of a religious institution or a society of common life such as a religious one, Can. 1391 , § 2 will be retained. CHAPTER IV OF THE PRINCIPLES OF THE CHURCH
Can. 304 . The rector of the church is a priest, who is required to care for a specific church, which is not parochial nor is it attached to the house of the institution of consecrated life.

Can. 305 . § 1 . The rector of the church is appointed by the eparchial bishop, subject to the right of the superior of a major religious institution or society of common life to propose suitable religious priests from his institution or society for nomination. § 2 . Although the church belongs to some institution of clerical life consecrated under pontifical or patriarchal right, the eparchial bishop has the right to appoint the rector of the church proposed by the Superior. § 3 . If the church is related to a seminary or other college governed by priests, the rector of the seminary or college is also rector of the church, unless the eparchial bishop decides otherwise.

Can. 306 . § 1 . In the church entrusted to him, the rector of the church cannot exercise parish functions except with the consent or, where appropriate, by delegating to the parish priest and signing Can. 336, § 2. § 2 . The rector of the church may celebrate the Divine Liturgy and divine praise there, respecting the legitimate statutes of the foundation and, provided that these do not harm in any way the parish ministry in the judgment of the local Hierarch.

Can. 307 . The local hierarch, if he considers it appropriate, can order the rector of the church to celebrate certain sacred functions in the church entrusted to him, including parish functions, as well as open the church to certain groups of faithful.

Can. 308 . Without the at least presumed permission of the rector of the church or a higher authority, no one may celebrate the Divine Liturgy or divine praises in the church, administer the sacraments or perform other sacred functions; but this permission must be granted or denied in accordance with the law.

Can. 309 . The church leader, under the authority of the local Hierarch, must ensure that the statutes and legitimate rights sought are preserved, that the Divine Liturgy, the sacraments and the divine praises are celebrated in the church according to the provisions of the liturgical books and the law, that the burdens are faithfully fulfilled, that the ecclesiastical property is carefully administered, that the sacred furniture and sacred buildings are provided for their preservation and beauty, and that do anything that is in any way inconsistent with the sanctity of the place and reverence due to the house of God.

Can. 310 . The eparchial bishop may remove the rector of the church for just cause; However, if the rector of the church is a member of a religious institution or a society of common life such as a religious one, Can. 1391 , § 2 will be retained. TITLE VIII OF THE EXARCHES AND THE EXARCHES

Can. 311 . § 1 . An exarchy is a portion of the people of God which, due to special circumstances, has not been established as an eparchy, and which is limited territorially or otherwise, and is entrusted to the Exarch. § 2 . In the establishment, alteration and suppression of the exarchy, which is situated within the limits of the patriarchal territory of the Church, Can. 85, § 3 must be observed; The establishment, modification and suppression of other exarchies belongs solely to the Apostolic See.
Can. 312 . An exarch governs an exarchy in the name of the one who appoints him or in his own name; on which matter must be established in the establishment or alteration of the exarchy.

Can. 313 . What is said in the law about eparchies or about eparchial bishops is also valid about exarchies or exarchs, unless expressly provided otherwise in the law or established by the nature of the matter.

Can. 314 . § 1 . Within the limits of the territory of the Patriarchal Church, an Exarch is appointed by the Patriarch with the consent of the permanent and firm Synod, if it is an Exarch who is to be ordained Bishop; In other cases, the appointment of the exarch belongs solely to the Apostolic See. § 2 . An exarch appointed by the Patriarch cannot be removed from office except with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church. § 3 . The exarch takes canonical possession of the exarchy that has been entrusted to him by showing him the decree of appointment, who meanwhile governs the exarchy.

Can. 315 . § 1 . An exarch appointed by the Patriarch outside the limits of the territory of the Patriarchal Church may search for suitable priests to undertake the pastoral care of the faithful in the exarchy; And may the Patriarch, to the extent possible, satisfy the Exarch's request. § 2 . Priests sent by the Patriarch to the exarchate for a fixed or indefinite period are considered attached to the exarchate and are in all things subject to the power of the Exarch.

Can. 316 . From the decrees of the Exarch, who governs the Exarchy in the name of the Roman Pontiff or Patriarch, appeal is made respectively to the Apostolic See or Patriarch; From the decrees of the exarch, who governs the exarch in his own name, resort is made to the ordinary rule of law.

Can. 317 . An exarch is obliged to visit the thresholds of the holy apostles Peter and Paul according to the Can. 208 norm, with the exception of exarchs who govern the exarchy entrusted to them in the name of the Patriarch.

Can. 318 . § 1 . An exarch appointed by the Patriarch must submit a written report to the Patriarch every five years regarding the spiritual and temporal status of the exarch. § 2 . An exarch appointed by the Roman Pontiff must submit the same report to the Apostolic See every five years and, if he belongs to the Patriarchal Church, also send a copy of the report to the Patriarch as soon as possible.

Can. 319 . § 1 . By the laws of the eparchial meeting, the eparchial tribunal, the presbyteral council, the college of eparchial counselors and the pastoral council, the exarch is obliged to the judgment of the authority of places and persons, equally adapted to the judgment of the anchorite, who established or changed the exarchy. § 2 . If a college of advisors cannot be established in accordance with the rules of Can. 271 , § 3 , the Exarch shall appoint a group of more prudent priests, not less than three, as far as possible from among the members of the presbyteral council, if one exists, selected, whose consent or advice he must seek, whenever the law determines that the eparchial bishop needs the consent or advice of the eparchial council of advisors to act.
