Passing to another independent monastery of the same confederation, he does not complete the novitiate or make a new profession, and from the day of the transition he loses his rights and is free from the obligations of the old monastery, assumes the rights and obligations of another and, if he is a clergyman, is also registered as a clergyman. § 2 . When passing from an independent monastery to another independent monastery that does not belong to any confederation or to another confederation, one must observe the provisions of the standard monastery to which the transfer occurs, regarding the obligation to complete the novitiate and make profession; but if in the typical case he does not deal with the matter, nor complete the novitiate nor make a new profession, but the effects of the transition occur from the day on which the transition occurs, unless the Superior of the monastery requires him to remain in the monastery for some time not exceeding one year for reasons of experience; At the end of the probationary period, either by the Superior with the consent of his council or by Synaxis, according to the norm of the typical, he must be permanently enrolled in a new monastery, or return to the old monastery. § 3 . In the transition from an independent monastery to an order or congregation, appropriate references to cann. 544 y 545 are maintained. § 4 . An independent convention, from which a member withdraws, preserves the property that has already been acquired by reason of the member himself; As for the dowry, it is due without ripe fruits from the day of the transition to the monastery to which the transition occurs. 9° Of exclusion and departure from the monastery

Can. 489 . § 1 . Exclusion from an independent monastery can only be granted to a member of perpetual vows at the request of the authority of the member to whom the monastery is subject, after hearing the Superior of the independent monastery together with his council. § 2 . The eparchial bishop can only grant this cancellation for a period of three years.

Can. 490 . At the request of the Superior of an independent monastery, with the consent of his council, excommunication may be imposed by the authority to which the monastery is subject, for grave cause, with equity and charity.

Can. 491 . The cloistered member remains bound by his vows and remains bound by the other obligations of the monastic profession, which may be combined with his status; he must leave the monastic habit; during the duration of the exclamatory period it lacks active and passive voice; He is also subject to the eparchial bishop of the place where he resides, rather than the Superior of his own monastery, by virtue of the vow of obedience.

Can. 492 . § 1 . A member of perpetual vows cannot request the cancellation of his departure from the monastery and his return to secular life, except for the most serious reasons weighed before the Lord; He had to transmit his request to the Superior of his independent monastery, who would send it to the Apostolic See together with his vote and his advice. § 2 . Such cancellation is reserved to the Apostolic See.

Can. 493 . § 1 . The indulgence to leave the monastery and return to secular life, legitimately granted and insinuated to the member, unless the member himself rejects it in the act of insinuation, automatically implies dispensation from vows, as well as from all obligations derived from the profession, but not from those linked to the sacred order, if the member is constituted in the holy order. § 2 . If a member who has left the monastery and returned to secular life is readmitted to the monastery, he reestablishes his novitiate and his profession, as if he had never been linked to religious life.

Can. 494 . § 1 . A monk ordained by perpetual vows and in holy order, if he has obtained forgiveness to leave the monastery and return to age, cannot exercise holy orders until he has found an eparchial bishop who is a benevolent recipient. § 2 . The eparchial bishop can receive it absolutely or on a trial basis for five years; In the first case the monk is registered by right of the eparchy, in the second for exactly five years, unless he has been expressly dismissed beforehand.

Can. 495 . The member who, after having made his profession, illegitimately left the monastery, must return to it without delay; The superiors must diligently seek it and, if the movement returns to true repentance, undertake it; Otherwise, he should be punished according to law or even released.

Can. 496 . § 1 . Whoever wishes to leave the monastery for serious reasons and return to secular life during his temporary profession must submit his request to the superior of the independent monastery. § 2 . The superior sends this request together with his vote and his advice to the eparchial bishop, whose duty, even in the case of monasteries of pontifical right, is to grant in this case the annulment of the abandonment of the monastery and the return to secular life, unless a particular right reserves this for monasteries located within the territory of the patriarchal Church. 10. About the dismissal of the monks

Can. 497 . § 1 . The member who: 1. has publicly renounced the Catholic faith, will be considered removed from the monastery by right; 2. You entered into a marriage or even attempted to do so in a civil manner. § 2 . In these cases, the superior of the monastery, on his own advice, without delay, issues a statement of the fact, based on the evidence gathered, to legally establish the release, and reports it as soon as possible to the authority to which the monastery is directly subject.

Can. 498 . § 1 . A member who is the cause of an imminent and serious external scandal or damage to the monastery may be immediately expelled from the monastery by the superior of the independent monastery with the consent of his lawyer, and immediately deposited in the monastic habit. § 2 . The superior of the autonomous monastery, if the case arises, will ensure that the dismissal process is carried out in accordance with the law, or will refer the matter to the authority to which the monastery is subject. § 3 . A member expelled from a monastery, which has been established in a holy order, is prohibited from exercising the holy order, unless the authority to which the monastery is subject decides otherwise.

Can. 499 . During a temporary profession, a member may be dismissed by the Superior of the independent monastery with the consent of his council according to Can. 552, §§ 2 and 3, but the dismissal, to be valid, must be confirmed by the eparchial Bishop or, if particular law requires it for monasteries located within the limits of the territory of the Patriarchal Church, by the Patriarch.

Can. 500 . § 1 . The President of a monastic confederation or the Superior of an independent monastery which is not confederated is competent to relieve a member of the perpetual vows of the firm, each with the consent of his council, which in the case together with the presiding Superior must be composed of at least five members to be valid, so that, if the ordinary councilors are absent or missing, others are called according to the norm or statutes of the confederation; and the vote must be done in secret. § 2 . To validly decide the dismissal, in addition to the other conditions established in the typical case, it is required that: 1° the reasons for the dismissal are serious, culpable and legally proven along with the lack of improvement; 2° the dismissal was preceded, unless the nature of the cause of dismissal precludes it, by two warnings with a formal threat of dismissal, which resulted in failure; 3° the reasons for the member's dismissal must be clearly indicated in writing, given to him after each reprimand with full opportunity to defend himself; 4. The useful time of the typical statute has elapsed since the last warning. § 3 . The member's written responses are attached to the records, which must be presented to them, as mentioned in § 1. § 4 . The decree of dismissal cannot be executed without having been approved by the authority to which the monastery is subject.

Can. 501 . § 1 . The dismissal decree will be communicated as soon as possible to the interested member. § 2 . n The member may, however, file an appeal against the dismissal decision within a period of thirty days with suspensive effect, or request that the case be processed through judicial means. § 3 . The Apostolic See or, if it is a member who is domiciled within the territory of the Patriarchal Church, hears the appeal against the decree of dismissal, the Patriarch. § 4 . But if the case has to be processed through judicial means, the court of authority immediately superior to him, which confirmed the decree of dismissal, hears about the matter; On the other hand, the superior who made the dismissal decree will deliver the minutes collected in the case to the same court and will proceed according to the canons of the criminal sentence removed from the appeal.

Can. 502 . With the legitimate dismissal, excluding that mentioned in Can. 497, all ties and obligations derived from the monastic profession cease by law, and if a member has been constituted in a sacred order, Can. 494 must be preserved.

Can. 503 . § 1 . Whoever legally leaves a monastery or is legally expelled from it cannot recover any of the work done there. § 2 . The convention, however, will maintain equity and charity towards the member who separates from it. Art. 3 OF THE ORDERS AND CONGREGATIONS

Can. 504 . § 1 . An order is a society established by a competent ecclesiastical authority, in which its members, although not monks, make a profession equivalent to the monastic. § 2 . A congregation is a society constituted by a competent ecclesiastical authority, in which the members make a profession with the three public vows of obedience, chastity and poverty, which, however, is not equivalent to a monastic profession, but has its own force according to the rule of law.

Can. 505 . § 1 . An order is of pontifical right, if it is established by the Apostolic See or recognized as such by decree of the same; of patriarchal right, if the decree erected by the Patriarch has not obtained the recognition of the Apostolic See. § 2 . A congregation is: 1° of pontifical right, if it was established by the Apostolic See or recognized as such by decree of the same; 2° of patriarchal right, if it was established by the Patriarch or was recognized as such by his decree and did not obtain the decree of recognition from the Apostolic See; 3° of eparchial right, if the decree erected by the eparchial bishop has not obtained the recognition of the Apostolic See or the Patriarch. § 3 . An order or congregation is clerical if, by reason of the aim or purpose intended by the founder, or by force of legitimate custom, it is under the supervision of priests, assumes the ministries proper to the sacred order, and is recognized as such by ecclesiastical authority. 1° On the constitution and suppression of an order, a congregation, a province, a house

Can. 506 . § 1 . n The eparchial bishop can only establish congregations; but he must not erect them without the prior written permission of the Apostolic See, and furthermore within the limits of the territory of the Patriarchal Church without the consultation of the Patriarch. § 2 . The Patriarch may establish orders and congregations with the consent of the permanent Synod and after consulting the Apostolic See. § 3 . Within the limits of the territory of the Patriarchal Church, a congregation of eparchial right, which has spread over several eparchies of the same territory, may be constituted by a decree of patriarchal right of the Patriarch after consulting the interested parties and with the consent of the synod in progress.

Can. 507 . § 1 . An order, even of patriarchal law, legitimately established, even if it is formed by a single house, cannot be suppressed except by the Apostolic See, which is also reserved to decide on the goods of the suppressed order, subject to the will of the offerors. § 2 . A congregation legitimately constituted by patriarchal or eparchial right, even if it is composed of a single house, may be suppressed by the Patriarch, apart from the Apostolic See, within the limits of the territory of the Church over which he presides, after consultation of the interested parties and with the consent of the permanent Synod and the Apostolic See.

Can. 508 . § 1 . A province indicates a part of the same order or congregation composed of several houses, which the major Superior governs directly. § 2 . Dividing an order or congregation into provinces, uniting provinces, limiting or otherwise suppressing them, and establishing new ones, belongs to the authority determined by the statutes of the order or congregation. § 3 . The determination of the assets of the suppressed province, in accordance with justice and the will of the offerors, unless the statutes provide otherwise, corresponds to the General Synaxis or, in urgent cases, to the Superior General with the consent of his lawyer.

Can. 509 . § 1 . An order or congregation cannot erect a valid house without the written consent of the eparchial bishop; If it is about erecting the first house of the order or congregation of patriarchal right in any eparchy, the consent of the Patriarch or, in other cases, of the Apostolic See, within the territory of the patriarchal Church, is required. § 2 . What is said in Can. 437 also applies to houses of orders and congregations.

Can. 510 . A house of order or congregation cannot be suppressed by force except with the consent of the eparchial bishop; but the suppression of a single house from an order or congregation is reserved for the same authority, who according to Can. 507 is responsible for suppressing the order or congregation itself. 2° Of the Superiors, the Synaxes and the financiers in orders and congregations

Can. 511 . § 1 . In the orders and congregations the Superiors and the Synaxes have this power, which is determined by common law and the statutes. § 2 . However, in clerical orders and congregations of pontifical or patriarchal right, the Superiors and Synaxes also have the power of government for the external and internal forum, in accordance with the statutes.

Can. 512 . § 1 . The general synaxis, which is the highest authority for the regulation of the statutes, must be formed in such a way that, representing the entire order or congregation, it becomes a true sign of the same unity in charity. § 2 . Not only the provinces and houses, but also each member can freely express their wishes in the manner determined by the statutes of the General Synaxis.

Can. 513 . § 1 . For members to be validly proposed or elected to the office of Superior, the statutes are required to determine an appropriate period after perpetual profession, which, in the case of major Superiors, must be at least ten years from the first profession. § 2 . If it is a Superior General, it is also required for its validity to have reached thirty-five years of age.

Can. 514 . § 1 . Superiors will be appointed for a specific period and for an appropriate period of time, unless the statutes provide otherwise for the Superior General. § 2 . They may, however, be removed from their position or transferred to another position before the expiration of the established period, for the reasons and in the manner determined by the statutes. § 3 . It is necessary to provide appropriate rules in the statutes so that members cannot be Superiors for a longer period without interruption.

Can. 515 . § 1 . An electoral superior general will be appointed in accordance with the statutes. § 2 . The other Superiors will be appointed in accordance with the statutes, so that, if elected, they will need confirmation from a competent major Superior; However, if they are appointed, appropriate consultation must precede. § 3 . cann. 947 - 960 as well as Can. 445 are carefully observed in the elections.

Can. 516 . § 1 . There must be bursars for the administration of temporal goods in the orders and congregations: a general bursar, who administers the goods of the entire order or congregation, a provincial bursar, that of the province, a local bursar, that of the individual houses; who all fulfill their duty under the control of the Superior. § 2 . The superior mayor himself cannot hold the office of general treasurer and provincial treasurer; but the position of local treasurer, although better distinguished from the position of Superior, can still be combined with it, if necessity requires it. § 3 . If the statutes do not say anything about the manner of appointing financiers, they will be appointed by the Major Superior with the consent of his council. 3° Admission to orders and congregations and to the novitiate

Can. 517 . § 1 . The age required for valid admission to the novitiate of an order or congregation is the completion of the seventeenth year; the other requirements for admission to the novitiate are met cann. 448, 450, 452 et 454. § 2 . No one can be legally admitted to the novitiate of a religious institution of another independent Church without the permission of the Apostolic See, unless it is a candidate who is destined for the province or house, mentioned in Can. 432, of the own Church.
Can. 518 . Before a candidate is admitted to the novitiate, he must be adequately prepared under the special care of an approved member during the time and manner determined by the statutes.
Can. 519 . The right to admit candidates to the novitiate belongs to the Major Superiors in accordance with the statutes Can. 453, §§ 2 and 3.
Can. 520 . The novitiate begins in the manner prescribed by the statutes.
Can. 521 . The establishment, transfer and suppression of the novitiate headquarters is carried out by decree of the Superior General with the consent of his council.

Can. 522 . § 1 . For the novitiate to be valid, it must take place in the house where the novitiate headquarters is located; In special cases and as an exception, with the permission of the Superior General and with the consent of his council, the novitiate may take place in another house of the same order or congregation under the supervision of an approved member acting as master of novices. § 2 . The major superior may allow a group of novices to remain for a certain time in another house of his order or congregation designated by him.

Can. 523 . § 1 . For the validity of the novitiate it is required that it comprise a complete and continuous year; but the absence of less than three months, continuous or interrupted, does not affect the validity, but the missing time, if it exceeds fifteen days, must be made up, even if it has been dedicated to the apostolic exercises to complete the formation of the novices. § 2 . If a longer period of novitiate is prescribed in the statutes, it is not necessary for the profession to be valid.

Can. 524 . § 1 . The training of novices must be carried out as a teacher, according to the rules of the statutes, being a member who demonstrates prudence, charity, piety, knowledge and respect for the religious condition, having professed for at least ten years and, if it is a clerical order or a congregation, appointed in the order of the presbytery. § 2 . The teacher, if necessary, is given collaborators, who support him in everything related to the control of the novices and the training of the novices. § 3 . It is up to the master alone to consult the formation of the novices, and the novitiate alone to control, so that no one can interfere with them under any pretext, except the Superiors whom the statutes allow, and the visitors; but as to the religious discipline of the whole house, the master, like the novice, is subject to the Superior. § 4 . The novice is subject to the authority of the master and superiors and is obliged to obey them.

Can. 525 . § 1 . Those prescribed in cann. 459 - 461 also apply to classes and congregations. § 2 . Before issuing a temporary profession, the novice must, during the entire period in which he is bound by the same profession, hand over the administration of his property that he actually has and that he himself may have later, to whomever he prefers, and freely dispose of the use and usufruct of the same. 4° About profession in orders and congregations

Can. 526 . § 1 . Temporary profession with the three vows of obedience, chastity and poverty is issued for a period determined in the statutes. § 2 . This profession may be renewed several times in accordance with the statutes, so that it may never be extended for a period of less than three years or more than six years.

Can. 527 . For the validity of the temporary profession it is required that: 1° the novitiate has been validly completed; 2° the novice is admitted to profession by a competent Superior, in accordance with the statutes, with the consent of his council, in addition to receiving profession from the same Superior by himself or by another; 3. The profession must be expressed and not given or received by force, serious fear or deception; 4° The other requirements for the validity of the profession established in the statutes must be met.

Can. 528 . The member with temporary vows has the same obligation to observe the statutes as the member with perpetual vows; It lacks active and passive voice, unless expressly provided otherwise in the statutes.

Can. 529 . § 1 . Temporary profession makes acts contrary to the vote illicit, but not invalid. § 2 . This profession does not deprive the partner of ownership of his assets or the ability to acquire other assets; However, it is not lawful for a partner to renounce ownership of his assets on a favorable basis through an inter vivos act. § 3 . But what a member acquires from temporal vows by his own energy or with a view to an order or congregation, he acquires for the order or congregation itself; Unless there is legitimate evidence to the contrary, it is presumed that the member acquires the opinion of the order or congregation. § 4 . The transfer or disposition, mentioned in Can. 525 , § 2 , a member may change temporary vows not at his own discretion, but with the consent of the superior, provided that the change of at least a significant part of the property is not made in favor of the order or congregation; but due to the departure of the order or congregation, such transfer and arrangement ceases to have effect. § 5 . If a member has incurred debts and obligations through temporary vows, he must respond, unless he has carried out the business of the order or congregation with the permission of the Superior. § 6 . Those dismissed for temporary employment are automatically vacated from any professional position.
Can. 530 . In congregations, at least before profession, a member can freely establish a living will, which is also valid in civil law.
Can. 531 . Through perpetual profession, the member definitively assumes religious status, loses his own eparchy and is integrated with full rights into the order or congregation.
Can. 532 . For the validity of the permanent profession, in addition to the requirements mentioned in Can. 464, it is required that the temporary profession has preceded the Can. 526 standard.
Can. 533 . In the orders, perpetual profession is equivalent to perpetual monastic profession, and therefore they are valid for it cann. 466 - 468 .

Can. 534 . In congregations: 1° the canonical effects of perpetual profession remain the same as those determined in Can. 529 of temporary profession, unless otherwise provided by common law; 2° The major superior, with the consent of his lawyer, may grant permission to a member of perpetual vows who requests it to abandon his property, subject to the rules of prudence; 3° It is a general synaxis to introduce in the statutes, if it seems appropriate, a mandatory renunciation of the patrimony acquired or acquired by the member, which, however, cannot be done before perpetual profession.

Can. 535 . § 1 . In the issuance of any profession, the provisions of the statutes will be observed. § 2 . The document of the profession issued, signed by the member himself and by the one who received the profession, also by delegation, will be kept in the archives of the order or congregation; If it is a matter of perpetual profession, the Major Superior must inform as soon as possible the parish priest with whom the member's baptism was registered. 5° Of the formation of members and religious discipline in orders and congregations

Can. 536 . § 1 . The installation method of members is determined by keeping Can. 471 , § 1 in the bylaws. § 2 . The formation of members who are destined for sacred orders must also be carried out according to the clerical formation system, mentioned in Can. 330, at the study headquarters of the order or congregation approved by the General Synaxis or by the Major Superiors in accordance with the statutes; However, if a suitable study location cannot be had according to the Can. 340 , § 1 standard, members must be trained under the direction of an approved director at another seminary or institute of higher learning approved by the ecclesiastical authority.

Can. 537 . § 1 . According to the rules of the statutes, superior elders can give letters of dispensation for holy ordination to members of perpetual vows. § 2 . The bishop to whom the superior must send the letter of dismissal is the eparchial bishop of the place where the person to be ordained has his domicile; but to another bishop, if the eparchial bishop has given permission, or is independent of another church and is to be ordained, or is absent, or, in short, if the eparchial see is vacant and he governs it, who is not ordained bishop; of which it is necessary that the ordaining bishop confirm in each case an authentic document from the eparchial tribunal.

Can. 538 . § 1 . In each house of orders and congregations the praises of God are celebrated according to established and legitimate customs. § 2 . The Superiors will ensure that all members comply with the statutes prescribed in Can. 473 , § 2 § 3 . Members of orders and congregations must receive the sacrament of penance frequently and Can. 474 , § 2

Can. 539 . § 1 . The superiors ensure that they are available to members who can confess. § 2 . The confessors of the clerical orders and of the congregations of pontifical or patriarchal right will be appointed by the Major Superior, in accordance with the statutes; In other cases, however, the local Hierarch listens to the Superior, who must previously consult the interested community.
Can. 540 . Regarding the conduct of the members, it is necessary to observe the provisions of the statutes and outside the houses themselves also the norms of the eparchial bishop.

Can. 541 . The rules on enclosure in the statutes of individual orders and congregations according to their own character are determined by the firm law of Superiors, including local ones, as an act and only for the reason of allowing otherwise.

Can. 542 . The superiors, as members designated by themselves, especially in the eparchy in which they live, if their help is requested by the local Hierarch or by the parish priest to consult the needs of the faithful, they will gladly provide it inside and outside their own churches, preserving the character and religious discipline of the institution.

Can. 543 . A member of an order or congregation who is a pastor remains bound by his vows and remains bound by the other obligations of his profession, as well as by the statutes, to the extent that the observance of these may be compatible with the obligations of his office; With regard to religious discipline, he is subordinate to the Superior, but in those matters that refer to the office of parish priest, he has the same rights and obligations as other parish priests and is subject in the same way to the eparchial bishop. 6° About the transition to another order or congregation or to an independent monastery

Can. 544 . § 1 . Within the limits of the territory of the Patriarchal Church, a member may validly transfer to another religious institution with the written consent of the Patriarch and with the consent of his own Superior General and the Superior General of the order or congregation to which he wishes to transfer, or, if the transition to a monastery is involved, the Superior of an independent monastery; To grant this consent, the Superiors need the prior consent of their council or, if it is a monastery, of the Synaxis. § 2 . A member may validly transfer from a congregation of eparchial right to another religious institution of eparchial right with the written consent of the local eparchial bishop, where the head of the religious institution to which the transfer is made is located, in consultation with the Superior General of the congregation from which the transfer is made, and with the consent of the Superior General of the congregation or the Superior of the independent monastery to which the transfer is made; To grant this consent, the Superiors need the prior consent of their council or, if it is a monastery, of the Synaxis. § 3 . In other cases, a member cannot validly transfer to another religious institution without the consent of the Apostolic See. § 4 . For the validity of the transfer to a religious institution of another independent Church, the consent of the Apostolic See is required.

Can. 545 . § 1 . The transient must complete the novitiate in its entirety, unless the Superior General or the Superior of the independent monastery, each with the consent of his council, reduces the period of the novitiate due to special circumstances, but not less than six months; During the novitiate, during the remaining vows, the particular rights and obligations that the member had in the previous order or congregation are suspended, and he is also subject to the superiors and the master of novices of the new religious institution by force of obedience to the vow. § 2 . Once the novitiate is over, the transient, who has already been professed with perpetual vows, publicly makes perpetual profession according to the provisions of the statutes of the new religious institute, by which profession he is fully integrated into the new institute and, if he is a clergyman, he is also registered as a clergyman; but he who still professes temporary vows will in the same way make a temporary profession that will last at least three years, unless he has completed the full three years of novitiate in the independent monastery to which he passes. § 3 . If a member does not make his profession in a new religious institute, he must return to the previous one, unless the period of profession has meanwhile expired. § 4 . Can. 488 , § 4 will be kept on property and dowry. 7° Of excommunication and departure from the order or congregation

Can. 546 . § 1 . The professed of temporary vows can freely leave the religious institution at the end of the period of profession. § 2 . Whoever, with persistent temporary vows, requests a serious reason to abandon the order or congregation, may obtain from the Superior General, with the consent of his council, the definitive cancellation of the abandonment of the order or congregation and the return to secular life with the effects mentioned in Can. 493; In congregations, the cancellation of the eparchial law must be confirmed as valid by the eparchial bishop of the place where the house leader of the same congregation is located.

Can. 547 . § 1 . The superior superior may, for just cause, by his own decision, exclude a member from temporary vows, from renewing the same vows or from issuing perpetual profession. § 2 . A physical or mental illness, even after a temporary profession, which, according to the judgment of experts, renders a member of temporary vows incapable of leading life in a religious institute, constitutes grounds for not admitting him to renew his temporary profession or to make perpetual profession, unless the illness has been contracted through negligence of the institute or through work performed therein. § 3 . However, if a member has alienated due to continuous temporary vows, even if he cannot make a new profession, he cannot be dismissed from the institution.

Can. 548 . § 1 . The exclusion may be granted by the authority to which the order or congregation is subject, after hearing the Superior General and his opinion; but the imposition of exclusivity is made by the same authority, requesting the consent of his lawyer from the Superior General. § 2 . cann. 489 - 491 remains above the rest on exclusion.

Can. 549 . § 1 . A member cannot ask for the cancellation of his perpetual vows to leave the order or congregation and return to secular life except for the most serious reasons; He had to transmit his request to the Superior General, who would send it, together with his vote and his advice, to the competent authority. § 2 . The cancellation of this type is reserved to the orders of the Apostolic See; but in congregations outside the Apostolic See he can also grant this: 1° the Patriarch to all the members who have their domicile within the limits of the territory of the Church that he is in charge of, after consultation, in the case of congregations of eparchial right, with the eparchial Bishop; 2° The eparchial bishop of the eparchy in which the member has his domicile, if it is a congregation of eparchial right. § 3 . Forgiveness for leaving an order or congregation has the same canonical effects as set forth in Can. 493; but in the case of a member who is constituted in a sacred order, Can. 494 is also valid.

Can. 550 . The member who is illegally absent from the house of his own order or congregation with the intention of evading the authority of the Superiors, is diligently searched for by the Superiors themselves; but if he does not return within the period prescribed by the statutes, he will be punished according to the law or even released. 8° On the expulsion of an order or congregation

Can. 551 . The provisions regarding dismissal or expulsion in cann. 497 y 498 also apply to members of classes or congregations; The competent authority is, effectively, the superior superior, consulted with his lawyer or, if it is an expulsion, with the consent of the same lawyer; If there is a danger of delay and there is no time to go to the Major Superior, the local Superior can also expel the member with the consent of his plan and immediately informing the Major Superior.

Can. 552 . § 1 . A member may be dismissed from temporary vows by the Superior General with the consent of his attorney, unless dismissal is reserved in the statutes to the eparchial bishop or other authority to which the order or congregation is subject. § 2 . To decide the dismissal, in addition to the other conditions provided for by the statutes, the following must be observed: 1° the reasons for the dismissal must be serious and, on the part of the partner, also external and culpable; 2° the lack of religious spirit, which may be a scandal to others, is sufficient cause for dismissal, if repeated warnings and healthy repentance have failed; 3° the reasons for the dismissal must be made known to the dismissing authority, although it is not necessary that they be formally verified; but the member must always appear, giving him full opportunity to defend himself, and his answers must be faithfully presented to the issuing authority. § 3 . An appeal against a dismissal decision has suspensive effect.

Can. 553 . The superior general is competent to release a member from perpetual vows; as for the rest, they must be observed cann. 500 - 503 . CHAPTER II OF COMMON LIFE SOCIETIES LIKE RELIGIOUS SOCIETIES

Can. 554 . § 1 . An institution in which the members profess evangelical counsels by some sacred bond, and not by religious vows, and imitate the way of life of the religious state under the rule of the Superiors according to the statutes, is a society of common life in the manner of the religious. § 2 . This society is of pontifical, patriarchal or eparchial law according to the norm Can. 505, § 2; It is effectively clerical according to the Can. 505, § 3 norm; It depends on the ecclesiastical authority as congregations according to the norm cann. 413 - 415, 419, 420, § 3 and, except for the special law established by the Apostolic See, Can. 418, § 2. § 3 . The members of these societies, with respect to canonical effects, are equivalent to religious ones, unless otherwise provided by law or determined by the nature of the matter.
Can. 555 . All members of these societies are subject to the Roman Pontiff as supreme superior, to whom they are bound by the duty of obedience also by virtue of the sacred bond of obedience.
Can. 556 . Regarding the establishment and suppression of the society and its provinces or houses, the same rules apply as those established for congregations in cann. 506 - 510.
Can. 557 . Governance is determined by the company's bylaws, but the rules on congregations in cann. 422 y 511 - 515 will apply to all, unless the nature of the matter prevents it.

Can. 558 . § 1 . The company and its legally constituted provinces and houses are legal entities in their own right according to the Can. 423 standard. § 2 . Asset administration is governed by cann. 424, 425 et 516. § 3 . Everything that happens to the members in view of the society, is acquired by the society; The partners retain, acquire and manage the other assets in accordance with the statutes.

Can. 559 . § 1 . When admitting candidates to the company, the statutes are respected by keeping cann. 450 y 451. § 2 . Regarding the appointment of members, the statutes are also observed; But in the training of those destined for sacred orders, the canons relating to the training of clerics are also observed.

Can. 560 . § 1 . The major superior of the society, according to the norms of the statutes, can give its members, who are permanently recruited, letters of dismissal for sacred ordination; these letters should be sent to the Bishop, from whom in Can. 537 , § 2 . § 2 . A member permanently enrolled as a cleric is enrolled in the society by diaconal ordination or, in the case of a cleric already enrolled in an eparchy, by permanent enrollment.

Can. 561 . The members of the company are bound by the obligations that common law prescribes to the secretaries, unless otherwise provided by law or the nature of the matter, by the firm rights and obligations determined by the statutes.

Can. 562 . § 1 . For the transfer to another society of common life, such as a religious or religious institute, the consent of the Superior General of the society from which the transfer occurs is required and, if it is a transfer to a society or institute of another independent Church, also the consent of the Apostolic See. § 2 . A member who passes to a religious institute must complete a full novitiate and is equal to other novices of the same institute; the profession must respect the statutes of the new institution. § 3 . In the company cann. 497 y 498 is competent to dismiss a member who has been hired permanently, except the rest cann. 500 - 503; a temporarily hired member is fired according to the Can. 552 rule. § 4 . The company's statutes will determine the authority whose responsibility it is to dissolve the sacred bond. CHAPTER III OF THE INSTITUTIONS OF THE CENTURY

Can. 563 . § 1 . A secular institute is a society in which the members: 1° tend to dedicate themselves entirely to God through the profession of the three evangelical councils, according to the statutes, strengthened by some sacred bond recognized by the Church; 2° they exercise apostolic activity as leaven in the world and of the world, in such a way that everything for the strength and growth of the Body of Christ is impregnated with the evangelical spirit; 3. They do not imitate the way of life of the religious, but live in communion with each other according to their own statutes; 4. The clergy or laity, for all canonical purposes, remain in their own state. § 2 . Secular institutions are of pontifical right, patriarchal right or eparchial right according to the norm Can. 505, § 2.
Can. 564 . The members of secular institutes are subject to the Roman Pontiff as supreme superior, to whom they are bound by the duty of obedience also by virtue of the sacred bond of obedience.

Can. 565 . A member of a secular institute is enrolled by diaconal ordination as a clergyman of the eparchy for whose service he was ordained, unless by virtue of a grant from the Apostolic See or, if it is a secular institute of patriarchal right, he is enrolled in the same institute of the Patriarch.

Can. 566 . Regarding the creation and suppression of secular institutes, their statutes and their dependence on ecclesiastical authority, which were established over the congregations in cann. 414, 506, 507, § 2, 509 and 510, must be observed.

Can. 567 . § 1 . Secular organizations and their legitimately constituted provinces and houses are legal entities in their own right according to the Can. 423 standard. § 2 . Asset administration is governed by cann. 424 y 425.

Can. 568 . § 1 . When admitting candidates, the company's statutes Can. 450 will be observed. § 2 . The permanent member of a secular institute is removed by decree issued in accordance with the statutes, which cannot be executed without the approval of the eparchial bishop or a competent higher authority; It is also the eparchial authority or that of the bishop himself to release the sacred bond.

Can. 569 . It is the particular right of each independent Church to decide with greater precision on secular institutions. CHAPTER IV OF OTHER FORMS OF CONSECRATED LIFE AND SOCIETIES OF APOSTOLIC LIFE

Can. 570 . By private right, other classes of ascetics may be established, imitating the eremitic life, whether or not they belong to the institutes of consecrated life; Likewise, consecrated virgins and widows can establish themselves separately in the world by professing chastity through public profession.

Can. 571 . It is solely up to the Apostolic See to approve new forms of consecrated life; Patriarchs and eparchial bishops must strive to discern the new gifts of consecrated life entrusted to them by the Holy Spirit of the Church and help their promoters so that they can better express their objectives and protect them with appropriate statutes.

Can. 572 . Societies of apostolic life, whose members, without religious vows, pursue the apostolic goal proper to the society and, leading a fraternal life in common according to their way of life, tend to the perfection of charity through the observance of the constitutions, and who approach the institutions of consecrated life, are governed only by the particular law of their own Church or established by the Apostolic See. TITLE XIII OF CHRISTIFIED ASSOCIATIONS

Can. 573 . § 1 . Associations created by the competent ecclesiastical authority or approved by it by decree are legal persons in the Church and are called public associations. § 2 . Other associations, although praised or recommended by ecclesiastical authority, are called private associations; These associations are not recognized in the Church, unless their statutes are recognized by the competent authority, but as for the rest they are governed only by a particular and firm law Can. 577.

Can. 574 . Except for the others, Can. 18 is the only ecclesiastical authority competent to establish associations of faithful that propose to impart Christian doctrine in the name of the Church or promote public worship or that pursue other purposes, the exercise of which is by nature reserved to the same ecclesiastical authority.

Can. 575 . § 1 . The competent authority to establish or approve Christian associations is for the associations and confederations thereof: 1° for eparchies, the eparchial Bishop, not the Administrator of the eparchy, except those associations whose establishment is reserved for others by apostolic or patriarchal privilege; 2° that they are open to all the Christian faithful of any independent patriarchal or metropolitan Church and that have their main seat in the territory of the same Church, the Patriarch having consulted the permanent Synod or the Metropolitan the two eparchial bishops with major episcopal ordination; 3. Another type of Apostolic See. § 2 . The establishment of a section of any non-eparchial association requires the written consent of the eparchial bishop; However, the consent given by the eparchial bishop for the establishment of a house of a religious institution is also valid for the establishment of an association in the same house or church attached to it, which is specific to that institution.

Can. 576 . § 1 . Every association will have its own statutes, which will determine the name of the association, its purpose, headquarters, government and the conditions required for its registration; Furthermore, the statutes determine the methods of action, taking into account the rite of the independent Church, the needs of the place and time, or interest. § 2 . The statutes and their modification require the approval of the ecclesiastical authority that established or approved the association.

Can. 577 . § 1 . Every association is subject to the supervision of the ecclesiastical authority that established or approved it; It is the duty of this authority to ensure that the same integrity of faith and morals is preserved, and to ensure that abuses are not introduced into ecclesiastical discipline. § 2 . It is the responsibility of the eparchial bishop to watch over all associations that carry out activity in his territory and, if the case arises, to inform the authority that has constituted or approved it and, furthermore, if the activity of the association produces serious damage to doctrine or ecclesiastical discipline or constitutes a scandal for the Christian faithful, to apply appropriate measures in the meantime.

Can. 578 . § 1 . The admission of members will be carried out in accordance with common law and the statutes of the association. § 2 . The same person can be registered in several associations. § 3 . Members of religious institutions may give their name to associations in accordance with the rules or statutes with the consent of their Superior.

Can. 579 . No association of Christians may register its own members as clerics except with a special grant from the Apostolic See or, if it is an association, about which in Can. 575 , § 1 , n. 2, is discussed, given by the Patriarch with the consent of the permanent Synod.

Can. 580 . He who has publicly renounced the Catholic faith, or who has publicly failed in communion with the Catholic Church, or who has been involved in a major excommunication, cannot be validly received into associations; but if it has already been legitimately registered, it will be declared released by the local Hierarch himself.
Can. 581 . No legally registered person may be dismissed from the association except for justified cause in accordance with common law and the statutes.

Can. 582 . A legally constituted or approved association manages temporary assets in accordance with the cann. 1007 - 1054 and statutes under the supervision of the authority that established or approved it, to which it must submit annual accounts of its management.

Can. 583 . § 1 . Associations created or approved by the Apostolic See can only be suppressed by it. § 2 . The other associations, firm Can. 927, § 2 and except for the right to resort suspensively to the rule of law, can be suppressed, except by the Apostolic See: 1° by the Patriarch with the consent of the permanent Synod or by the Metropolitan, who is in charge of the independent metropolitan Church, with the consent of two eparchial bishops by episcopal ordination of the elders; 2° by the eparchial bishop, if they were erected or approved by him. TITLE XIV OF THE EVANGELIZATION OF THE GENTILES

Can. 584 . § 1 . Obeying Christ's mandate to evangelize all nations and moved by the grace and charity of the Holy Spirit, the Church recognizes itself as entirely missionary. § 2 . The evangelization of nations must be carried out in such a way that, preserving the integrity of faith and morals, the Gospel can be expressed in the culture of each people, that is, in catechesis, in the liturgical rites themselves, in sacred art, particularly in law and, finally, in all ecclesial life.

Can. 585 . § 1 It is up to each Church to ensure that the Gospel is preached throughout the world under the supervision of the Roman Pontiff, through heralds duly prepared and sent by the competent authority, in accordance with the norm of common law. § 2 . In the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or in the Council of Hierarchs, there is a commission to promote more effective collaboration of all the eparchies in the missionary activity of the Church. § 3 . In each eparchy a priest will be appointed to effectively promote mission projects. § 4 . May the faithful foster knowledge and love of the missions in themselves and others, pray for them and encourage vocations, and support them generously with their resources.

Can. 586 . It is strictly prohibited that anyone be forced to embrace the Church, nor induced or seduced through importunities; but that all Christian faithful see to it that the right to religious freedom is vindicated, that no one is dissuaded from the Church by unjust persecutions.

Can. 587 . § 1 . Those who wish to join the Church must be admitted through liturgical ceremonies to the catechumenate, which is not a mere exposition of dogmas and precepts, but a duly prolonged formation and preparation of the entire Christian life. § 2 . Those enrolled in the catechumenate have the right to be admitted to the liturgy of the word and other liturgical celebrations not reserved for the faithful. § 3 . It is a particular right to establish the rules according to which the catechumens are organized, determining what the catechumens must do and what prerogatives they are recognized.

Can. 588 . It is essential that catechumens be registered in any independent Church according to the Can. 30 norm; But be careful not to suggest anything to them that could prevent them from joining the Church, which is more coherent with their culture.

Can. 589 . Missionaries, whether foreign or indigenous, must be qualified with appropriate gifts and talents; They must be properly trained in missiology and missionary spirituality, as well as in the history and culture of the peoples who are to be evangelized.

Can. 590 . In missionary activity it is necessary to ensure that the young Churches reach maturity as soon as possible and are fully constituted, so that they can fend for themselves under the guidance of their own hierarchy and can take on and continue the work of evangelization.

Can. 591 . Missionaries must diligently ensure that: 1° vocations to sacred ministries are prudently promoted among neophytes, so that the new Church may flourish as soon as possible among the native clergy; 2° the catechists are formed in such a way that, as strong collaborators of the sacred ministers, they can play their role in evangelization and liturgical activity to the best of their ability; A special law should be provided for, so that catechists have fair remuneration.

Can. 592 . § 1 . In mission territories, special care must be taken to promote appropriate forms of lay apostolate; Institutions of consecrated life must be promoted, taking into account the character and character of each people; As necessary, schools and other similar institutions of Christian education and cultural development should be established. § 2 . Likewise, dialogue and cooperation with non-Christians must be carefully and prudently encouraged.

Can. 593 . § 1 . All priests, whatever their status, who work in the mission territories, as if they formed a single presbytery, must fervently cooperate in evangelization. § 2 . They and the other Christian missionaries, to give a single testimony of Christ the Lord, willingly cooperate according to the Can. 908 standard.

Can. 594 . They are the territories of the missions that the Apostolic See has recognized as such. TITLE XV OF ECCLESIASTICAL ADMINISTRATION CHAPTER I OF THE TEACHING FUNCTION OF THE CHURCH IN GENERAL

Can. 595 . § 1 . The Church, to whom Christ the Lord entrusted the deposit of faith, so that, with the help of the Holy Spirit, the revealed truth may be sanctified, thoroughly investigated, faithfully announced and expounded, has a natural right independent of any human power and the obligation to preach the Gospel to all men. § 2 . It is the duty of the Church always and everywhere to announce moral principles, also those relating to the social order, and to judge all human affairs, to the extent that the dignity of the human person and his fundamental rights or the security of souls demand it.

Can. 596 . The task of teaching in the name of the Church corresponds solely to the bishops; However, both those who have been made cooperators of the bishops by the sacred order, and those who have received the mandate to teach without being established in the sacred order, have a part in the same office, according to law.

Can. 597 . § 1 . The Roman Pontiff rejoices in the infallibility of his magisterial office, if, as supreme Pastor and Teacher of all Christians, whose duty it is to confirm his brothers in the faith, he proclaims the doctrine of faith or morals that must be sustained by a definitive act. § 2 . The Episcopal College will also have infallibility in teaching, if the teaching is exercised by bishops gathered in an Ecumenical Council, who, as teachers of faith and morals and judges of the entire Church, declare that the doctrine of faith or morals is definitively maintained, or if, maintaining the bond of communion spread throughout the world among themselves and with the successor of Saint Peter, together with the Roman Pontiff himself, authentically teaching the questions of faith or morals, they agree on a opinion that should be had. Definitely. § 3 . No doctrine is understood to be infallibly defined unless it is clearly established.

Can. 598 . In the divine and Catholic faith, all those things must be believed that are contained in the written or transmitted word of God, that is, the only deposit of faith entrusted to the Church, and at the same time they are proposed as divinely revealed, either by the solemn magisterium of the Church, or by its ordinary and universal magisterium, which is certainly manifested by the common adherence of the faithful under the direction of the sacred magisterium; Therefore, all Christians are obligated; avoid any doctrine that is contrary to it.

Can. 599 . In effect, it is not the assent of faith that must be guaranteed, but rather the religious obedience of the intellect and will to the doctrine of faith and morals, which is enunciated by the Roman Pontiff or the College of Bishops, when they exercise the authentic magisterium, even if they do not intend to proclaim it in a definitive act; Therefore, Christians are careful to avoid things that do not agree with the same.

Can. 600 . The bishops who are in communion with the head of the College and with the members, whether individually or gathered in synods or in particular councils, although they are not strong in the teaching of infallibility, are authentic teachers and masters of the faith of the faithful entrusted to their care; to which the Christian faithful are obliged to adhere with religious obedience to the authentic teaching of their bishops.

Can. 601 . It is up to each Church, especially the patriarchs and bishops, to exercise it in a manner adapted to each generation and culture, to answer the perennial questions of men about the meaning of life, as well as to advise on the Christian solution to pressing problems, in the light of the Gospel, examining the signs of the times, so that everywhere the light of Christ illuminates all men.

Can. 602 . In pastoral care, not only the principles of the sacred sciences are recognized and used, but also the knowledge of other sciences, so as to lead the faithful to a more conscious and reflective life of faith.

Can. 603 . The culture of letters and the arts, due to its power to express and communicate the meaning of faith with singular effectiveness, must be recognized with fair freedom and cultural diversity.

Can. 604 . The Pastors of the Church must, above all, diligently ensure that the same sense of faith is preserved and promoted among the various doctrinal statements of the various Churches, in such a way that the integrity and unity of the faith is not damaged, but that the catholicity of the Church is better brought to light through legitimate diversity.

Can. 605 . It is up to the Bishops especially gathered in Synods or Councils, but particularly to the Apostolic See, to religiously promote, guard and defend with authority the integrity and unity of the faith and good customs, even rebuking, to the necessary extent, opinions that are contrary to them, or warning against them, which may endanger them.

Can. 606 . § 1 . It is for theologians, because of their deeper understanding of the mystery of salvation and their experience in the sacred and related sciences, as well as their experience in new questions, faithfully obeying the authentic teaching of the Church and at the same time using their equal freedom to illustrate and defend the faith of the Church and to consult for doctrinal progress. § 2 . In investigating and expressing theological truths, they must be concerned with building the community of faith and skillfully cooperating with bishops in their task of teaching. § 3 . Those engaged in theological studies, especially in seminaries, universities and colleges, should strive to cooperate with people who excel in other sciences, with shared ideas and strengths. CHAPTER II OF THE MINISTRY OF THE WORDS OF GOD

Can. 607 . The ministry of the Word of God, that is, preaching, catechesis and all Christian instruction, among which liturgical homilies must have an exceptional place, must be healthily nourished by the Holy Scriptures and based on sacred tradition; but the celebration of the word of God must be encouraged in a timely manner.

Can. 608 . Bishops, priests and deacons, for their respective sacred degrees, have the first office of ministering the word of God, to exercise the rule of law; but the other faithful, according to their own aptitude, state of life and mandate received, should gladly participate in this service. Art. 1 ON THE PREACHING OF THE WORD OF GOD
Can. 609 . The eparchial bishop has the right by common law to control the preaching of the word of God in his territory.

Can. 610 . § 1 . Bishops have the right to preach the word of God throughout the world, unless the eparchial bishop expressly refuses in a special case. § 2 . Priests are endowed with the ability to preach wherever they are legitimately sent or invited. § 3 . Deacons are also endowed with the same capacity to preach, unless particular law determines otherwise. § 4 . In extraordinary circumstances, especially to make up for a shortage of clergy, the eparchial bishop may also give the mandate to preach in the firm church Can. 614 , § 4 .

Can. 611 . By virtue of the office, all those entrusted with the care of souls are endowed with the ability to preach, and they may also invite any firm priest or deacon Can. 610 , § 3 entrusted to their care to preach, unless they are legally prohibited.

Can. 612 . § 1 . In religious institutions or societies of common life, it is up to the Major Superiors to control the preaching of papal or patriarchal law, as well as clerical religious. § 2 . Indeed, all Superiors, including local Superiors, of any institute of consecrated life may invite any firm priest or deacon Can. 610 , § 3 to preach to their own members, unless legally prohibited.
Can. 613 . Against the Hierarch's decree, which prohibits preaching, one can only resort to restitution, which must be determined without delay.

Can. 614 . § 1 . The homily, in which the mysteries of the faith and the norms of the Christian life are explained from the Holy Scriptures throughout the liturgical year, is highly recommended as part of the liturgy itself. § 2 . The parish priest and the rector of the churches have the obligation to ensure that, at least on Sundays and holidays, there is a homily as part of the Divine Liturgy, which should not be omitted except for serious reasons. § 3 . It is not lawful for a priest to habitually pay through another for the obligation to preach to the people in charge of his pastoral care, except for a just cause approved by the local Hierarch. § 4 . The homily is reserved for the priest or, according to the norm of particular law, also for the deacon.
Can. 615 . The eparchial bishops, given the norms, ensure that a special series of sacred sermons are celebrated at appropriate times for the spiritual renewal of the Christian people.

Can. 616 . § 1 . The preachers of the word of God, leaving aside the words of human wisdom and the abstruse arguments of the faithful, preach the whole mystery of Christ, which is the way, the truth and the life; that show that earthly things and human institutions, according to the plan of God the Creator, are also ordered for the salvation of men and, therefore, can contribute not a little to the edification of the Body of Christ. § 2 . Therefore, they also teach the teaching of the Church on the dignity of the human person and his fundamental rights, on family life, on civil and social collaboration, as well as on the search for a sense of justice in economic life and at work, which contributes to building peace in the world and achieving the progress of peoples. Art. II ON THE CATECHEICAL INSTITUTION

Can. 617 . It is a grave obligation of each independent Church, especially its Bishops, to provide catechists through whom the faith matures and the disciple of Christ is formed through a deeper and more organized knowledge of the doctrine of Christ and through an ever closer adherence to the Person Himself.

Can. 618 . Parents are obligated first, by word and example, to train their children in the faith and practice of the Christian life; Those who occupy the place of parents and godparents are subject to the same obligation.

Can. 619 . In addition to the Christian family, the parish itself and any ecclesial community must take care of the catechetical formation of its members and their integration into their own community, providing them with those conditions in which they can live as fully as possible what they have learned.

Can. 620 . Associations, movements and circles of the faithful, whether their objective is piety and apostolate or works of charity and assistance, deal with the religious formation of their members under the direction of the local Hierarch.

Can. 621 . § 1 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or the Council of Hierarchs is competent, within the territorial limits of the Church itself, to apply the norms of catechetical training contained in the Catechetical Directory that is conveniently prepared, observing those prescribed by the supreme authority of the Church. § 2 . In the catechetical directory, the special nature of the Eastern Churches must be taken into account, so that in catechesis they highlight the biblical and liturgical importance, as well as the traditions of the independent Church in patrology, hagiography and iconography itself. § 3 . The Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or the Council of Hierarchs must ensure that catechisms adapted to the various groups of Christians are provided along with resources and instruments, as well as that the various catechetical initiatives are promoted and coordinated with each other.

Can. 622 . § 1 . In every autonomous Church there is a commission on catechesis, which can also be established with other autonomous Churches of the same territory or sociocultural region. § 2 . A catechetical center must also be available to the commission on catechetical matters, the purpose of which is to be a resource for the Churches themselves to coordinate catechetical projects and pay more effectively and serve the ongoing formation of catechists.

Can. 623 . § 1 . It is the responsibility of the eparchial bishop to promote, direct and control catechetical education in his eparchy with the greatest concern. § 2 . For which purpose is the eparchial catechetical center of the eparchial tribunal.

Can. 624 . § 1 . The parish priest must pay maximum attention to the norms established by the competent authority to provide catechism to all those entrusted to his pastoral care, whatever their age or condition. § 2 . Priests and deacons assigned to the parish are obliged to provide assistance to parishioners; and members of religious institutes according to the cann. 479 y 542 § 3 standard. Other Christians who have been properly formed are willing to contribute to the teaching of catechism.

Can. 625 . Catechesis must have an ecumenical reason, providing a correct image of other Churches and ecclesial Communities; However, it is absolutely necessary to ensure that the correct system of Catholic catechesis is secure. Can: 626 - All those who serve to teach the catechism remember that they are members of the Church and that they were sent to communicate the revealed word of God, not their own; Therefore, they must present the entire doctrine of the Church in a way adapted to catechesis and responding to the demands of their culture. CHAPTER III OF CATHOLIC EDUCATION

Can. 627 . § 1 . The care of children's education is directed mainly to parents or those who take their place; Therefore, it is the same in the environment of the Christian family, illuminated by faith and animated by mutual love, to educate children above all in piety towards God and love of neighbor. § 2 . If one's own strength is exceeded, to guarantee the complete education of one's children, it is also up to parents to entrust part of the task of education to others, as well as to choose the necessary or useful educational instruments. § 3 . Parents must have adequate freedom to choose the means of education, signature Can. 633 ; Therefore, the Christian faithful must ensure that this right is recognized by civil society and that, according to the demands of the institution, it is also promoted with adequate resources.

Can. 628 . § 1 . For the Church, when it has generated new creatures through baptism, it is incumbent, together with the parents, to take care of Catholic education itself. § 2 . All those entrusted with the care of souls must help parents in the education of their children, make them aware of their own rights and obligations and ensure religious education, especially of the young.

Can. 629 . Let all educators ensure that attention is paid to the formation of the entire human person, so that young people, harmoniously cultivated in physical, intellectual and moral gifts, endowed with Christian virtues, may be conformed to know and love God more perfectly, to appreciate human and moral values ​​with a right conscience and to embrace true freedom, and at the same time to pursue fraternal association with others with a cultivated sense of justice and social responsibility.

Can. 630 . § 1 . Let the Christian faithful work with great hearts, so that the benefits of appropriate education and instruction spread more quickly to all the peoples of the world, taking special care of those of lesser fortune. § 2 . All the faithful support appropriate Church initiatives for the advancement of education, especially to erect, direct and sustain schools. Art. I IN SCHOOLS, ESPECIALLY CATHOLIC

Can. 631 . § 1 . Among the various means of education, the Catholic school must be promoted with special care, in which the concern of parents, teachers and the ecclesial community must converge. § 2 . It is the right of the Church to establish and regulate schools of every type and degree.
Can. 632 . A school is not considered Catholic in law unless it has been established as such by the eparchial bishop or by a higher ecclesiastical authority or recognized as such by them.

Can. 633 . § 1 . It is up to the eparchial bishop to judge and decide on the schools, whether or not they correspond to the demands of Christian education; It is also convenient for him, for a serious reason, to prevent attendance at any Christian school. § 2 . Parents should ensure that their children are sent to Catholic schools at the same level as others.

Can. 634 . § 1 . The Catholic school is the obligation of the scientific community to create an environment animated by the evangelical spirit of freedom and charity, to help young people to develop in themselves and to grow together according to the new creation they have made through baptism, and to order all human culture to the message of salvation, in such a way that the knowledge that students acquire about the world, life and man is illuminated by faith. § 2 . It is up to the competent ecclesiastical authority to adapt them to the specific circumstances of the Catholic school itself, if it is attended mainly by non-Catholic students. § 3 . The Catholic school is no less than other schools in pursuing the cultural and human and social formation of young people.

Can. 635 . It is especially the responsibility of the eparchial bishop to ensure the existence of Catholic schools, especially where other schools, including professional and technical schools, are lacking or insufficient, to the extent that the circumstances of place and time specifically demand them.

Can. 636 . § 1 . Catechetical training in any school is subject to the authority and supervision of the eparchial bishop. § 2 . It is also the duty of the eparchial bishop to appoint or approve the teachers of the Catholic religion and, if reasons of faith or morality so require, to remove them or demand their removal.
Can. 637 . In schools where Catholic instruction is lacking or insufficient in the judgment of the eparchial bishop, true Catholic formation must be provided to all Catholic students.

Can. 638 . § 1 . The eparchial bishop has the right to canonically visit all existing Catholic schools in his eparchy, with the exception of schools that are open exclusively to the students of the institutes of consecrated life of pontifical or patriarchal right, and except in any case for the autonomy of the institutes of consecrated life to control their own schools. § 2 . When there are several eparchial bishops, the right of canonical visitation corresponds to the one who founded or approved the college, unless otherwise provided in the statutes of the foundation or in a special agreement concluded between them.

Can. 639 . Teachers, as they are the most responsible, so that the Catholic school can make its objectives and initiatives a reality, they must be excellent in their teaching and role models for the testimony of their lives, and they must work as collaborators, especially with parents, but also with other schools. Art. II OF THE CATHOLIC UNIVERSITIES OF STUDIES

Can. 640 . § 1 . The universality of Catholic studies pursues this objective, so that the public, stable and universal presence of Christian thought is realized in the effort to promote general culture; For this reason, he established an institution of research, reflection and instruction of a higher order, in which multiple human knowledges are illuminated by the light of the Gospel. § 2 . Other institutions of higher learning or autonomous Catholic faculties, pursuing the same objective, are equivalent to the university of Catholic studies, but not to the universities and faculties of ecclesiastical studies, as mentioned in cann. 646 - 650.

Can. 641 . In Catholic universities of study, each discipline is cultivated with its own principles, its own method, and its own freedom of scientific inquiry, so that a deeper understanding of those disciplines is gained, and by careful consideration of the new questions and investigations of the advancing age, a deeper insight is gained into how faith and reason conspire into a single truth, and men truly excellent in learning are formed, prepared for greater responsibilities in society and witnesses of faith in the world.

Can. 642 . § 1 . The Catholic University of Standards is an institution of higher learning, which has been created or approved as such, either by the highest administrative authority of the independent Church, after consultation with the Apostolic See, or by the Apostolic See itself; which must be recorded in a public document. § 2 . Within the boundaries of the territory of the Patriarchal Church, this highest authority is the Patriarch with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church.
Can. 643 . In Catholic universities of studies, where there is no theology faculty, at least theology courses must be taught to accommodate students from the different faculties.

Can. 644 . Those who teach disciplines related to faith and morals in universities of Catholic studies must be covered by the mandate of the ecclesiastical authority designated by them, as mentioned in Can. 642; The same authority may withdraw this mandate for serious reasons, especially if there is a lack of scientific or pedagogical competence, honesty or integrity in teaching.

Can. 645 . It is up to the hierarchs to foresee a concerted plan, so that also in other universities and Catholic university centers there are prisoners, in which the Christian faithful, carefully selected and prepared, can provide permanent spiritual and intellectual assistance to young university students. Art. 3 OF ECCLESIASTICAL STUDIES IN UNIVERSITIES AND FACULTIES

Can. 646 . Ecclesiastical hierarchs must constantly promote universities and faculties of study, that is, those that deal mainly with divine Revelation and the sciences related to it and, therefore, more closely related to the evangelizing task of the Church.

Can. 647 . The objective of the university or faculty of ecclesiastical studies is: 1° to investigate in depth and scientifically the divine relationship and everything related to it, to systematically develop and organize the truths of divine revelation, to consider the new questions of the advancing age in its light and to present them to the people of the time adapted to their own culture; 2° to form students more deeply in the various disciplines according to Catholic teaching and to prepare them adequately for the different works of apostolate, ministry or teaching in the same disciplines and to promote continuous formation.

Can. 648 . Universities and faculties of ecclesiastical studies are those that have been canonically established or approved by the competent ecclesiastical authority to develop and transmit the sacred sciences and the sciences related to them and have been augmented with the right to confer academic degrees that have canonical effects.

Can. 649 . The establishment or approval of universities or ecclesiastical faculties is carried out by the Apostolic See or a higher administrative authority, as discussed in Can. 642, together with the Apostolic See.

Can. 650 . Regarding the statutes of ecclesiastical studies of a university or college, especially with regard to governance, administration, the appointment or dismissal of professors, the study program and the granting of academic titles, the regulations issued by the Apostolic See must be observed. CHAPTER IV OF SOCIAL COMMUNICATION INSTRUMENTS AND PARTICULARLY OF BOOKS

Can. 651 . § 1 . To carry out the task of announcing the Gospel throughout the world, the Church is obliged to use appropriate means and, therefore, the right to use social media and, in particular, to freely publish writings in print must be claimed everywhere. § 2 . May all the faithful cooperate with their part in the great mission of the Church and support and encourage the projects of this apostolate; Furthermore, especially those who know how to create and transmit communications, diligently help the pastoral activity of the Bishops and strive with all diligence so that the use of these instruments is impregnated with the spirit of Christ.

Can. 652 . § 1 . Eparchial bishops must ensure that, with the help of social media institutions in particular, the faithful are taught about the critical and profitable use of the same media; foster cooperation between these various institutions; provide for the training of experts; Finally, what more can be done than to punish and condemn bad things, to promote good projects by praising and blessing especially good books. § 2 . To protect the integrity of faith and morals, the eparchial bishop, the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, the Council of Hierarchs and the Apostolic See have the right to prevent Christian faithful from using social communication tools to the extent that they are harmful to their integrity, or from sharing them with others.
Can. 653 . It is a particular right to establish more precise rules on the use of radio, cinema, television and similar media when dealing with them, which relate to Catholic teaching or behavior.
Can. 654 . The common law rules relating to books also apply to any other writings or speeches intended for public dissemination and reproduction by technical inventions in any form.

Can. 655 . § 1 . Access to the Holy Scriptures must be widely open to the faithful; Consequently, appropriate and correct versions, provided with sufficient explanations, where lacking, must be prepared by the care of the eparchial bishops or, insofar as this can be conveniently and usefully done, by common work with other Christians. § 2 . All Christian believers, especially pastors of souls, should take care to distribute copies of the Holy Scriptures with appropriate annotations and adapted for the use of non-Christians as well. § 3 . For liturgical or catechetical use, only those editions of the Holy Scriptures that have been granted ecclesiastical approval should be used; other editions must at least be protected by ecclesiastical license.

Can. 656 . § 1 . Only books with ecclesiastical approval should be used in liturgical celebrations. § 2 . Precum or devotional books intended for public or private use by the faithful require ecclesiastical license.

Can. 657 . § 1 . The approval of liturgical texts is reserved in the Patriarchal Churches with the prior review of the Apostolic See by the Patriarch with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church; in the Metropolitan Churches of the autonomous Metropolitan with the consent of the Council of Hierarchs; In the other Churches, this is an exclusive right of the Apostolic See, and within the limits of the statutes of the bishops and their legitimately constituted groups. § 2 . The same authorities also have the right to approve versions of the same books intended for liturgical use, made in relation to the Apostolic See, in the case of independent patriarchal or metropolitan Churches. § 3 . To republish liturgical books or their versions in another language intended for liturgical use or their parts, it is necessary and sufficient to confirm their agreement with the edition approved by the certification of the local Hierarch, as mentioned in Can. 662, § 1. § 4 . In changes to the liturgical text Can. 40 , § 1
