Can. 658 . § 1 . Catechisms, as well as other writings intended for catechetical instruction in schools of each type and level or their versions, need ecclesiastical approval. § 2 . The same rule should apply to other books dealing with faith or morals if they are used as texts on which catechetical instruction is based.

Can. 659 . It is recommended that any writing illustrating Catholic faith or morals be at least obtained by ecclesiastical license, except for the provisions of institutes of consecrated life, which require more.

Can. 660 . In newspapers, newspapers or periodical pamphlets, which tend to openly attack the Catholic religion or good morals, the Christian faithful should not write anything except for a just and reasonable reason; Additionally, clerics and members of religious institutes only with their permission, as mentioned in Can. 662.

Can. 661 . § 1 . An ecclesiastical license with a single printed word means that the work is free of errors about the Catholic faith as a moral. § 2 . The approval granted by the competent authority demonstrates that the text accepted by the Church or the work is in accordance with the authentic teaching of the Church. § 3 . If, in addition, the work has been praised or blessed by the eparchial bishop or by a higher authority, this means that it well expresses the authentic teaching of the Church and, therefore, it should be recommended.

Can. 662 . § 1 . Ecclesiastical approval or permission to publish books, unless the law expressly provides otherwise, may be granted either by the local Hierarch of the author or by the Hierarch of the place where they are published, or finally by a higher authority exercising the executive power of government over persons or places. § 2 . Members of religious institutes, in order to publish written matters that deal with Catholic faith or morals, also need the authorization of their Major Superior, in accordance with the norm or statutes.

Can. 663 . § 1 . The license to publish any work or the approval, praise or blessing of any work is valid for the original text, but not for new editions or versions. § 2 . If these are editions of the Holy Scriptures or other books that require ecclesiastical approval in accordance with the law, the approval legitimately granted by a local Hierarch is not enough for them to be used in another eparchy, but the explicit consent of the local Hierarch of the same eparchy is required.

Can. 664 . § 1 . The judgment on the books may be entrusted by the local Hierarch to censors from a list drawn up by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or by the Council of Hierarchs, or by his prudence to other persons whom he trusts; Finally, a special commission of censors can be established, which can consult the local Hierarch, the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or the Council of Hierarchs. § 2 . The censors must be chosen with excellent knowledge, correct doctrine and prudence, and in the fulfillment of their duty, apart from any acceptance of persons, they must issue a judgment according to Catholic teaching, as proposed by the authentic teaching of the Church. § 3 . Reviewers must give their opinion in writing; which, if favorable, the Hierarch, according to his prudent discretion, grants permission or approval by expressing his name; Otherwise, the reasons for the rejection will be communicated to the author of the work.

Can. 665 . § 1 . Pastors and church leaders must be careful not to display, sell or distribute in their churches icons or images of sacred art other than German or books that are not in line with Christian religion or morals. § 2 . Likewise, it is the duty of parish priests and rectors of churches, as well as directors of Catholic schools, to ensure that shows of any kind are chosen under their sponsorship with a sense of Christian discretion. § 3 . Let all Christian believers be careful, lest by buying, selling, reading, or sharing with others the things mentioned in § 1 they cause spiritual harm to themselves or others.

Can. 666 . § 1 . The intellectual work of the author is under the protection of the law either to the extent that it manifests his personality or to the extent that it is a source of economic rights. § 2 . Under the protection of the law are the texts of the laws and official acts of any ecclesiastical authority and their authentic collections; Therefore, it is not permitted to publish them again unless permission has been obtained from the same or a higher authority and the conditions prescribed by the same have been observed. § 3 . In accordance with the particular law of each independent Church, more specific regulations on this matter will be carried out, observing the provisions of civil law on copyright. TITLE XVI OF DIVINE WORSHIP AND ESPECIALLY THE SACRAMENTS

Can. 667 . Through the sacraments that the Church is obliged to administer, so that under a visible sign it communicates the mysteries of Christ, our Lord Jesus Christ sanctifies men by the power of the Holy Spirit, so that they become worshipers of the truth of God the Father in a unique way, and grafts them into Himself and into the Church, His Body; Therefore, all Christian faithful, and especially sacred ministers, must diligently observe the precepts of the Church, religiously celebrating and receiving the same sacraments.

Can. 668 . § 1 . Divine worship, if it is exercised in the name of the Church by persons legitimately designated for this purpose and by acts approved by ecclesiastical authority, is said to be public; otherwise private. § 2 . The competent authority for the organization of public divine worship is that which in Can. 657 , signs Can. 199 , § 1 ; no one else may add, remove or change anything to the bylaws by this authority.

Can. 669 . Since the sacraments are the same for the entire Church and belong to the divine deposit, it is only up to the supreme authority of the Church to approve or define what is required for their validity.

Can. 670 . § 1 . The Catholic faithful may, for just cause, be present at the divine worship of other Christians and participate in it, subject to the observances that have been established by the eparchial bishop or by a higher authority, taking into account the degree of communion with the Catholic Church. § 2 . If non-Catholic Christians lack places where they can celebrate divine worship with dignity, the eparchial Bishop may grant the use of a Catholic building, cemetery or church, in accordance with the particular law of his own Church.

Can. 671 . § 1 . Catholic ministers legally administer the sacraments only to the Catholic faithful, who also legally receive them only from Catholic ministers. § 2 . However, if necessity demands it or true spiritual usefulness suggests it, and provided that the danger of error or indifference is avoided, it is permitted for Catholic Christians, for whom it is physically or morally impossible to approach a Catholic minister, to receive the sacraments of penance, the Eucharist and the anointing of the sick from non-Catholic ministers, in whose Churches such sacraments validly exist. § 3 . Likewise, Catholic ministers licitly administer the sacraments of penance, the Eucharist and the anointing of the sick to the faithful of the Eastern Churches, who do not have full communion with the Catholic Church, if they request it of their own free will and are duly deposited; which also applies to the faithful of other Churches who, according to the judgment of the Apostolic See, are, with respect to the sacraments, in the same situation as the aforementioned Eastern Churches. § 4 . However, if there is danger of death, or there is another serious need that presses the judgment of the eparchial bishop or the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or the Council of Hierarchs, Catholic ministers legally minister the same sacraments to other Christians who do not have full communion with the Catholic Church, who cannot approach the minister of their own ecclesial community and request it of their own will, provided that they manifest a faith in the same sacraments consistent with the faith of the Church Catholic. and are disposed of properly. § 5 . For the cases mentioned in §§ 2, 3 and 4, the rules of particular law should not be applied except after consulting with the competent authority of at least the local Church or non-Catholic ecclesial community in question.

Can. 672 . § 1 . The sacraments of baptism, chrismation, holy miracles and holy ordination cannot be repeated. § 2 . However, if there are reasonable doubts as to whether they have actually been validly concluded or not, the doubt will be permanently resolved after serious investigation.
Can. 673 . The celebration of the sacraments, especially the Divine Liturgy, as an activity of the Church, to the extent possible, is carried out with the active participation of the faithful.

Can. 674 . § 1 . In the celebration of the sacraments, the contents of the liturgical books must be scrupulously observed. § 2 . The minister will celebrate the sacraments according to the liturgical prescriptions of his own independent Church, unless the law establishes otherwise or he has obtained a special faculty from the Apostolic See. CHAPTER I OF BAPTISM

Can. 675 . § 1 . In baptism the person is freed from sin through a bath of natural water with the invocation of the name of God the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, he is regenerated to a new life, he is clothed with Christ and he is incorporated into the Church, which is his Body. § 2 . Only by actually receiving baptism does a person become capable of receiving the other sacraments.
Can. 676 . In case of urgent need, baptism may be administered by placing only those things that are necessary for its validity.

Can. 677 . § 1 . Baptism is ordinarily administered by a priest; but his ministry is subject to the right of a certain parish priest to baptize another priest with permission from the same parish priest or the local Hierarch, which is legitimately presumed to be a serious cause. § 2 . But in case of necessity, baptism can be administered by a deacon or, in his absence or impediment, by another clergyman, a member of an institute of consecrated life, or any other faithful Christian; but to the father or mother, if another who knows how to baptize is not available.

Can. 678 . § 1 . No one may administer baptism in foreign territory without proper permission; but this permission cannot be denied by the pastor of an independent church other than the priest of the independent church to whom the baptism is to be attributed. § 2 . In places where there are not a few Christian faithful who do not have a parish priest of the independent church to which they are registered, the eparchial bishop will designate, if possible, a priest from the same church, who will administer the baptism.
Can. 679 . Any and only person who has not yet been baptized is capable of receiving baptism.
Can. 680 . An aborted fetus, if alive and possible, must be baptized.

Can. 681 . § 1 . For a child to be licitly baptized it is necessary: ​​1. There must be a firm hope that he will be raised in the Catholic faith of Erclesia § 5 ; 2° the parents, at least one of them, or the one who legally holds the same position, must give their consent. § 2 . The exposed and found child, unless it is certain that the child's baptism is confirmed, will be baptized. § 3 . Those deprived of the use of reason from infancy must be baptized when they are children. § 4 . A child, whether of Catholic parents or even of non-Catholic parents, who is involved in the crisis of life, so that it is prudently anticipated that he will die before reaching the use of reason, is licitly baptized. § 5 . A non-Catholic Christian child is legally baptized if the parents, or at least one of them, or whoever legally holds the same position, request it and if it is physically or morally impossible for them to access their own minister.

Can. 682 . § 1 . In order to be baptized after infancy, it is required that you express your willingness to receive baptism, that you be sufficiently instructed in the truths of the faith and tested in the Christian life; May he also be admonished to repent of his sins. § 2 . A child who is in danger of death can be baptized if he has knowledge of the main truths of the faith and has in some way expressed his intention to receive baptism.
Can. 683 . Baptism must be celebrated according to the liturgical prescriptions of the independent Church, to which the baptized person must belong according to the rule of law.

Can. 684 . § 1 . According to the oldest custom of the Churches, the person who is going to be baptized must have at least one godfather. § 2 . It is the godfather's responsibility to baptize someone who has been baptized as a child, to assist in Christian initiation or to present the child for baptism, and to ensure that the baptized person leads a Christian life appropriate to baptism and faithfully fulfills the obligations associated with it.

Can. 685 . § 1 . In order for someone to function effectively as a godfather, it is required that: 1° they be initiated into the three sacraments of baptism, chrismation of the holy miracle and the Eucharist; 2° the company § 3 belongs to the Catholic Church; 3° has the intention of carrying out that task; 4° he must be baptized by himself, or by his parents or guardians, or, if they are absent, by the minister; 5° you must not be a father, mother or spouse to baptize; 6° It will not be punished with the penalty of excommunication, even a minor one, suspension, deposition or deprivation of the right to exercise the function of sponsor. § 2 . For a person to lawfully act as a godfather, he or she must also be of the age required by particular law and lead a life of faith appropriate to the performance of the position. § 3 . It is permitted, for just cause, to admit as a sponsor a member of the Christian faith of a non-Catholic Eastern Church, but always together with a Catholic sponsor.

Can. 686 . § 1 . Parents have the obligation to have the child baptized as soon as possible according to legitimate custom. § 2 . The priest must ensure that the parents of the child to be baptized, as well as those who are to assume the role of godparent, are duly instructed in the meaning of this sacrament and the obligations related to it, and are properly prepared for the celebration of the sacrament.

Can. 687 . § 1 . Baptism must be celebrated outside of cases of necessity in the parish church, in accordance with legitimate customs. § 2 . In private homes, however, baptism may be administered according to the rules of particular law or with the permission of the local Hierarch.
Can. 688 . The person who administers the baptism will ensure that, if the godfather is not present, there is at least one witness by whom the celebration of the baptism can be proven.

Can. 689 . § 1 . The parish priest of the place where the baptism is celebrated must diligently and without delay record the names of the baptized, with mention of the minister, parents and godparents, and, if present, witnesses, of the place and day of the baptism, in the book of the baptized, indicating at the same time the place of birth and the independent church to which the baptized are registered. § 2 . If it is a child born to a single mother, the mother's name must be inserted, if it is publicly established about her maternity, or the mother requests it voluntarily in writing or in the presence of two witnesses; Likewise, the name of the father must be inserted if his paternity is proven by some public document or by his own statement made before the priest and two witnesses. In other cases, the name of the baptized person is recorded, without indicating the name of the father or parents. § 3 . In the case of an adopted child, the names of the adopters and, at least if this is done in the civil act of the region, the names of the natural parents are recorded in accordance with §§ 1 and 2 particular law.
Can. 690 . If the baptism was not administered by or in the presence of the pastor, the minister must report the matter to the local pastor.

Can. 691 . To prove baptism, if no one is harmed, the statement of a witness is sufficient, with the exception of the eldest, or the statement of the baptized person based on indubitable evidence, especially if he himself received baptism as a child. CHAPTER II OF THE CHRISMATION OF SAINT MYRI

Can. 692 . It is necessary that those who have been baptized be chrismated with the holy miracle, so that, sealed with the seal of the gift of the Holy Spirit, they become more suitable witnesses and co-builders of the Kingdom of Christ.
Can. 693 . Holy myrrh, which is composed of olive oil or other plants and spices, is prepared only by the Bishop, except by special law, according to which this power is reserved to the Patriarch.
Can. 694 . According to the tradition of the Eastern Churches, the holy miracle chrismation is administered by a priest together with baptism or separately.

Can. 695 . § 1 . The chrismation of the holy miracle must be administered together with baptism, except in cases of real necessity, in which, however, care must be taken that it is administered as soon as possible. § 2 . If the celebration of the chrismation of the holy miracle is not performed at the same time as the baptism, the minister is obliged to inform the parish priest of the place where the baptism was administered.

Can. 696 . § 1 . All priests of the Eastern Churches can validly administer the chrismation of the holy miracle, either together with baptism or separately, to all the faithful of each independent Church, including the Latin Church. § 2 . The faithful of the Eastern Churches can receive the chrismation of the holy miracle even from the priests of the Latin Church, according to the faculties with which they are endowed. § 3 . Every priest lawfully administers the chrismation of the holy miracle to the faithful of his own church; But with respect to the faithful of other autonomous Churches, this is done lawfully, if they are his own subjects, those he legitimately baptizes with another title, or those who are in danger of death, and always respecting the agreements concluded on this matter between the autonomous Churches.

Can. 697 . The sacramental initiation into the mystery of salvation is completed with the reception of the Divine Eucharist, and therefore the Divine Eucharist after the baptism and chrism of the holy wonder of Christ is ministered as soon as possible according to the norm of the particular law of the Church proper in its own right. CHAPTER III OF THE DIVINE EUCHARIST

Can. 698 . In the Divine Liturgy, through the ministry of the priest in the person of Christ, acting on the offering of the Church, what He Himself did at the Last Supper, the Lord Jesus, who gave His Body on the Cross to be offered for us and His Blood to be shed for us, is perpetuated by the power of the Holy Spirit, establishing a true and mystical sacrifice, by which that bloody sacrifice of the Cross is commemorated with thanksgiving, activated and shared by the Church both by offering and by communion to signify and complete the unity of the people of God in the building of His Body, which is the Church

Can. 699 . § 1 . Only bishops and priests have the power to celebrate the Divine Liturgy. § 2 Deacons, together with bishops and priests, participate more closely in the celebration of the Divine Liturgy through their own ministry, as provided in the liturgical books. § 3 . The other Christian faithful, by the power of baptism and chrismation of the holy miracle, gather in the celebration of the Divine Liturgy, in the manner specified in the liturgical books or in particular law, they actively participate in the Sacrifice of Christ, and even more fully, if they participate in the Body and Blood of the Lord in the same Sacrifice.

Can. 700 . § 1 . Regarding the way of celebrating the Divine Liturgy, whether individually or in concelebration, the pastoral needs of the faithful must be taken into account above all. § 2 . However, if possible, priests should celebrate the Divine Liturgy together with the Presiding Bishop or with another priest, since in this way the unity of the priesthood and sacrifice is manifested; However, the right of each priest to celebrate the Divine Liturgy individually remains intact, but not at the same time that the concelebration takes place in the same church.

Can. 701 . A concelebration between bishops and priests of different independent Churches, for the just cause, especially of promoting charity and manifesting the union between churches, may be carried out with the permission of the eparchial bishop in all the following provisions of the liturgical books of the first celebrant, eliminating both liturgical syncretisms and preferably preserving the liturgical vestments and insignia of his own independent Church.
Can. 702 . Catholic priests were prohibited from concelebrating the Divine Liturgy together with non-Catholic priests or ministers.

Can. 703 . § 1 . A foreign priest is not admitted to celebrate the Divine Liturgy, unless he presents to the rector of the church a letter of recommendation from his Hierarch, or in some other way the rector himself is sufficiently convinced of his integrity. § 2 . It is appropriate that the eparchial bishop establish more defined rules in this matter, which must be observed by all priests, even those who are exempt in some way.

Can. 704 . The Divine Liturgy can be laudably celebrated on all days except those that are excluded according to the provisions of the liturgical books of the autonomous Church in which the priest is registered.

Can. 705 . § 1 . A Catholic priest can celebrate the Divine Liturgy at the altar of any Catholic Church. § 2 . For a priest to celebrate the Divine Liturgy in a non-Catholic church, he needs the permission of the local Hierarch.

Can. 706 . In the Divine Liturgy the sacred gifts offered are simply wheat bread freshly made in such a way that there is no danger of corruption, and natural wine from the seed of the vine that has not been corrupted.

Can. 707 . § 1 . Regarding the preparation of the Eucharistic bread, the prayers that priests must offer before the celebration of the Divine Liturgy, the observance of the Eucharistic fast, the liturgical vestments, the time and place of the celebration and so on, must be exactly determined by the particular law of each autonomous Church. § 2 . To the surprise of the faithful, it is permitted to use the liturgical vestments and bread of another independent Church, if the liturgical vestments and bread of the independent Church are not available.

Can. 708 . Local hierarchs and parish priests should ensure that the Christian faithful are instructed with all diligence about the obligation to receive the Divine Eucharist in danger of death, as well as in the hours established by the most praiseworthy tradition or by the particular law of the independent Church itself, especially at the time of Easter, when Christ the Lord delivered the Eucharistic mysteries.

Can. 709 . § 1 . The divine Eucharist is distributed by the priest or, by the particular right of his own independent Church, also carried by the deacon. § 2 . It is up to the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or the Council of Hierarchs to establish appropriate norms according to which the other Christian faithful can also distribute the Divine Eucharist.

Can. 710 . Regarding the participation of children in the Divine Eucharist after the baptism and chrismation of the Holy Spirit, the provisions of the liturgical books of the Church itself are observed with due precautions.

Can. 711 . Whoever is aware of a serious sin should not celebrate the Divine Liturgy or receive the Divine Eucharist, unless there is a serious cause and there is no opportunity to receive the sacrament of penance. in which case it should provoke an act of perfect contrition, which includes the intention of approaching this sacrament as soon as possible.
Can. 712 . Those who are publicly unworthy of receiving the Divine Eucharist must be banished.

Can. 713 . § 1 . The Divine Eucharist must be distributed during the celebration of the Divine Liturgy, unless a just cause suggests otherwise. § 2 . Regarding preparation for participation in the Divine Eucharist during the year of fasting, the prayers and other works of the Christian faithful must faithfully observe the norms of the independent Church to which they are attached, not only within the territorial limits of the Church itself, but, as far as possible, throughout the world.

Can. 714 . § 1 . In churches, where divine worship is public and at least a few times a month the Divine Liturgy is celebrated, the Divine Eucharist is preserved especially for the sick, the prescriptions of the liturgical books of the independent Church itself being faithfully observed, and it is venerated with the greatest reverence by the faithful. § 2 . The custody of the Divine Eucharist is under the supervision and control of the local Hierarch.

Can. 715 . § 1 . Priests are permitted to receive the offerings that the faithful offer themselves according to the approved custom of the Church for the celebration of the Divine Liturgy for their own purposes. § 2 . It is also permitted, if legitimate custom so requires, to receive offerings for the Liturgy of the Presanctified and for the commemorations of the Divine Liturgy.

Can. 716 . It is strongly recommended that eparchial bishops, as far as possible, introduce a practice according to which only those offerings which the faithful offer voluntarily are accepted on the occasion of the Divine Liturgy; but individual priests gladly celebrate the Divine Liturgy even without any offering for the Christian faithful, especially those in need.

Can. 717 . Priests, if they receive offerings for the celebration of the Divine Liturgy from the faithful of another independent Church, have a heavy obligation to observe the norms of that Church regarding these offerings, unless the offerer agrees otherwise. CHAPTER IV OF THE SACRAMENT OF PENANCE

Can. 718 . In the sacrament of penance, the Christian faithful who, having committed sins after baptism, turn to God with their hearts guided by the Holy Spirit and, moved by the pain of their sins, enter into the purpose of a new life, through the ministry of the priest, done by confession and the acceptance of a worthy satisfaction, obtain God's forgiveness and at the same time are reconciled with the Church, which they have wounded by sinning; In this way this sacrament contributes as much as possible to the promotion of Christian life and provides for the reception of the Divine Eucharist.

Can. 719 . He who is aware of a serious sin must receive the sacrament of penance as soon as possible; but all Christian believers are strongly recommended to receive this sacrament frequently and especially during times of fasting and penance in their own independent Church.

Can. 720 . § 1 . Individual and complete confession and absolution constitute the only ordinary method by which a Christian, conscious of his grave sin, is reconciled with God and the Church; only physical or moral impossibility excuses such confession, in which case reconciliation can also be achieved by other means. § 2 . Absolution cannot be given to several penitents at the same time without prior individual and general confession, unless: 1° the danger of death is imminent and time is not sufficient for the priest or priests to administer the sacrament of penance to each penitent; 2° there is a serious need, that is, if, given the number of penitents, there are not enough priests available to administer to each penitent the sacrament of penance in an adequate time, so that, through no fault of their own, they are forced to miss sacramental grace or the reception of the Divine Eucharist for a long time; but the need is not considered sufficient, since confessors cannot be made available only by a large gathering of penitents, such as might be had at some great festival or pilgrimage. § 3 . It is up to the eparchial bishop to decide whether such a serious need exists, who, in consultation with the patriarchs and eparchial bishops of other independent churches exercising their authority in the same territory, can determine cases of such need, including according to the general provisions.

Can. 721 . § 1 . In order for a faithful Christian to enjoy the sacramental absolution given at the same time to several, it is required not only that he be duly disposed, but also that he at the same time propose to confess grave sins, which cannot be confessed at the present moment. § 2 . The Christian faithful, to the extent possible, must be instructed about these demands and, furthermore, even in case of danger of death, they must be exhorted to provoke the act of transgression.

Can. 722 . § 1 . The sacrament of penance is administered only by the priest. § 2 . All bishops throughout the world may administer the sacrament of penance by law, unless, with respect to legality, the eparchial bishop expressly refuses in a special case. § 3 . But for priests to act effectively, it is also necessary that they be endowed with the capacity to administer the sacrament of penance, a power conferred upon them either by right or by a special contribution from the competent authority. § 4 . Priests who are endowed with the faculty to minister the sacrament of penance by force of office or by force of collation of the local Hierarch of the eparchy in which they are enrolled or in which they have their domicile, can validly administer the sacrament of penance to any Christian faithful throughout the world, unless the local Hierarch expressly refuses in a special case; They licitly use the same faculty, observing the norms issued by the eparchial bishop, as well as at least the presumed authorization of the rector of the church or, if it is the house of the institute of consecrated life, of the Superior.

Can. 723 . § 1 . By virtue of the office, each one is endowed with the capacity to administer the sacrament of penance in his own jurisdiction, in addition to the local Hierarch, also the parish priest and another who is in the place of the parish priest. § 2 . Every superior of a religious institution or of a society of common life is endowed with the power to administer the sacrament of penance, like the religious of pontifical or patriarchal right, if he is a priest, to the members of his own institution, as well as to those who spend long hours and nights in his home.

Can. 724 . § 1 . Only the local Hierarch has the right to confer the power to administer the sacrament of penance to any of the faithful through a special contribution to the priests. § 2 . The superior of the institute of consecrated life, provided he is endowed with the executive power of government, can confer the faculty of what in Can. 723, § 2, according to the norm of the typical or the statutes, to any priest.

Can. 725 . Any priest may validly and legally absolve any penitent who is in danger of death of any sin, even if another priest endowed with the ability to administer the sacrament of penance is present.

Can. 726 . § 1 . The power to administer the sacrament of penance should not be revoked except for serious cause. § 2 . Having revoked the power to administer the sacrament of penance conferred by the Hierarch, with respect to which in Can. 722 , § 4 , the priest loses the same in all parts of the world; but if it is revoked by another competent authority, it loses control only of the revoker. § 3 . Aside from revocation, the ability to administer the sacrament of penance, as described in Can. 722, § 4, ceases upon loss of office, eparchy registration, or domicile.

Can. 727 . In some cases, to provide for the salvation of souls, it may be advisable to limit the ability to absolve sins and reserve it to a specific authority; However, this can only be done with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or the Council of Hierarchs or the Apostolic See.

Can. 728 . § 1 . It is up to the Apostolic See to absolve the following sins: 1. direct violation of the sacramental seal; 2nd absolution of accomplices in sin against chastity. § 2 . But it is up to the eparchial bishop to absolve the sin of causing an abortion after its effect.

Can. 729 . Any reservation of absolution of sin lacks all force: 1° if the confession is made by a sick person who cannot leave home, or by the spouse in order to celebrate a marriage; 2° if the ability to absolve the confessor cannot be requested from the competent authority without serious inconvenience for the penitent or without risk of violating the sacramental seal; 3° outside the borders of the territory in which the reserving authority exercises power.
Can. 730 . The absolution of an accomplice in a sin against chastity is not valid except in danger of death.

Can. 731 . He who confesses to having falsely reported to the ecclesiastical authority an innocent confessor for the crime of soliciting the sin against chastity will not be acquitted, unless he has previously formally retracted the false report and is willing to repair the damages, if any.

Can. 732 . § 1 . Depending on the quality, severity and number of the sins, taking into account the condition of the penitent as well as his disposition to conversion, the confessor must bring the appropriate medicine to the illness, imposing appropriate works of penance. § 2 . The priest must remember that he was appointed by God to be a minister of divine justice and mercy; as if a spiritual father also provided adequate advice so that one could progress in one's vocation to holiness.

Can. 733 . § 1 . The sacramental seal is inviolable; Therefore, the confessor must be careful not to betray the penitent in any way, with words, signs or in any other way and for any reason. § 2 . The interpreter, if there is one, is also bound by the obligation of secrecy, as are all others to whom knowledge of sins has come to them in some way from confession.

Can. 734 . § 1 . All confessors are prohibited from using the knowledge acquired in confession to the detriment of the penitent, even if all risk of revelation is excluded. § 2 . He who is placed in authority must in no way use the knowledge he has of sins, except in confession, at any time for external government. § 3 . Directors of educational institutes do not normally administer the sacrament of penance to their students.

Can. 735 . § 1 . Everyone to whom the power of the ministry requires the care of souls has the grave obligation to ensure that the sacrament of penance is ministered to the Christian faithful entrusted to him, that they request it at the appropriate time, and that they are given the same opportunity to confess individually on the days and hours set for their convenience. § 2 . Every priest endowed with the ability to administer the sacrament of penance, and every other priest in danger of death, must administer this sacrament with urgent urgency.

Can. 736 . § 1 . The proper place to celebrate the sacrament of penance is the church, except for particular law. § 2 . Due to illness or other just cause, this sacrament can also be celebrated outside its proper place. CHAPTER V ANOINTING OF THE SICK

Can. 737 . § 1 . Through the sacramental anointing of the sick by the priest with a prayer, the faithful afflicted with a serious illness and with a broken heart perceive grace, through which they are strengthened with the hope of an eternal reward and freed from their sins, and are prepared to improve their lives and are helped to overcome their illnesses and to suffer with patience. § 2 . In churches where it is customary for the sacrament of anointing of the sick to be administered by several priests at the same time, care should be taken that, as far as possible, this custom is observed.

Can. 738 . Let the faithful gladly receive the anointing of the sick, when they are seriously ill; but that the shepherds of souls and the relatives of the sick ensure that the sick are relieved at the appropriate time by this sacrament.

Can. 739 . § 1 . The anointing of the sick is powerfully ministered by all and only by the priests. § 2 . Administering the anointing of the sick corresponds to the parish priest, the parochial vicar and all other priests in their environment, whose care is entrusted to them by duty; At least with his presumed permission, any priest can lawfully administer this sacrament, and indeed must do so in case of need.

Can. 740 . Seriously ill Christians, who have lost their senses or the use of reason, are presumed to want this sacrament administered to them under danger of death or even at the discretion of the priest at another time.

Can. 741 . The oil to be used in the sacrament of the anointing of the sick must be blessed, and in fact, unless the particular law of the independent Church itself dictates otherwise, by the same priest who administers the sacrament.

Can. 742 . The anointings are carried out precisely in the words, order and manner prescribed in the liturgical books; In case of need, however, an anointing with the appropriate formula is sufficient. CHAPTER VI OF THE SACRED ORDINANCE

Can. 743 . Through the sacramental ordination carried out by the Bishop, by the working force of the Holy Spirit, sacred ministers are appointed, who add to the role and power entrusted by Christ the Lord to his apostles and enjoy in varying degrees of announcing the Gospel, feeding and sanctifying the people of God. Art. I OF THE MINISTER OF THE HOLY ORDINANCE
Can. 744 . Only the bishop validly administers sacred ordination through the laying on of hands and prayer prescribed by the Church.

Can. 745 . Episcopal ordination is reserved to the norms of the law of the Roman Pontiff, Patriarch or Metropolitan, so that no bishop can ordain anyone as a bishop, unless previously agreed by legitimate mandate.

Can. 746 . § 1 . A bishop will be ordained by the three bishops, except in cases of extreme necessity. § 2 . The second and third bishops, if bishops from the same autonomous church as the first ordaining bishop cannot be present, may be from another autonomous church.
Can. 747 . A candidate for the diaconate or priesthood must be ordained by his own eparchial bishop or by another bishop with a legitimate letter of dismissal.

Can. 748 . § 1 . The proper eparchial bishop, with regard to the sacred ordination of one who is assigned to an eparchy, is the bishop of the eparchy in which the candidate is domiciled, or of the eparchy to whose service the candidate has declared in writing that he wishes to dedicate himself; As for the sacred ordination of the one who is already enrolled in any eparchy, he is the bishop of that eparchy. § 2 . An eparchial bishop cannot ordain a candidate who is subject to him and who has been registered by another Church in its own right, except with the permission of the Apostolic See; but if it is a candidate who is registered in the Patriarchal Church and has a domicile or quasi-domicile within the territory of the same Church, the Patriarch can also grant this permission.

Can. 749 . In a foreign eparchy, a bishop is prohibited from celebrating sacred ordination without the permission of the eparchial bishop, unless the particular law of the patriarchal church, as far as the patriarch is concerned, has established otherwise.

Can. 750 . § 1 . The dismissal letters can be delivered to the signatures cann. 472, 537 et 560, § 1: 1° The eparchial bishop himself; 2° The administrator of the patriarchal Church and the administrator of the eparchy by agreement of the college of eparchial counselors. § 2 . The Administrator of the Patriarchal Church must not grant letters of dismissal to those who have been rejected by the Patriarch, nor the Administrator of the Eparchy to those who have been rejected by the Eparchial Bishop.
Can. 751 . Letters of dismissal should not be granted unless all the evidence required by law has been previously obtained.

Can. 752 . Letters of removal may be sent by the corresponding eparchial bishop to any independent bishop of the same church, but not to the bishop of another church who is to be ordained, except with the permission of those mentioned in Can. 748, § 2.

Can. 753 . Release letters may be limited or revoked by the grantor himself or his successor in title, but once granted they are not extinguished by the termination of the grantor's rights. Art. II ON THE MATTER OF THE SACRED ORDINANCE
Can. 754 . Only a baptized man can validly receive holy ordination.

Can. 755 . The eparchial bishop and the major superior can only, for very serious reasons, even hidden ones, prevent the ascension to the presbytery of a deacon subject to him and destined for the presbytery, except by legal recourse to the norm of the law.
Can. 756 . It is not permissible to force anyone, in any way and for any reason, to receive holy orders, nor to prevent him from receiving them according to an appropriate rule of law.

Can. 757 . Anyone who refuses to take a higher sacred order cannot be prevented from exercising the sacred order he has taken, unless he is detained due to canonical impediment, or there is a serious objection to the judgment of the eparchial bishop or major superior. 1° About the requirements of candidates for sacred ordination

Can. 758 . § 1 . In order for one to be licitly ordained, the following is required: 1° to receive the chrismation of the holy miracle; 2° the morality and the physical and psychological qualities inherent to the adoption of sacred orders; 3° the age prescribed by law; 4th due knowledge; 5° the reception of lower orders according to the norm of the particular law of the Church itself by right; 6° observance of the deadlines prescribed by the particular law. § 2 . Additionally, the candidate is required to be unhindered as per the Can. 762 standard. § 3 . Regarding the admission of marriages to sacred orders, the particular law of the independent Church itself or the special norms established by the Apostolic See will be observed.

Can. 759 . § 1 . The age prescribed for the diaconate is the twenty-third year completed, and for the presbytery the twenty-fourth year completed, according to the particular law of the independent Church which requires a higher age. § 2 . The dispensation beyond one year of the age prescribed by common law is reserved to the Patriarch, if it is a candidate who has a domicile or quasi-domicile within the territory of the Patriarchal Church; unlike the Apostolic See.

Can. 760 . § 1 . A deacon can be ordained only after successfully completing the fourth year of the course of philosophical-theological studies, unless the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or the Council of Hierarchs decides otherwise. § 2 . But if it is a candidate who is not destined for the priesthood, he may be ordained a deacon only after successfully completing the third year of studies, as mentioned in Can. 354; but if by chance he is admitted to the priesthood in the future, he must first timely complete his theological studies.

Can. 761 . The candidate for the order of deacon or priest, to be legitimately ordained, must deliver to the corresponding eparchial bishop or major superior a declaration signed by his own hand, in which he testifies that he will voluntarily and freely assume the sacred order and the obligations inherent to the same order and that he will permanently dedicate himself to the ecclesiastical ministry, at the same time requesting to be admitted to assume the sacred order. 2° Obstacles to receiving or exercising sacred orders

Can. 762 . § 1 . The following are prevented from receiving sacred orders: 1° who suffers from some form of madness or other mental weakness, for which experts judge him incapable of adequately carrying out the ministry; 2° who has committed the crime of apostasy, heresy or schism; 3° who has attempted to contract a marriage, even a civil one, whether he himself is prevented from celebrating the marriage by a marriage bond or by a sacred order or by a public vow of perpetual chastity, or is united to a woman by a valid marriage or is in dispute with the same vow; 4° who committed a voluntary murder or procured an abortion after the effect and everyone cooperated positively; 5° who seriously and maliciously mutilated himself or another, or attempted to take his own life; 6° the one who placed the act of order in the order of episcopacy or presbyterate reserved by the constitutions, or lacking them, or prohibited its exercise by some canonical penalty; 7° the one who exercises a position or administration prohibited to clerics, for which he must give an account, until he has been released by depositing the position and administration and the accounts rendered; 8° a neophyte, unless he has been sufficiently proven by the judgment of the Hierarch. § 2 . Acts, of which luggage, mentioned in § 1, nos. 2 - 6 can rise, they do not give birth, unless there are serious and external sins committed after baptism.

Can. 763 . The following are prevented from practicing sacred orders: 1° he who, being affected by the impediment from taking sacred orders, took them illegitimately; 2° that has committed infractions or acts, of which in Can. 762, § 1, nos. 2 - 6; 3° those who suffer from insanity or other mental illness, of which in Can. 762 , § 1 , n. 1, remains affected until the Hierarch has permitted the sacred exercise of the same order to an expert.

Can. 764 . No impediments to receiving or exercising sacred orders can be established by particular law; but the custom that introduces a new impediment or contradicts an impediment established by common law is condemned.
Can. 765 . Ignorance of obstacles does not exempt them from them.

Can. 766 . The impediments are multiplied by their different causes, but not by the repetition of the same cause, unless it is an impediment due to voluntary murder or an induced abortion followed by an effect.

Can. 767 . § 1 . An eparchial bishop or a hierarch of the institute of consecrated life may exempt his subjects from impediments to receiving or exercising sacred orders, with the following exceptions: 1° if the act on which the impediment is based has been brought before a judicial forum; 2nd of the obstacles mentioned in Can. 762 , § 1 , nos. 2 - 4. § 2 . The dispensation from these obstacles is reserved to the Patriarch with respect to candidates or clerics who have a domicile or quasi-domicile within the limits of the territory of the Church over which he presides; unlike the Apostolic See. § 3 . The same power of dispensation belongs to every confessor in the most urgent occult cases, in which the competent authority cannot be resorted to and there is imminent danger of serious harm or infamy, but for the moment, so that penitents can legally exercise the sacred orders they have already received, with the firm burden of going to the same authority as soon as possible.

Can. 768 . § 1 . In the prayers to obtain dispensation all impediments must be indicated; The general dispensation, however, also applies to impediments established in good faith, with the exception of those provided for in Can. 762 , § 1 , n. 4, or others taken to judicial jurisdiction, but not due to bad faith reluctance. § 2 . If these are interferences due to voluntary manslaughter or induced abortion, for the validity of the dispensation the number of crimes must also be expressed. § 3 . The general dispensation of impediments to receiving sacred orders is valid for all orders. Art. 3 OF THEM, WHICH MUST BE PRESENTED TO THE HOLY ORDINANCE

Can. 769 . § 1 . The authority that admits the candidate to holy ordination must obtain: 1° the declaration, mentioned in Can. 761, as well as the testimony of the last sacred ordination or, if it is the first sacred ordination, also the testimony of the baptism and chrism of the holy miracle; 2° if the candidate is married, the marriage certificate and the written consent of the wife; 3rd certificate of completed studies; 4° testimonial letters from the rector of the seminary or the Higher Institute of Consecrated Life or the priest to whom the candidate was recommended outside the seminary, regarding the candidate's good conduct; 5th testimonial letters, mentioned in Can. 771, § 3; 6° testimonial letters, if you so decide, from other eparchial bishops or superiors of institutes of consecrated life where the candidate has resided for some time, about the candidate's qualities and his freedom from any canonical impediment. § 2 . These documents are kept in the archives of the same authority.

Can. 770 . The ordaining bishop with a legitimate letter of dismissal, by which it is affirmed that the candidate is suitable to receive sacred orders, may assent to this certification, but is not obliged; But if according to his conscience he considers that the candidate is not suitable, he should not ordain him.

Can. 771 . § 1 . The names of the candidates to be promoted to holy orders will be publicly known in the parish church of each candidate in accordance with the law of particularity. § 2 . All Christian faithful have the obligation to reveal any obstacles, if known, to the eparchial bishop or priest before sacred ordination. § 3 . The eparchial bishop instructs the priest who makes the publication, and also other priests, if it seems appropriate to do so, to carefully investigate the life and character of the candidates for trustworthy persons, and to send testimonial letters regarding this investigation and publication to the eparchial tribunal. § 4 . The eparchial bishop must not fail to carry out other investigations, even private ones, if he directs them.

Can. 772 . Every candidate to be promoted to sacred ordination is released for spiritual retreats in the manner determined by particular law. Art. IV. OF THE TIME, PLACE, REGISTRATION AND WITNESS OF THE SACRED ORDINATION
Can. 773 . The sacred ordinances are celebrated in the church with the largest number of Christians on Sunday or festival, unless a just cause suggests otherwise.

Can. 774 . § 1 . After the sacred ordination has been celebrated, the names of the ordained and the ordaining Bishop, the place and the day of the sacred ordination will be recorded in a special book that is kept in the archives of the eparchial tribunal. § 2 . To each of those ordained, the ordaining bishop will deliver an authentic certificate of reception of the sacred ordination; who, if they have been ordained by a bishop with a letter of dismissal, present it to their own eparchial bishop or major superior for the registration of the sacred ordination in a special book that is kept in the archive.

Can. 775 . The eparchial bishop or major superior sends notification of the sacred ordination of each deacon to the parish priest with whom the baptism of the ordained person was recorded. CHAPTER VII MARRIAGE

Can. 776 . § 1 . The marriage alliance founded by the Creator and instructed by his laws, by which a man and a woman, by irrevocable personal consent, establish with each other a partnership for life, is directed by its natural character to the good of the spouses and to the generation and education of children. § 2 . Since the institution of Christ, valid marriage between the baptized is a sacrament by which spouses are united by God in the image of the unfailing union of Christ with the Church, and are, so to speak, consecrated and strengthened by sacramental grace. § 3 . The essential properties of marriage are unity and indissolubility, which in marriage between the baptized obtain special firmness due to the sacrament.
Can. 777 . From marriage, equal rights and obligations arise between spouses regarding those things that belong to the partnership of marital life.
Can. 778 . Anyone who is not prohibited by law can marry.
Can. 779 . Marriage enjoys the favor of the law; so the validity of the marriage must be in doubt until proven otherwise.

Can. 780 . § 1 . The marriage of Catholics, even if only one of the parties is Catholic, is governed not only by divine law, but also by canon law, except for the jurisdiction of civil authority over the purely civil effects of marriage. § 2 . Marriage between a Catholic party and a baptized non-Catholic party is also governed by divine law: 1° by the proper law of the Church or the ecclesial Community to which the non-Catholic party belongs, if this Community has its own matrimonial law; 2° by the law to which the non-Catholic party is obliged, if the ecclesial community to which it belongs lacks its own marriage law.

Can. 781 . If at any time the Church must decide on the validity of the marriage of baptized non-Catholics: 1° with respect to the law by which the parties were governed at the time of the celebration of the marriage Can. 780, § 2; 2° Regarding the form of celebration of marriage, the Church recognizes any form prescribed or admitted by law, to which the parties were subject at the time of the celebration of the marriage, provided that the consent is expressed publicly and, if at least one of the parties is a member of the Christian faith of a non-Catholic Eastern Church, the marriage has been celebrated with a sacred rite.

Can. 782 . § 1 . Betrothal, which according to the oldest tradition of the Eastern Churches is laudably preceded by marriage, is governed by the particular law of its own independent Church. § 2 . From the marriage promise there is no action that allows the celebration of the marriage; It is given, however, for the repair of damages, if any. Art. I OF PASTORAL CARE AND THOSE THAT SHOULD BE CARRIED OUT BEFORE THE CELEBRATION OF THE MARRIAGE

Can. 783 . § 1 . Pastors of souls are obliged to ensure that the faithful are prepared for the married state: 1° through preaching and catechesis adapted to young people and adults, through which the faithful are instructed about the meaning of Christian marriage, about the obligations of spouses towards each other, as well as about the right and primary obligation that parents have to take care of the physical, religious, moral, social and cultural education of their children for their strength; 2. The instruction of personal godparents for marriage, by which the spouses prepare for their new status. § 2 . Catholic spouses are strongly encouraged to receive the Divine Eucharist in marriage. § 3 . But once the marriage is celebrated, pastors of souls must provide help to the spouses, so that, faithfully keeping and protecting the marital alliance, they lead a holier and fuller life as a family.

Can. 784 . By the particular right of each autonomous Church, in consultation with the Eparchial Bishops of other autonomous Churches exercising their authority in the same territory, rules are established regarding the examination of godparents and other means of investigation, especially with regard to baptism and free status, which must be carried out before marriage, and if they are carefully observed, the marriage can proceed to the celebration.

Can. 785 . § 1 . Pastors of souls are obliged to protect, for the needs of the places and times, with appropriate measures, all the dangers derived from invalid and illicitly celebrated marriages; Therefore, before celebrating the marriage, it must be established that nothing hinders its valid and legal celebration. § 2 . In danger of death, if no other evidence can be obtained, it is sufficient, unless proven otherwise, for the godparents to affirm, if the case permits, even under oath, that they have been baptized and that they have no impediment.
Can. 786 . All Christian faithful have the obligation to reveal obstacles, if they know of any, to the priest or the local Hierarch before the celebration of the marriage.
Can. 787 . The parish priest who has carried out the investigations must immediately inform the parish priest whose marriage is to be blessed by means of an authentic document.
Can. 788 . If, after thorough investigations, any doubt remains as to the existence of the obstacle, the parish priest must refer the matter to the local Hierarch.

Can. 789 . Although a marriage can be validly celebrated in other cases, the priest, in addition to other cases determined by law, cannot bless without the permission of the local Hierarch: 1° the marriage of vagabonds; 2° marriage that cannot be recognized or contracted according to the rules of civil law; 3° the marriage of someone who is obliged by natural obligations to a third party, or to children born from a previous union with that person; 4° the marriage of a child to the family of a minor without the knowledge or against the will of the parents; 5° the marriage of someone who, by ecclesiastical opinion, is prohibited from entering into a new marriage, unless certain conditions are met; 6° the marriage of someone who has publicly renounced the Catholic faith, even if he or she has not joined the non-Catholic Church or ecclesial community; In this case, however, the local leader should not grant permission unless he or she has observed Can. 814 and made appropriate references. Art. 2. INTERVENTIONS AND SOLUTIONS IN GENERAL

Can. 790 . § 1 . The dissolution of the obstacle leaves the person incapable of validly celebrating the marriage. § 2 . The impediment, even if it is only one of the parties, invalidates the marriage.
Can. 791 . It is considered a public impediment, which can be proven in the foreign market; otherwise it is hidden.

Can. 792 . By the particular right of the independent Church, remedies should not be established except for the most serious reasons, after consultation with the eparchial bishops of the other interested independent Churches, and in consultation with the Apostolic See; but no lower authority can establish new impediments and remedies.
Can. 793 . A custom that introduces a new obstacle or is contrary to existing ones is rejected.

Can. 794 . § 1 . The local hierarch may prohibit marriage to the Christian faithful subject to him wherever they reside, as well as to the other Christian faithful of his own independent Church who actually live within the limits of the territory of the eparchy, in a special case, but only for a time, for a serious and lasting cause. § 2 . If it is a local Hierarch, who exercises his authority within the territory of the Patriarchal Church, the Patriarch may add a dissipating clause to such a prohibition; in other cases, however, only the Apostolic See.

Can. 795 . § 1 . The local hierarch can dispense the Christian faithful subject to him wherever they reside, as well as other Christian faithful registered in their own Church and who actually live within the limits of the territory of the eparchy, with the exception of the following impediments of ecclesiastical law: 1° of sacred orders; 2nd of the public vow of perpetual chastity issued in a religious institute, unless they are congregations of eparchial right; 3rd of marriage. § 2 . The dispensation of these impediments is reserved to the Apostolic See; The patriarch, however, can dispense with impediments to marriage and the public vow of perpetual chastity issued in congregations of any legal status. § 3 . Dispensation from the impediment of consanguinity is never granted in the direct line or in the second degree of the collateral line.

Can. 796 . § 1 . In case of urgent danger of death, the local Hierarch may exempt the Christian faithful subject to him wherever they reside, as well as other Christian faithful who actually live within the limits of the territory of the eparchy, from the form of celebration of marriage prescribed by law and from each and every impediment of ecclesiastical law, public or hidden, except the impediment of the order of the sacred priesthood. § 2 . Under the same circumstances and only in cases where even the local Hierarch cannot be approached, the parish priest, another priest endowed with the ability to bless marriages and the Catholic priest have the same power of administration, as discussed in Can. 832, § 2; but the confessor has the same power, if it is a hidden impediment, for the internal forum, whether inside or outside the act of sacramental confession. § 3 . A local hierarch is considered unreachable if this can only be done in any way other than by letter or personal access.

Can. 797 . § 1 . If an impediment is discovered, everything being ready for the celebration of the marriage, and the marriage cannot be celebrated without probable danger of serious harm, until the dispensation has been obtained from the competent authority, the power to dispense with all impediments, except those mentioned in Can. 795, § 1, nos. 1 and 2, have a local Hierarch and, provided the case is hidden, all those mentioned in Can. 796 , § 2 , subject to the conditions prescribed therein. § 2 . This power is also valid to validate a marriage, if the same risk is pending and there is no time to go to the competent authority.

Can. 798 . The priests, mentioned in cann. 796, § 2 and 797, § 1, of the dispensation or validation granted for the external forum must immediately inform the local Hierarch and it will be recorded in the marriage book.

Can. 799 . Unless the written record of the Apostolic See or within the limits of its jurisdiction of the local Patriarch or Hierarch establishes otherwise, a dispensation in the non-sacramental internal forum granted for a secret impediment will be recorded in the secret archive of the eparchial court and no further dispensation for the external forum is necessary, even if the secret impediment later turns out to be public. Art. 3 ON IMPLEMENTS IN SPECIES

Can. 800 . § 1 . A man before turning sixteen years of age and a woman before turning fourteen years of age cannot validly celebrate marriage. § 2 . It is an integral part of the right of the independent Church to establish a year prior to the legal celebration of marriage.

Can. 801 . § 1 . The antecedent and perpetual impotence of sexual relations, whether of the man or the woman, absolute or relative, dissolves marriage by its very nature. § 2 . If the obstacle of impotence is doubtful, whether due to doubt of law or fact, the marriage should not be prevented, nor is there any doubt to be declared. § 3 . Sterility does not prevent or dissolve marriage.

Can. 802 . § 1 . One who is bound by the bond of a previous marriage attempts to contract an invalid marriage. § 2 . Even if a previous marriage is invalid or dissolved for any reason, it is not lawful to celebrate another marriage until the nullity or dissolution of the previous one is legally and definitively established.

Can. 803 . § 1 . Marriage cannot be validly celebrated with unbaptized persons. § 2 . If, at the time of the marriage, one of the parties was generally considered to have been baptized, or his baptism was doubtful, the validity of the marriage shall be presumed according to the rule of Can. 779, until it is proven with certainty that one of the parties was baptized and the other was not. § 3 . Regarding processing conditions, Can. 814 will apply.
Can. 804 . He attempts an invalid marriage, which is established in the sacred order.
Can. 805 . He attempts to marry an invalid who has taken a public vow of perpetual chastity in a religious institution.

Can. 806 . When a person has been kidnapped or at least held with a view to celebrating marriage with him, the marriage cannot be validly celebrated, unless he is subsequently separated from the kidnapper or retainer and settles in a safe and free place and chooses to marry of his own free will.

Can. 807 . § 1 . He who, in order to celebrate a marriage with a certain person, causes the death of his spouse or his own spouse, attempts that marriage invalidly. § 2 . They also try to marry each other as invalids, those who have caused the physical or moral death of the spouses.

Can. 808 . § 1 . In a direct line of consanguinity, the marriage is void between all ascendants and descendants. § 2 . The collateral line is invalid up to and including the fourth degree. § 3 . Marriage is never permitted if there is doubt as to whether the parties are consanguineous in some degree of direct line or in the second degree of collateral line. § 4 . Inbreeding does not multiply.
Can. 809 . § 1 . Affinity dissolves the marriage in any degree of the direct line and in the second degree of the collateral line. § 2 . The affinity barrier does not multiply.

Can. 810 . § 1 . An obstacle to public honesty arises: 1° from invalid marriage after life together is established; 2° of notorious or public coexistence; 3° of the establishment of the common life of those who, having been bound by the form of marriage celebration prescribed by law, have attempted to contract marriage in the presence of a civil official or a non-Catholic minister. § 2 . This obstacle dissolves direct line first degree marriage between the man and the woman's blood relatives and also between the woman and the man's blood relatives.

Can. 811 . § 1 . From baptism a spiritual kinship arises between the godfather and the baptized person and their parents, which dissolves the marriage. § 2 . If baptism is repeated under the condition, spiritual kinship does not arise, unless the same godfather is used again.
Can. 812 . Those who are legally related by adoption in a direct line or in the second degree of a collateral line cannot validly celebrate marriage with each other. Art. IV OF MIXED MARRIAGES
Can. 813 . Marriage between two baptized people, one of whom is Catholic and the other non-Catholic, is prohibited without prior authorization from the competent authority.

Can. 814 . The local Hierarch may grant permission for just cause; but it should not grant it unless the following conditions are met: 1. The Catholic party declares that it is willing to eliminate the dangers of failing in the faith, and makes a sincere promise that it will do everything in its power to see that all children are baptized and educated in the Catholic Church; 2° that these promises are made by the Catholic party, the other party must be informed in a timely manner so that it can be established that it has true knowledge of the promise and obligation of the Catholic party; 3° both parties must be educated about the essential purposes and properties of marriage, excluding either spouse.

Can. 815 . By the particular right of each independent Church, the way in which these declarations and promises, which are always required, will be made will be determined, and the way in which they will be established in the external forum will be determined, and the non-Catholic party will be informed.

Can. 816 . Local hierarchs and other shepherds of souls must ensure that Catholic couples and children born of a mixed marriage do not lack spiritual help to fulfill their obligations of conscience, and help spouses to foster the unity of marital and family life. Art. V. CONSENT TO MARRIAGE

Can. 817 . § 1 . Marital consent is an act of will by which a man and a woman give themselves to each other in an irrevocable agreement and agree to form a marriage. § 2 . Marital consent cannot be supplemented by any human power.

Can. 818 . The following are incapable of celebrating marriage: 1° those who lack sufficient use of reason; 2° that they suffer from a serious lack of discretion regarding the mutual transfer and acceptance of essential rights and obligations of marriage; 3° who, for psychological reasons, cannot assume the essential obligations of marriage.

Can. 819 . For there to be marital consent, it is necessary that those entering into marriage at least not ignore that marriage is a permanent partnership between a man and a woman designed to produce children through some sexual cooperation.

Can. 820 . § 1 . A mistake in person invalidates the marriage. § 2 . The error in the quality of a person, even if it gives rise to the marriage, does not dissolve the marriage, unless this quality is directly and mainly intentional.

Can. 821 . He who solemnizes a deceived marriage to obtain an agreement regarding some quality of the other party, which by its very nature can seriously disturb the partnership of conjugal life, solemnizes it invalidly.
Can. 822 . The error relating to the unity or indissolubility or sacramental dignity of marriage, as long as it does not determine the will, does not vitiate marital consent.
Can. 823 . Knowledge or belief of the nullity of the marriage does not necessarily exclude marital consent.

Can. 824 . § 1 . The internal consent of the mind is presumed to conform to the words or signs used in the celebration of marriage. § 2 . But if one or both parties by a positive fact effectively exclude the marriage itself or some essential element or essential property of the marriage, the marriage is invalidly celebrated.
Can. 825 . A marriage is invalid if it is entered into by force or by serious external fear, even without consultation, from which the person is forced to choose marriage to free himself.
Can. 826 . A marriage cannot be celebrated under a valid condition.

Can. 827 . Even if the marriage has been invalidly celebrated due to the impediment or lack of the form of celebration of the marriage prescribed by law, the consent given is presumed to subsist until its revocation is established. Art. VI OF THE FORM OF THE CELEBRATION OF MARRIAGE

Can. 828 . § 1 . Only those marriages are valid that are celebrated with a sacred rite before the local Hierarch or local priest or presbyter, who has been conferred the ability to bless the marriage by either party, and with at least two witnesses as provided in the following canons, and with the exception of the exceptions mentioned in cann. 832 y 834, § 2. § 2 . Here the rite is considered sacred due to the priest's own intervention assisting and blessing.

Can. 829 . § 1 . The local hierarch and the local parish priest, having taken possession of the canonical office, while carrying out their legitimate office, validly bless the marriage in all places within the limits of their territory, whether the spouses are subjects or, provided that at least one of the contracting parties is enrolled in their own independent Church, non-subjects. § 2 . The hierarch and the pastor, by personal force of office, only validly bless the marriage of those of whom at least one is subject to them, within the limits of their jurisdiction. § 3 . The patriarch is endowed by right with the ability to bless marriages himself throughout the world, provided that at least a portion of the church he presides is registered.

Can. 830 . § 1 . The local hierarch and the local parish priest, in the fulfillment of their legitimate duties, may grant priests of any autonomous Church, including the Latin Church, the ability to bless a specific marriage within the limits of their territory. § 2 . However, only the local Hierarch can confer the general ability to bless marriages. § 3 . The granting of the power to bless marriages, to be valid, must be expressly given to certain priests; Furthermore, if it is a general power, it must be given in writing.

Can. 831 . § 1 . The hierarch of the place or the parish priest of the place legally blesses the marriage: 1° after having established the domicile or quasi-domicile or the monthly residence or, if it is a vagabond, the actual residence of either spouse in the place of marriage; 2nd considering, if these conditions are lacking, the authorization of the Hierarch or the parish priest of the domicile or quasi-domicile of any of the parties, unless a just cause exempts it; 3° also in the exclusive place of another independent Church, unless the Hierarch, who exercises his power in this place, expressly refuses. § 2 . The marriage will be celebrated in the presence of the groom's priest, unless a particular law provides otherwise or a just cause exempts it.

Can. 832 . § 1 . If a competent priest according to the law cannot be obtained or addressed without serious inconvenience, those who intend to celebrate that true marriage can validly and lawfully celebrate it only in the presence of witnesses: 1° in danger of death; 2° out of danger of death, provided that it is prudently anticipated that his condition will last a month. § 2 . In both cases, if another priest is available, he should, if possible, be called to bless the marriage preserving the validity of the marriage in the presence only of witnesses; In the same cases a non-Catholic priest can also be called. § 3 . If the marriage was celebrated in the presence only of witnesses, the spouses should not neglect to receive the marriage blessing from the priest as soon as possible.

Can. 833 . § 1 . The local hierarch may grant any Catholic priest the power to bless the marriage of the faithful of a non-Catholic Eastern Church, who cannot go to a priest of their own Church without serious inconvenience, if they request it of their own free will and provided that nothing prevents a valid or licit celebration of the marriage. § 2 . The Catholic priest, if possible, before blessing the marriage, informs the competent authority of those Christians about this matter.

Can. 834 . § 1 . The form of marriage celebration prescribed by law must be observed, if at least one of the parties celebrating the marriage has been baptized in the Catholic Church or received into it. § 2 . However, if a Catholic party attached to an independent Eastern Church celebrates a marriage with a party belonging to the non-Catholic Eastern Church, the form of marriage celebration prescribed by law shall be observed solely for reasons of legality; but for its validity the blessing of the priest is required, having preserved others from the law.
Can. 835 . The dispensation from the form of marriage celebration prescribed by law is reserved for the Apostolic See or the Patriarch, who will only grant it for very serious reasons.
Can. 836 . Except in cases of necessity, the provisions of the liturgical books and legitimate customs are observed in the celebration of marriage.

Can. 837 . § 1 . To validly celebrate a marriage it is necessary that the parties be present together and mutually express their consent to the marriage. § 2 . A marriage cannot be validly celebrated by a proxy, unless the particular law of the independent Church itself establishes otherwise, in which case it is also necessary to provide for the conditions under which such a marriage can be celebrated.

Can. 838 . § 1 . The marriage must be celebrated in the parish church or with the permission of the local Hierarch or the local priest in another sacred place; but in other places it cannot be celebrated except with the permission of the local Hierarch. § 2 . At the time of the celebration of the marriage, the norms established by the particular law of the independent Church will be observed.

Can. 839 . Before or after the canonical celebration, another religious celebration of the same marriage is prohibited to guarantee or renew marital consent; Likewise, a religious celebration in which both a Catholic priest and a non-Catholic minister seek the consent of the parties is prohibited.

Can. 840 . § 1 . Permission for a secret marriage may be granted by the local Hierarch for a serious and urgent reason and entails a serious obligation to keep the secret on the part of the local Hierarch, the parish priest, the priest with the capacity to bless the intended marriage, the witnesses and the other spouse, the other not consenting to the publication. § 2 . The obligation to preserve the secret ceases on the part of the local Hierarch, if the observance of the secret threatens serious scandal or serious damage to the sanctity of marriage. § 3 . A marriage celebrated in secret will only be registered in a special book that is kept in the secret archive of the eparchial court, unless there is a very serious cause.

Can. 841 . § 1 . When a marriage has been celebrated, the parish priest of the place of celebration or the one who exercises his functions, even if neither of the two has blessed the marriage, enters as soon as possible in the marriage book the names of the spouses, the benefactor priest and the witnesses, the place and day of the marriage celebrated, the dispensation, if any, of the form of celebration of the marriage or of impediments and of its author together with the impediment and its degree, the power to bless the marriage conferred and according to other methods prescribed by his own eparchial bishop. § 2 . In addition, the local priest will record in the baptism book that the couple celebrated their marriage that day in his parish; but if the spouse has been baptized elsewhere, the parish priest of the place will send the marriage certificate himself or by the eparchial tribunal to the parish priest with whom the baptism of the spouses was registered, and will not rest until he has received notification of the registration of the marriage in the baptism book. § 3 . If the marriage has been celebrated according to the Can. 832 norm, the priest, if he has blessed it, otherwise the witnesses and the spouses must ensure that the celebration of the marriage is recorded in the prescribed books as soon as possible.

Can. 842 . If the marriage is validated in a foreign forum or is declared null or legally dissolved except by death, the parish priest of the place of celebration of the marriage must be informed, so that the registration can be made in the marriage and baptism books. Art. 7 OF THE VALIDATION OF MARRIAGE 1. Of simple validation

Can. 843 . § 1 . To validate a marriage invalid due to impediment, it is required that the impediment cease or be dispensed with and that consent be renewed by at least one of the parties aware of the impediment. § 2 . This renewal is necessary for the validity of the validation, even if both parties initially gave their consent and did not subsequently withdraw it.
Can. 844 . The renewal of consent must be a new act of the will to marry, which the renewer knows or believes to be invalid from the beginning.

Can. 845 . § 1 . If there is public impediment, the consent of both parties must be renewed in the form of marriage celebration prescribed by law. § 2 . If the impediment is hidden, it is sufficient for the contract to be renewed privately and confidentially; by the party that knows of the obstacle, provided that the other party continues in the intended agreement, or by both parties, if the obstacle is known to both parties.

Can. 846 . § 1 . A marriage invalid due to lack of consent is validated if the party who did not consent already consents, provided that the consent of the other party continues. § 2 . If lack of consent cannot be proven, it will be sufficient for the party who did not give consent to give consent privately and confidentially. § 3 . If the lack of consent can be proven, it is necessary that the consent be renewed in the form of marriage celebration prescribed by law.
Can. 847 . A marriage invalid due to lack of the form of marriage celebration prescribed by law, to be valid, must be celebrated again in this form. 2° Healing at the root

Can. 848 . § 1 . The cure of an invalid marriage is basically the validation of the same consent without renewal granted by the competent authority, entailing the dispensation of the impediment, if present, and of the form of celebration of the marriage prescribed by law, if it has not been observed, as well as the regression of the canonical effects to the past. § 2 .
