Validation occurs from the moment of granting grace; But the setback is understood to have occurred at the time of the celebration of the marriage, unless expressly provided otherwise in the grant.

Can. 849 . § 1 . Healing a marriage from the root can be validly granted even without the knowledge of one or both parties. § 2 . Root healing should not be granted except for serious reasons and unless it is probable that the parties wish to continue in the partnership of conjugal life.

Can. 850 . § 1 . An invalid marriage can be healed, as long as the consent of both parties persists. § 2 . A marriage invalid due to an impediment of divine law cannot be validly healed until the impediment has ceased.

Can. 851 . § 1 . If the consent of one of the parties is missing, the marriage cannot be validly healed from the roots, whether the consent was lacking from the beginning, or whether it was given from the beginning and then revoked. § 2 . But if consent was indeed lacking from the beginning, but was given later, the remedy may be granted from the moment the consent was given.

Can. 852 . The patriarch and the eparchial bishop may grant root healing in each case, if the validity of the marriage is impeded by the lack of the form of marriage celebration prescribed by law or by some obstacle that they can dispense with, and in cases prescribed by law, if the conditions mentioned in Can. 814 are met; In other cases, and if it is an interference with divine right, which has already ceased, root healing can be granted only by the Apostolic See. Art. 8 CONCLUSION OF THE SEPARATION 1° Of the dissolution of the bond
Can. 853 . The marriage bond, once consummated through sacramental marriage, cannot be dissolved by any human power and by any other cause than death.

Can. 854 . § 1 . A marriage celebrated between two unbaptized persons is dissolved by the Pauline privilege in favor of the faith of the party who received the baptism, as of right, if a new marriage is celebrated by the same party, provided that the unbaptized party departs. § 2 . The unbaptized party is considered to leave if he does not want to live peacefully with the baptized party without offending the Creator, unless the Creator, after receiving baptism, has given him a just reason to leave.

Can. 855 . § 1 . For the baptized person to validly celebrate the new marriage, it is necessary to ask the unbaptized person if: 1° he also wishes to receive baptism; 2° at least he wants to live in peace with the baptized without offending the Creator. § 2 . This intervention must be carried out after baptism; but the local Hierarch may, for a serious reason, allow burial to take place before baptism, or may even dispense with burial before or after baptism, if it becomes clear, at least by a summary and extrajudicial procedure, that it cannot be done or that it would be useless.

Can. 856 . § 1 . The interpellation is regularly carried out under the authority of the local Hierarch of the convert, who must grant the other spouse a period of time to respond, if requested, with the warning that his silence after that period has elapsed is unnecessarily considered a negative response. § 2 . An interpellation made in private, converted by the party itself, is valid, even lawful, if the previously prescribed form cannot be observed. § 3 . In both cases, the intervention must be legally established and its outcome in the external market.

Can. 857 . The baptized person has the right to celebrate a new marriage with the Catholic, if: 1° the other party responded negatively to the question; 2° the intervention was lawfully omitted; 3. The unbaptized person, whether interrupted or not, previously persisting in a peaceful coexistence, later withdrew without just cause; in which case, however, intervention according to the cann. 855 y 856 standard must be preceded.

Can. 858 . The local hierarch, however, for serious reasons, may grant that the baptized person, using the Pauline privilege, may celebrate a marriage with a non-Catholic party, whether baptized or not, also observing the provisions of the canons on mixed marriages.

Can. 859 . § 1 . The unbaptized man who has several unbaptized wives at the same time, having received baptism in the Catholic Church, if he finds it difficult to continue with the first of them, can retain one of them, dismissing the others; The same applies to a baptized woman who has several unbaptized husbands at the same time. § 2 . In this case, the marriage must be celebrated in the manner prescribed by law, also observing other legal observances. § 3 . The local hierarchy, taking into account the moral, social and economic condition of the place and the town, will ensure that the needs of those dismissed are sufficiently covered according to the norms of justice, charity and equity.

Can. 860 . The unbaptized person who, having received baptism in the Catholic Church, cannot reestablish cohabitation with his or her unbaptized spouse due to captivity or persecution, may celebrate another marriage, even if the other party has received baptism in the meantime, with the signature Can. 853.
Can. 861 . In matters of doubt, the privilege of faith enjoys the favor of the law.

Can. 862 . An unconsummated marriage can be dissolved for just cause by the Roman Pontiff at the request of either party, even if the other is not willing. 2° About the separation of the remaining link

Can. 863 . § 1 . It is strongly recommended that the spouse, out of concern for the love and good of the family, should not refuse to forgive the part of adultery and should not break the partnership of marital life; but if he has not expressly or tacitly forgiven the guilt thereof, he has the right to dissolve the partnership of conjugal life, unless he has consented to the adultery or given the same cause, or he himself has also committed adultery. § 2 . There is tacit forgiveness if the innocent spouse, after being informed of the adultery, voluntarily converses with the other spouse with conjugal affection; It is presumed, however, if for six months he maintained the partnership of conjugal life and did not address the matter to the ecclesiastical or civil authority. § 3 . If the innocent spouse voluntarily dissolves the conjugal life partnership, he must, within six months, refer the cause of separation to the competent authority, which will evaluate all the circumstances observed, whether the innocent spouse can be led to forgive the fault and not prolong the separation.

Can. 864 . § 1 . If one of the spouses makes the common life of the spouse or children dangerous or too difficult, he gives the other a legitimate reason to leave by decree of the local Hierarch and also by his own authority, if danger is pending. § 2 . By the particular right of the independent Church, other causes may be established due to the character of the town and the circumstances of the place. § 3 . In all cases, the conjugal life partnership must be reestablished upon completion of the cause of separation, unless otherwise determined by the competent authority.
Can. 865 . After the separation of spouses, it is always necessary to take care of the proper maintenance and education of children.

Can. 866 . The innocent spouse may laudably readmit the other spouse into the partnership of conjugal life, in which case he or she waives the right of separation. CHAPTER VIII OF THE SACRAMENTALS, OF SACRED PLACES AND TIMES, OF THE CULT OF THE SAINTS, OF VOWS AND OATHS Art. I OF THE SACRAMENTALS

Can. 867 . § 1 . By means of sacramentals, which are sacred signs, by which spiritual effects are signified in some imitation of the sacraments, and which are obtained from the acquisition of the Church, men are disposed to receive the main effect of the sacraments, and the various circumstances of life are sanctified. § 2 . Regarding the sacraments, the norms of the particular law of the full Church are observed. Art. II ON THE SACRED PLACES
Can. 868 . Sacred places intended for divine worship can only be erected with the authorization of the eparchial bishop, unless expressly provided otherwise in common law. 1° Of the churches
Can. 869 . A church is a house dedicated exclusively to divine worship through consecration or blessing.
Can. 870 . No building intended for a church shall be constructed without the express written consent of the eparchial bishop, unless otherwise provided by common law.

Can. 871 . § 1 . Cathedral churches and, if possible, parish churches, monasteries and churches attached to religious houses will be dedicated by consecration. § 2 . Consecration is reserved for the eparchial bishop, who may confer on another bishop the power to consecrate the church; A document is written about the consecration or complete blessing of the church that will be kept in the archives of the eparchial court.

Can. 872 . § 1 . You should stay away from churches, anything that is not in tune with the sanctity of the place. § 2 . Let all those to whom it corresponds take care that the cleanliness that befits the house of God is preserved in the churches, and that security means are used to protect sacred and precious things.

Can. 873 . § 1 . If a church can no longer be used in any way for divine worship and there is no possibility of rebuilding it, the eparchial bishop may reduce it to profane and unfilthy use. § 2 . If other serious reasons suggest that a certain church should no longer be used for divine worship, the eparchial bishop may reduce it to a profane, not sordid, use, with the advice of the presbyteral council, with the consent of those who legitimately claim rights over it, and provided that the salvation of souls is not prejudiced. 2° Of cemeteries and ecclesiastical funerals

Can. 874 . § 1 . It is the right of the Catholic Church to own its own cemeteries. § 2 . The Church's own cemeteries should be preserved, whenever possible, or at least spaces in civil cemeteries designated for the faithful dead to be blessed one by one; but if they cannot be obtained, the tomb will be blessed on the occasion of the burial. § 3 . The deceased were not to be buried in churches, contrary to custom, except those who were patriarchs, bishops or exarchs. § 4 . Parishes, monasteries and other religious institutions may have their own cemeteries.

Can. 875 . At ecclesiastical funerals, through which the Church obtains spiritual help for the deceased, honors their bodies and at the same time brings the consolation of living hope, all the faithful and catechumens of the deceased must attend, unless they are deprived of them by right.

Can. 876 . § 1 . Ecclesiastical funerals may be granted to non-Catholic baptized persons at the discretion of the local Hierarch, unless it is clear that their wishes are contrary, and provided that a suitable minister cannot be arranged. § 2 . Children whom their parents intended to baptize, and others who in some way appeared to be connected with the Church, but died before receiving baptism, may also receive ecclesiastical funerals at the discretion of the local Hierarch. § 3 . Those who have chosen to cremate their own corpse, unless it is clear that they have done so for reasons contrary to Christian life, should be granted an ecclesiastical funeral celebrated in such a way that it is not hidden that the Church prefers the burial of bodies to cremation and scandal is avoided.

Can. 877 . Sinners must be deprived of ecclesiastical funerals, unless before their death they have given some signs of penitence, to which the same cannot be granted without public scandal for the Christian faithful.

Can. 878 . § 1 . When celebrating ecclesiastical funerals, all reception of people is avoided. § 2 . It is strongly recommended Can. 1013 that eparchial bishops, as far as possible, introduce the practice according to which on the occasion of ecclesiastical funerals only those offerings are received that the faithful offer voluntarily.
Can. 879 . Once the burial has been completed, the registration in the book of the deceased must be made in accordance with the rules of the particular law. Art. 3 OF THE DAYS OF FESTIVAL AND PENANCE

Can. 880 . § 1 . Establishing, transferring or suppressing the days of festivals and penance common to all the Eastern Churches is only the firm authority of the supreme Church § 3 . § 2 . It is also the authority to establish, transfer or suppress the days of feasts and penances of individual Churches in their own right, which has the particular right to establish those Churches, with due consideration, however, of the other independent Churches and of the firm Can. 40 , § 1 . § 3 . The days of obligation common to all the Eastern Churches, except Sunday, are the days of the Nativity of Our Lord Jesus Christ, the Epiphany, the Ascension, the Dormition of the Holy Mother of God Mary and the days of Saints Peter and Paul, except by particular law of the independent Church approved by the Apostolic See, by which certain days of obligation are suppressed or transferred to Sunday.

Can. 881 . § 1 . The Christian faithful are obliged to participate in the Divine Liturgy on Sundays and holidays, or to celebrate divine praises according to the prescribed or legitimate custom of their own independent Church. § 2 . So that the Christian faithful can fulfill this obligation more easily, it is decided that a good amount of time passes from the evening vigil until the end of Sunday or the feast of the commandment. § 3 . The Christian faithful are strongly recommended to receive the Divine Eucharist more frequently or even daily on these days. § 4 . On these days, the Christian faithful must abstain from those works and activities that prevent the worship of God, the joy of the Lord's Day or the proper rest of mind and body.
Can. 882 . During the days of penance, the Christian faithful are obliged to observe fasting or abstinence in the manner established by the particular law of their own independent Church.

Can. 883 . § 1 . The Christian faithful outside the borders of the territory of their own independent Church can fully comply with the regulations in force in the place where they live, regarding the days of festivals and penances. § 2 . In families in which the spouses are enrolled in different independent churches, it is permissible to observe the provisions of one or another independent church regarding vacations and penance. Art. IV OF THE CULT OF SAINTS, ICONS OR SACRED IMAGES AND RELICS

Can. 884 . To promote the sanctification of the people of God, the Church commends the faithful to a special and filial veneration of the Most Holy Mary, ever Virgin, Mother of God, whom Christ named Mother of all men, and promotes the true and authentic worship of the other saints, by whose example the faithful are edified and sustained by her intercession.
Can. 885 . Only those servants of God who are classified among the Saints or Blessed by the authority of the Church may be venerated in public worship.

Can. 886 . The practice of presenting icons or sacred images for the veneration of the faithful in churches must remain firm in the form and order established by the particular law of the independent Church.

Can. 887 . § 1 . Sacred icons or valuable images, that is, prominent in antiquity or art, displayed in churches for the veneration of the faithful, cannot be transferred or alienated to another church without the written consent of the Hierarch who exercises his power over the same church, signature cann. 1034 - 1041. § 2 . Nor can sacred icons or valuable images be restored without the written consent of the Hierarch himself, who, before granting it, consults experts.

Can. 888 . § 1 . It is not allowed to sell sacred relics. § 2 . The relics, icons or monumental images that are honored in a given church with great veneration of the people cannot be validly alienated in any way or permanently transferred to another church, except with the consent of the Apostolic See or the Patriarch, who cannot give it except with the consent of the permanent Synod. § 3 . Regarding the restoration of these icons or images, Can. 887 , § 2 will be saved. Art. 5 votes and oaths

Can. 889 . § 1 . A vow, that is, a deliberate and free promise made to God about a better and possible good, must be fulfilled by virtue of religion. § 2 . All those who have adequate use of reason are eligible to make vows, unless the law prohibits it. § 3 . A vote made out of serious and unjust fear, or by deception, is null and void. § 4 . A vote is public if it is accepted in the name of the Church by a legitimate ecclesiastical Superior; otherwise it is private.
Can. 890 . A vow does not bind anyone by itself except the one who made it.

Can. 891 . A vow ceases due to the passage of time to terminate the inherent obligation, due to a substantial change in the matter promised, due to non-compliance with the condition on which the vow depends, or due to its final cause, dispensation or change.
Can. 892 . The person who has power over the matter of the vote may suspend the obligation to vote whenever compliance with the vote causes harm.

Can. 893 . § 1 . He can dispense private vows for just cause, provided that the dispensation does not prejudice the rights claimed by others: 1° every Hierarch, parish priest and local superior of the institute of consecrated life, who has the power of government, is subject to him; 2° the other Christian faithful of the local Hierarch of the Church, provided that they actually reside within the limits of the territory of the eparchy; as well as the local parish priest within the limits of the territory of his own parish; 3. Those who reside long and nightly in the house of the institute of consecrated life, the local Superior, who has the power of government, and its major Superior. § 2 . This dispensation can be granted under the same conditions, but only for the internal forum, by any confessor.
Can. 894 . Vows taken before religious profession are suspended as long as the voter remains in the monastery, order or congregation.

Can. 895 . The oath, that is, the invocation of the divine Name as a testimony to the truth, can only be taken before the Church in cases established by law; otherwise it produces no canonical effect. TITLE XVII OF BAPTIZED CATHOLICS INTO FULL COMMUNION WITH THE CATHOLIC CHURCH

Can. 896 . No burden greater than necessary should be imposed on those who have been baptized in non-Catholic Churches or Ecclesial Communities and who request full communion with the Catholic Church of their own free will, whether as individuals or groups.

Can. 897 . A faithful Christian of any non-Catholic Eastern Church must be received into the Catholic Church with the sole profession of the Catholic faith, subject to doctrinal and spiritual preparation for the situation of each individual.

Can. 898 . § 1 . In addition to the Roman Pontiff, a bishop of a non-Catholic Eastern Church may be received into the Catholic Church by a Patriarch with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or by a Metropolitan of an independent Metropolitan Church with the consent of the Council of Hierarchs. § 2 . The right to receive any other person into the Catholic Church rests with the local Hierarch or, if particular law so requires, even with the Patriarch. § 3 . The right to receive individual laypeople into the Catholic Church also applies to the pastor, unless prohibited by a particular law.

Can. 899 . A clergyman of a non-Catholic Eastern Church suitable for full communion with the Catholic Church may exercise his own sacred order according to the norms established by the competent authority; A bishop, however, cannot exercise the power of government without the consent of the Roman Pontiff, head of the College of Bishops.

Can. 900 . § 1 . Anyone who has not yet reached fourteen years of age will not be able to be received by their recalcitrant parents. § 2 . If serious inconveniences for the Church or for themselves are foreseen due to their reception, the reception is postponed, unless there is an imminent danger of death.

Can. 901 . If non-Catholics, who do not belong to any Eastern Church, are received into the Catholic Church, the norms indicated above must be observed through appropriate references, provided they are validly baptized. TITLE XVIII OF EUCEMENISM OR THE PROMOTION OF CHRISTIAN UNITY

Can. 902 . Since the concern of the Christian councils for the establishment of unity looks at the entire Church, all the faithful, especially the Pastors of the Church, must pray for the fullness of the unity of the Church desired by the Lord and work by skillfully participating in the ecumenical work raised by the grace of the Holy Spirit.

Can. 903 . It is up to the Eastern Catholic Churches to promote unity among all the Eastern Churches through prayer, the example of life, religious fidelity to the ancient traditions of the Eastern Churches, mutual and better knowledge, collaboration and fraternal appreciation of things and souls.

Can. 904 . § 1 . The initiatives of the ecumenical movement in each Church in its own right are diligently promoted by the special norms of the particular law that regulates the same movement by the Roman Apostolic See for the entire Church. § 2 . To this end, a commission of experts on ecumenical matters should be established in each independent Church, if the circumstances of the situation so suggest, in consultation with the patriarchs and eparchial bishops of other independent Churches exercising their authority in the same territory. § 3 . Likewise, he meets with the eparchial bishops, either for each eparchy or, if he considers it appropriate, for several eparchies, to promote the plan of the ecumenical movement; and in those eparchies that cannot have their own council, there is at least one faithful Christian appointed by the eparchial bishop with the special task of promoting this movement.

Can. 905 . In carrying out ecumenical work, especially through open and trusting dialogue and initiatives with other Christians in common, due caution must be observed to avoid the dangers of false irenicism, indifference and unbridled zeal.

Can. 906 . In order for the faithful to know more clearly what the Catholic Church and other Churches or ecclesial communities really teach and transmit, preachers of the word of God, those who control the media of social communication, and all those who dedicate their energies as teachers or administrators in Catholic schools, especially in institutions of higher learning, must work diligently.

Can. 907 . Administrators of schools, hospitals, and other similar Catholic institutions must ensure that other Christians who attend or live there can obtain spiritual help from their own ministers and receive the sacraments.

Can. 908 . It is to be expected that the Catholic faithful, observing the norms of communication in any sacred task in which they can cooperate with other Christians, will not pay separately, but jointly, such as works of charity and social justice, the defense of the dignity of the human person and their fundamental rights, the promotion of peace, days of commemoration of the country, national holidays. TITLE 19 ON PERSONS AND LEGAL ACTS CHAPTER 1 ON PERSONS Art. I ON NATURAL PERSONS

Can. 909 . § 1 The person who has reached eighteen years of age is older; a minor under this age. § 2 . A minor under seven years of age is called a child and is considered not to have self-control; but after seven years it is presumed that he has the use of reason. § 3 . Those who lack the habit of reason are considered out of control and assimilated to children.

Can. 910 . § 1 . The elderly person has the full exercise of their rights. § 2 . In the exercise of his rights, the minor is subject to the authority of his parents or guardians, with the exception of those in whom the minors are dispensed from their authority by divine or canon law; With regard to the establishment of guardians, the provisions of civil law shall be observed, unless otherwise provided by common law or the particular law of the independent Church, and the firm right of the eparchial bishop, if necessary, to appoint guardians himself.

Can. 911 . It is said that a person is a foreigner in an eparchy different from the one in which he or she has a domicile or quasi-domicile; but he is said to be a vagabond if he has no domicile or quasi-domicile anywhere.

Can. 912 . § 1 . Domicile is acquired by residence in the territory of a parish or, at least, an eparchy, which is related to the intention to remain there permanently, if there is no reason to do so, or which has been effectively extended to five full years. § 2 . Quasi-domicile is acquired by residence in the territory of a parish or at least an eparchy, which is related to the intention to remain there for at least three months, if nothing is achieved, or is effectively extended to the full three months.

Can. 913 . Members of religious institutes, as well as societies of common life, such as religious ones, acquire their domicile in the place where the house to which they are registered is located; quasi-domicile in a place where your stay lasts at least three months.
Can. 914 . The spouses have a common domicile or quasi-domicile; However, for just cause, each person can have their own domicile or quasi-domicile.

Can. 915 . § 1 . The minor necessarily retains the domicile and quasi-domicile of the person to whose authority he or she is subject; The person who has abandoned childhood can also acquire a quasi-domicile of his own, and when he is legally emancipated according to the rules of civil law, he can also acquire his own domicile. § 2 . Any person who has been legally placed under guardianship or guardianship for any reason other than minority has the domicile and quasi-domicile of the guardian or conservator.

Can. 916 . § 1 . And by domicile and quasi-domicile, each one corresponds to his own local Hierarch and parish priest of the independent Church to which he is registered, unless otherwise provided by common law. § 2 . The parish priest of the person who has no more than an eparchial domicile or quasi-domicile is the parish priest of the place where he actually resides. § 3 . More specifically, the local hierarch and pastor of the homeless person is the pastor and hierarch of the local church where the homeless person actually resides. § 4 . If there is a lack of parish priest for the faithful of an independent Church, the eparchial bishop will designate a pastor from another independent church who will take care of them as their own pastor, with the consent of the eparchial bishop to appoint a pastor. § 5 . In places where even an exarchy has not been established for the faithful of any independent church, the local Hierarch of another independent church, including the Latin church, must be considered the appropriate Hierarch of those Christian faithful. but if there are more, the person designated by the Apostolic See will be deemed to be the one, or, if they are faithful of a specific patriarchal Church, the Patriarch with the consent of the Apostolic See.
Can. 917 . The domicile and quasi-domicile are lost when leaving a place with the intention of not returning without saving cann. 913 y 915.

Can. 918 . Consanguinity is calculated by lines and degrees: 1° in a straight line there are as many degrees as there are people in the lineage; 2nd on the collateral line there are as many steps as there are people in each section of the block.

Can. 919 . § 1 . Affinity arises from a strong marriage and exists between each other's spouses and each other's relatives. § 2 . By what line and to what degree is a person related to one spouse, related to the other? Art. II OF LEGAL PERSONS

Can. 920 . In the Church, in addition to natural persons, there are also legal persons, whether groups of people or groups of things, that is, subject in canon law to rights and obligations that correspond to their nature.

Can. 921 . § 1 . Legal entities are established for the purpose of the mission of the Church, either by the provisions of the law itself or by a special concession given by decree of the competent ecclesiastical authority. § 2 . By law, independent churches, provinces, eparchies, exarchies, as well as other institutions are legal entities, with respect to which this is expressly established in common law. § 3 . The competent authority may not confer legal personality except to those associations of people or things that pursue a specific purpose that is truly beneficial and have considered, after all, means that are expected to be sufficient to achieve the desired goal.

Can. 922 . § 1 . Every legal entity established by special concession from the competent ecclesiastical authority must have its own statutes approved by the competent authority to constitute the same legal entity. § 2 . By firm common law in the statutes, for their approval it is necessary to provide more precisely the following: 1° on the specific object of the legal entity; 2° on the nature of the legal entity; 3° who controls the legal entity and how it should be exercised; 4° who will represent the legal entity in the ecclesiastical and civil jurisdiction; 5° who is competent to dispose of the assets of the legal entity and who is the executor in the event of extinction of the legal entity, division into several legal entities or union with other legal entities, always observing the will of the offerors as well as the claimed rights. § 3 . Before the statutes are approved, the legal entity cannot act validly.
Can. 923 . A university of people cannot be established as a legal entity unless it is made up of at least three natural persons.

Can. 924 . Regarding collegiate acts, unless otherwise expressly provided by law: 1° that has the force of law, which, in the presence of the majority of those who must be convened, has been agreed upon by the absolute majority of those present; but if the votes are equal, the president will break the tie with his vote; 2° However, if the rights sought by individuals are affected, the consent of each of them is required; 3rd around the elections Can. 956 will remain.

Can. 925 . If a single member of the legal entity survives and still does not cease to exist in accordance with the statutes, it is up to that member to exercise all the rights of the same legal entity.

Can. 926 . § 1 . Unless otherwise provided by law, the assets and rights of a legal entity, which lacks members, must be preserved, administered or exercised by the care of that authority, which, in the event of its extinction, has the right to decide on them; This authority must, in accordance with the law, ensure faithful compliance with the charges imposed on these assets, as well as ensure that the will of the founders or donors is scrupulously observed. § 2 . The registration of the members of this legal entity may be carried out by said authority, subject to the provisions of the law, and must be carried out according to the cases to which the immediate care of the same person is entitled; It will be kept if the remaining partners are legally incapable of making the subscription. § 3 . The appointment of the administrators of the university of things, if it cannot be done in accordance with the law, is delegated to the immediately higher authority; The burden of administration falls on the same authority in accordance with the § 1 rule, until a suitable administrator is appointed.

Can. 927 . § 1 . The legal entity is by nature perpetual; However, it expires if it is suppressed by the competent authority or if the fact has ceased to exist for a period of one hundred years. § 2 . A legal entity can only be suppressed for serious reasons after consulting the administrators themselves and observing what is prescribed in the statutes regarding the case of suppression.

Can. 928 . With the exception of cases expressed by common law: 1° The Patriarch is consulted by the Permanent Synod to suppress the legal entities established or approved by him; but with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, the Patriarch may nevertheless suppress a legal entity, with the exception of those that have been established or approved by the Apostolic See; 2° It is up to the eparchial bishop, in consultation with the eparchial counselors, to suppress the legal entities that he has erected, unless they have been approved by a higher authority; 3° in other cases, whoever establishes legal entities cannot validly delete them, unless they obtain the consent of a higher authority.

Can. 929 . When the territory of a legal entity is divided in such a way that either a part of it is joined to another legal entity or a separate legal entity is erected for the dismembered part, even the common property that was intended for the benefit of the entire territory, and the debts that were contracted for the entire territory, must be divided by the authority to whom the division corresponds, in good and equal terms, saving each and every one of the obligations and also saving the wills of the pious founders or donors, the rights persecuted and the statutes by which the legal entity is governed.

Can. 930 . When the legal entity is extinguished, its assets become those of the immediately superior legal entity, always excepting the wills of the founders or donors, the rights sought and established by which the extinguished legal entity was governed. CHAPTER II LEGAL ACTS

Can. 931 . § 1 . For the validity of a legal act, it is required that it be carried out by a capable and competent person and that he or she attend it, which essentially constitutes the act itself, as well as the formalities and requirements imposed by law for the validity of the act. § 2 . A legal act is presumed valid if its external elements are placed in accordance with the law.

Can. 932 . § 1 . A legal act imposed by force imposed on a person from the outside, which the person cannot resist, is considered null and void. § 2 . The legal act imposed by another force or by fear of a serious and unjust attack, or by fraud, is valid, unless otherwise provided by law; but it may be revoked by the judge by means of a ruling, either at the request of the injured party or his successors, or ex officio.

Can. 933 . A legal act placed through ignorance or error, which revolves around that which constitutes its substance, or which reverts to a condition without which it does not exist, is nobody; Otherwise it is valid, unless otherwise provided by law, but a legal act carried out through ignorance or error may give rise to the action of rescission according to the rule of law.

Can. 934 . § 1 . If it is established by law that to constitute a legal act the authority needs the consent or advice of a group of people, the group must be convened in accordance with the Can. 948 rule, unless otherwise provided by a particular law for cases established by the same law, in which it is only a matter of requesting advice; but for a legal act to be valid, it is required that the consent of the absolute majority of those present be obtained, or that the advice of all be requested, signature § 2, n. 3. § 2 . If it is established by law that to establish a legal act the authority needs the consent or advice of certain people, such as individuals: 1° if consent is required, the legal act of the authority is invalid if it does not seek the consent of those people or acts against their will or that of someone; 2° if advice is required, the legal act of the authority that does not consult the same people is void; 3. The authority, although it is not obliged to adhere to the same plan, even if there is an agreement, but without compelling reason that it must evaluate in its judgment, must not deviate from the same plan especially in agreement. § 3 . For those whose consent or advice is required, the authority requiring consent or advice must provide them with the necessary information and protect in all ways their free expression of mind. § 4 . All those whose consent or advice is required are obliged to express their opinion in good faith and to maintain secrecy, an obligation that may be imposed by the authorities.
Can. 935 . Whoever causes damage to others by illegitimate legal act or by any other act due to fraud or negligence, is obliged to repair the damage caused. TITLE XX OF OFFICIALS

Can. 936 . § 1 . In the Church, a duty is any task established by the Lord Himself or by a competent authority to be performed for a spiritual purpose. § 2 . The rights and obligations of each position are determined by the law by which the position is created or by decree of the competent authority. § 3 . The authority that has the duty to establish it is also to change it, delete it and establish its canonical disposition, unless otherwise expressly provided by law or established by the nature of the matter.

Can. 937 . § 1 . Whoever establishes a position must ensure that the necessary means are available for its execution and that fair remuneration is provided to those who carry out the position. § 2 . The way in which these provisions will be applied will be determined more precisely by the particular law of each independent Church, unless already provided for by common law in certain respects. CHAPTER I OF THE PROVISION OF CANONICAL OFFICES
Can. 938 . The office cannot be obtained without a valid canonical provision.

Can. 939 . The provision of the canonical office is carried out: 1° through a free contribution from the competent authority; 2° if the election has been preceded by its confirmation or, if the election does not need confirmation, by the acceptance of those elected; 3° if the claim has preceded, by its admission.

Can. 940 . § 1 . For a person to be promoted to a position, they must be qualified, that is, endowed with the qualities required by law. § 2 . When the provision lacks the required qualities, it will be void only if so provided by law; Otherwise it is valid, but may be rescinded by decision of the competent authority in equity.

Can. 941 . The canonical provision, for which the law does not establish any deadline, can never be postponed beyond six working months, counted from the receipt of notification of the vacancy of the office.
Can. 942 . No one may be entrusted with two or more jobs that cannot be adequately performed by the same person at the same time, unless there is a real need.

Can. 943 . § 1 A disposition of an office that is not vacated by law is void by law and is not validated by a subsequent vacancy of the office. § 2 . But if it is an office conferred by law for a certain period, the canonical disposition can be made within six months, before this period expires, and has effect from the date of the vacancy of the office. § 3 . A promise of any duty, by whom it is made, has no canonical effect.

Can. 944 . A vacant office may be conferred by law, which may be possessed by someone illegitimately, provided that it is declared in accordance with law that the possession is not canonical, and this declaration is stated in the letter of contribution.

Can. 945 . He who, replacing another negligent or incapacitated person, confers an office, does not thereby acquire any power over the person to whom it is conferred, but his legal status is the same as if the canonical provision had been issued in accordance with the ordinary rule of law.
Can. 946 . The provision of a charge made for fear of grave injustice, fraud, material error or fraud is itself null and void. Art. ME IN THE ELECTIONS

Can. 947 . § 1 . If any group has the right to be elected to a position, the election, unless otherwise provided by law, must never be delayed more than three business months from receipt of notification of the vacancy to be computed; When the period has expired unnecessarily, the competent authority, who has the right to confirm the election or the right to dispose successively, may freely dispose of the vacant position. § 2 . The competent authority may freely fill the vacancy even if the group has lost the right to elect otherwise.

Can. 948 . § 1 . Without prejudice to the particular right of the group, the president will call the electors at the place and time that suits them; If the summons must be personal, it will be valid if it is made at the place of domicile or quasi-domicile or at the place of residence. § 2 . If one of the candidates is neglected and therefore absent, the election is valid, but at his request the competent authority must annul the proven absence and absence even after confirmation, provided that, according to the rule of law, the appeal has been filed at least within three days of receipt of the notification of the election. § 3 . But if more than one-third of the electors are neglected, the election is by right null and void, unless all those excluded are actually present.

Can. 949 . § 1 . In a canonical call, the right to vote corresponds to those who are present at the place and on the day provided for in the call, excluding the valid right to vote by mail or by proxy, unless otherwise provided by law. § 2 . If any of the electors is present in the chamber where the election is being held, but cannot participate in the election for health reasons, their written vote will be requested by the tellers.
Can. 950 . Although a person has the right to vote in their own name due to their titles, they can only vote once.
Can. 951 . No one outside the group may be admitted to vote; Otherwise there is no choice by right.
Can. 952 . If the freedom of choice is hindered in any way, the choice itself is null and void.

Can. 953 . § 1 . He is incapable of voting: 1° incapable of performing a human act; 2° lacking active voice; 3. Anyone who has publicly renounced the Catholic faith or has publicly renounced communion with the Catholic Church. § 2 . If any of the above is admitted, your vote is null, but the election is valid, unless it is proven that the person elected did not obtain the required number of votes. Can. 954 - § 1 . There is no suffrage, unless it is: 1. free, and therefore there is no suffrage, if the elector is directly or indirectly induced by serious fear or deception to elect a certain person or several persons separately; 2nd secret, certain, absolute, determined rejected by contrary custom. § 2 . The conditions imposed on the vote prior to the election will be considered not added.

Can. 955 . § 1 . Before the start of the election, at least two tellers will be appointed from among the group. § 2 . The tellers will collect the votes and, in the presence of the election president, will examine whether the number of ballots corresponds to the number of voters; § 3 . If the number of votes is not equal to the number of voters, nothing is done. § 4 . The ballots will be destroyed immediately after the end of each vote or after the session, if several votes are held in the same session. § 5 . All the minutes of the election of the person acting as actuary are faithfully described and, after having been read in front of the voters, are signed by at least the same actuary, the president and the tellers, and are preserved in the group's files.

Can. 956 . § 1 . In elections, unless otherwise provided by common law, that which, in the presence of a larger part of those who must be called, has pleased an absolutely larger part of those present or, after two ineffective ballots, a relatively larger party on the third ballot, has the force of law; But if the votes are equal after the third vote, those elected will be considered older, unless they are elections among clerics or religious only, in which case those elected will be considered older by sacred ordination or older among religious of first profession. § 2 . The election of the president is to announce those elected.

Can. 957 . § 1 . The election will be immediately notified to the voter in writing or in another lawful manner. § 2 . The elected person must, within eight working days following receipt of the summons to be counted, declare to the president of the group whether or not he accepts the election; otherwise the election will have no effect. § 3 . If the chosen one does not accept, he or she loses all rights derived from the election, and the election is not validated by subsequent acceptance; but again he may be chosen; the group must proceed to a new election within one month of receiving information about the unaccepted election.

Can. 958 . The person elected by acceptance of the election, if confirmation is not required, immediately obtains full office, unless otherwise provided by law; Otherwise, he only acquires the right to demand confirmation of the election.

Can. 959 . § 1 . The voter, if the election requires confirmation, must request confirmation from the competent authority by himself or another person no later than eight days after the day of the accepted election; Otherwise, he will be deprived of all rights derived from the election, unless he proves that he was prevented by a just impediment from the requested confirmation. § 2 . Before receiving confirmation of the chosen one, he is not allowed to interfere in the administration of the office, and his actions cannot be blamed on anyone.

Can. 960 . § 1 . The competent authority, if it finds the candidate suitable and the election has been carried out in accordance with the law, may not deny confirmation. § 2 . Upon receipt of confirmation, the person elected exercises his or her position as a matter of right, unless otherwise provided by law. Art. II ON DEMAND

Can. 961 . Voters; If there is a canonical obstacle to the election of the one they consider most suitable and preferred, which can be dispensed with, they can with their votes, unless the law provides otherwise, demand it from the competent authority.
Can. 962 . For the application to be valid, at least two-thirds of the votes are required; Otherwise, the election will take place as if nothing had been done.

Can. 963 . § 1 . The group must send the request as soon as possible and within a maximum period of eight days to the competent authority to which it belongs to confirm the election; which authority, if it does not have the power to dispense with the impediment and wishes to admit the request, must obtain the dispensation from the competent authority; If confirmation is not required, the request must be sent to the competent authority to grant the waiver. § 2 . If the request is not sent within the established period, it is automatically null and void and the group loses the right to choose for that shift, unless it proves that it was prevented from sending the request due to a just impediment. § 3 . No right is acquired by demand; which the competent authority is not obliged to admit. § 4 . Voters cannot withdraw an application sent to the competent authority.

Can. 964 . § 1 . The right to vote is returned to the group if the request is not accepted by the competent authority. § 2 . The admission of the request is immediately hinted at by the request and saved Can. 957 , §§ 2 and 3. § 3 . Whoever accepts the accepted application immediately obtains the job with full rights. CHAPTER II ADMISSION OF OFFICE

Can. 965 . § 1 . Employment is lost, in addition to other cases prescribed by law, after the expiration of a certain period, reaching the age defined by law, resignation, transfer, dismissal and deprivation. § 2 . If the authority conferred on it is extinguished in any way by law, the duty is not lost, unless otherwise provided by law. § 3 . Once the established period has elapsed or the age determined by law has been reached, the loss of office only takes effect from the moment it is notified in writing by the competent authority. § 4 . Anyone who loses service by reaching the age determined by law or by resigning may obtain the title of retiree.
Can. 966 . The loss of the position carried out must be known as soon as possible by all those who have any right to the canonical provision of the position. Art. 1 ABOUT RESIGNATION
Can. 967 . He who has self-control can resign from office for just cause.
Can. 968 . A resignation made due to serious and unjustified fear, fraud, substantial error or fraud is not legally valid.

Can. 969 . To be valid, the resignation must be made in writing or in the presence of two witnesses from the authority to whom the canonical disposition of the position in question corresponds; Unless acceptance is required, it takes effect immediately.

Can. 970 . § 1 . A waiver, which requires acceptance, takes effect after the waiver has been communicated to the waiver; But if within three months the renunciant is not notified of the acceptance of the resignation, the resignation will be without any force. § 2 . The resignation can only be revoked by the renunciant before his acceptance has been intimated. § 3 . The authority will not accept a report that is not based on a fair and proportionate reason.
Can. 971 . Anyone who has resigned from a position may obtain the same position with another title. Art. II ON TRANSLATION

Can. 972 . § 1 . The transfer can only be made by the person who has the right to provide for the position that is lost, and at the same time for the position that is conferred upon him. § 2 . If the transfer is carried out against the will of the person holding the position, a serious cause is required and the procedure prescribed by law is observed, except for the rules relating to members of a religious institution or a society of common life, such as religious people, and it is always necessary to explain reasons contrary to the law. § 3 . For the transfer to take effect, it must be notified in writing.

Can. 973 . § 1 . In case of transfer, the first office assumed by the canonical possession of another office remains vacant, unless otherwise provided by law or prescribed by the competent authority. § 2 . He received the remuneration corresponding to the old transferred position, until he took the canonical possession of another. Art. 3. OF THE MOTION

Can. 974 . § 1 . A person can be removed from office either by decree of legally competent authority with broad observance of rights perhaps obtained from a contract or by law itself according to the Can. 976 standard. § 2 . The dismissal decision must be in writing to be effective.

Can. 975 . § 1 . Except as otherwise provided by law, no one may be removed from a position assigned to him for an indefinite period, except for serious cause and in the manner prescribed by law. The same goes for the fact that a person can be removed from a position conferred for a certain period, before said period has elapsed. § 2 . The position that, according to the provisions of the law, is conferred on a person at the prudent discretion of the competent authority, may be removed for just cause that will be assessed in the judgment of the same authority, in equity.

Can. 976 . § 1 . By right, the following will be removed from office: 1° who has lost his clerical status; 2° who has publicly renounced the Catholic faith or has publicly renounced communion with the Catholic Church; 3. a clergyman who tried to get married, even if it was only civil. § 2 . The elimination, of which in § 1, nos. 2 and 3, can only be executed if confirmed by declaration from the same competent authority.

Can. 977 . If a person is removed, not by right, but by decree of a competent authority, from the position which provides him with his subsistence, the same authority shall ensure that he is provided with subsistence for an appropriate period, unless otherwise provided. Art. IV OF PRIVATION
Can. 978 . Deprivation of office can only be imposed as punishment for a crime. TITLE XXI OF THE POWER OF THE GOVERNMENT

Can. 979 . § 1 . The power of government, which is a divine institution in the Church, is limited by law to those who are named in the sacred order. § 2 . In the exercise of government power, other Christians may cooperate according to the law.

Can. 980 . § 1 . The power of government is different in the external forum and different in the internal forum, whether sacramental or not. § 2 . If the power of the government is exercised only for the internal market, the effects that its exercise was intended to have for the external market are not recognized in this market, except to the extent determined by law for specific cases.

Can. 981 . § 1 . The ordinary power of government is that which is attributed by right to some office; delegate, which is not granted to the person himself through the position. § 2 . The power of the ordinary government can be its own or indirect.

Can. 982 . § 1 . The usual powers are governed by the provisions of the delegated power. § 2 . But the usual power granted to the Hierarch, unless otherwise provided for in its grant, or chosen by the energy of the person, does not perish by the rescission of the right of the Hierarch to whom it was granted, but passes to any Hierarch who succeeds him in the government.

Can. 983 . § 1 . Whoever claims to be a delegate has the burden of proving the delegation. § 2 . A delegate who exceeds the limits of his mandate, whether in things or people, does nothing. § 3 . A delegate who, in a manner other than that determined therein, carries out those things for which he has been delegated, is not understood to exceed the limits of his mandate, unless the delegator himself prescribes a method for its validity.

Can. 984 . § 1 . In addition to the Roman Pontiff, the hierarchs are mainly the Patriarch, the Major Archbishop, the Metropolitan, who presides over the independent metropolitan Church, and the eparchial Bishop, as well as those who temporarily succeed them in government according to law. § 2 . The local hierarchs, in addition to the Roman Pontiff, are the eparchial Bishop, the Exarch, the Apostolic Administrator, who, if the previous ones are lacking, legitimately succeed to the government in the meantime, as well as the Protosincellus and Syncellus; But the patriarch, the major archbishop, the metropolitan, who presides over the independent metropolitan church, as well as those who meanwhile succeed them in government according to the rule of law, are local hierarchs only in the area of ​​the eparchy that they govern, firmly Can. 101 . § 3 . The superior elders in the institutes of consecrated life, who are endowed with the power of ordinary government, are also Hierarchs, but not local.

Can. 985 . § 1 . The power of the government is divided into legislative, executive and judicial. § 2 . The legislative power must be exercised in the manner prescribed by law, and that which the legislator has in the Church below the supreme authority of the Church cannot be validly delegated, except as otherwise provided in the common law; A law contrary to a higher law cannot be validly passed by an inferior legislator. § 3 . The judicial power held by judges or judicial boards must be exercised in the manner prescribed by law and cannot be validly delegated except for the performance of preparatory acts for any decree or sentence.

Can. 986 . A person, even if he exists outside the borders of the territory, may exercise executive power over subjects, even absent from the territory, unless otherwise provided by common law or determined by the nature of the matter; on foreigners who actually reside in the territory, if it involves granting favors or ordering the execution either by common law or by particular law, to which they are obliged according to the Can. 1491, § 3 standard.

Can. 987 . What the common law and the particular law of the independent Church specifically grant to the eparchial bishop in the area of ​​the executive power of the government, is understood to belong only to the eparchial bishop and the exarch, excluding the Protosyncello and Syncelli, except by special mandate.

Can. 988 . § 1 . The ordinary executive power may be delegated either to act or for all cases, unless expressly provided otherwise by law. § 2 . The executive power delegated by the Apostolic See or by the Patriarch may be subdelegated, either for an act or for all cases, unless the power of the person is selected or subdelegation is expressly prohibited. § 3 . The executive power delegated by another authority that has ordinary power, if it has been delegated for all cases, may only be subdelegated in individual cases; but if it has been delegated for an act or acts for which it has been extinguished, it cannot be validly subdelegated except with the express consent of the delegater. § 4 . No subdelegated power may be validly subdelegated again, unless expressly authorized by the person delegating it.

Can. 989 . The ordinary executive power, as well as the power delegated to the universe of cases, must be interpreted in a broad sense, but any other in a strict sense; But to whom the power is delegated, those without which the same power cannot be exercised are also understood to have been granted.

Can. 990 . § 1 . The executive power delegated to the majority is presumed to be individually delegated to it. § 2 . When the conduct of the same business is delegated individually to several persons, the one who first begins to manage it excludes others from doing the same, unless he is later prevented or refuses to continue in the conduct of the business. § 3 . In the event that several delegates act collectively, all must proceed according to the provisions of the statutes on collegiate acts, unless otherwise provided in the mandate.

Can. 991 . § 1 . Ordinary power is lost due to the loss of the position to which it is assigned. § 2 . Unless otherwise provided by law, the ordinary power is suspended if an appeal or judicial remedy is filed against the dismissal or removal from office.

Can. 992 . § 1 . The delegated power is lost at the end of the mandate; upon expiration of the contribution time or exhaustion of the number of cases for which contributions have been made; on the termination of the cause of definitive delegation; the revocation of the delegate communicated directly to the delegate as well as the resignation of the delegate made to the delegate and accepted by him; but not by right of the delegate, unless it appears from the attached clauses. § 2 . On the contrary, an act of delegated power, which is exercised only for the internal market, is inadvertently valid after time has elapsed or after the number of cases has been exhausted.
Can. 993 . The executive power of the government is not suspended by the filing of an appeal, unless otherwise expressly provided by common law.

Can. 994 . In a general error of fact or law, and also in a positive and probable doubt, whether of law or fact, the Church provides the executive power of the government for the forum, both external and internal.

Can. 995 . The provisions of the law apply to the executive branch of the government, unless the common law provides otherwise or appears from the nature of the matter, including the power mentioned in cann. 441, § 1 and 511, § 1 and the powers that are legally required for the effective celebration or administration of the sacraments. TITLE XXII OF APPEALS AGAINST ADMINISTRATIVE DECREES

Can. 996 . What is established in the canons of this title on decrees applies to all individual administrative acts that are imposed in an external forum by any legitimate power of the Church outside the court, except those that are initiated by the Roman Pontiff or the Ecumenical Council.

Can. 997 . § 1 Whoever considers himself burdened by a decree may, in accordance with the law, appeal to a higher authority than the one who made this decree. § 2 . The first appeal against the decrees of the Protosyncelli or Syncelli is filed before the eparchial bishop, and against the decrees of those who act by delegated authority, before the delegate.

Can. 998 . § 1 . It is highly desirable that, if anyone believes himself aggrieved by a decree, there should not be a dispute between him and the author of the decree, but that an equitable solution should be sought between them, perhaps by employing serious men for mediation or study, so that the dispute may be settled by a voluntary amendment of the decree, or by just compensation, or by some other suitable means. § 2 . The higher authority will inform the parties of these before receiving the appeal.

Can. 999 . § 1 . Before anyone files an appeal, they must request the revocation or modification of the decree in writing from the author of the same within the peremptory period of ten days from the notification of the decree; by which request it is understood that the suspension of execution is also requested by law. § 2 . The obligation to request the revocation or modification of the decree does not apply, if it is the first appeal against the decrees, mentioned in Can. 997 , § 2 , or if it is a question of subsequent appeals, except appeals against the decrees of the Eparchial Bishop, by which any first appeal has been decided.

Can. 1000 . § 1 . In cases where the appeal stays the execution of the decree, the petition, as described in Can. 999 , § 1 , also does the same. § 2 . In other cases, unless the author of the decree suspends its execution within ten days following receipt of the request, the temporary suspension may be requested from the higher authority, which may only decide for serious reasons and with caution, so that the safety of souls is not jeopardized; If an appeal is subsequently filed, the authority hearing the appeal decides whether to confirm or revoke the suspension of the execution of the decree. § 3 . If no appeal is filed against the decree within the stated period, or if the appeal is filed solely to request compensation for damages, the suspension of the execution of the decree automatically ceases.

Can. 1001 . § 1 . The appeal must be filed within the peremptory period of fifteen days. § 2 . The period of fifteen days runs: 1° in the case in which the request for revocation or modification of the decree must be submitted in advance, from the day of notification of the decree on which the author first modified the decree or rejected the petition, or, if nothing has been decided, from the thirtieth day counted from the receipt of the petition; 2° in other cases, from the day on which the decree was issued.

Can. 1002 . The higher authority must issue the decision by which the appeal is resolved within sixty days following its receipt, unless the particular law of the independent Church establishes other terms; But if this has not been done and the appellant requests in writing that this decree be issued, counting the thirtieth day since this request was received, if even then nothing has been done, the appeal will be considered rejected as if it had been rejected by decree of that day, so that a new appeal can be filed against it.

Can. 1003 . In appeals against administrative decrees, it remains admissible, referring to Can. 1517; the appellant always has the right to resort to an agent or a lawyer for the useless habits of life; rather, an ex officio patron may be appointed if the appellant lacks a patron and a higher authority deems it necessary; However, a higher authority can always order the appellant to appear in person for questioning.

Can. 1004 . The higher authority hearing the appeal can not only confirm the decree or declare it void, but also rescind and revoke it, but not modify it, unless by the particular right of its own independent Church this power is also given to the higher authority.

Can. 1005 . Although the decree was confirmed by a higher authority, nothing was declared, rescinded, revoked or modified, regarding the reparation of damages, if any were due, responded the one who made the first decree; However, the higher authority is so far only liable to the extent that its decree has caused damage.

Can. 1006 . The appeal against an administrative decree of the Patriarch, even if it is a decree affecting the Patriarch's eparchy, or a decree against which the Patriarch decides to appeal, is presented to a special group of bishops to establish a particular rule of law, unless the matter is referred to the Apostolic See; There is no recourse against the decision of this group other than challenging it before the Roman Pontiff himself. Lettera Apostolica in forma di Motu Proprio - Ab initio - of November 21, 2020):

Can. 1007 . To seek the spiritual good of men, the Church needs and uses temporal goods, to the extent that its own mission demands it; Therefore, it has the natural right to acquire, possess, manage and dispose of those temporal goods that are necessary for its own purposes, especially for divine worship, for works of apostolate and charity, and for the adequate support of ministers.

Can. 1008 . § 1 . The Roman Pontiff is the supreme administrator and steward of all the temporal goods of the Church. § 2 . The ownership of the temporal goods of the Church, under the supreme authority of the Roman Pontiff, belongs to the legal entity that legitimately acquired them.

Can. 1009 . § 1 . Any legal person is a subject capable of acquiring, possessing, managing and disposing of temporal property in accordance with canon law. § 2 . Ecclesiastical property is all temporary property belonging to legal persons. CHAPTER I. ACQUISITION OF TEMPORARY GOODS
Can. 1010 . Legal entities can acquire temporary assets in the same ways as others.
Can. 1011 . The competent authority has the right to demand from the Christian faithful what is necessary for the Church's own purposes.

Can. 1012 . § 1 . It is the right of the eparchial bishop, to the extent necessary for the good of the eparchy, to impose on the legal persons subordinate to him taxes proportional to the income of each person, with the consent of the council of financial affairs; but no tax may be imposed on the offerings received on the occasion of the celebration of the Divine Liturgy. § 2 . Taxes may only be imposed on natural persons in accordance with the particular law of the independent Church.

Can. 1013 . § 1 . It is up to the eparchial bishop to determine, within the limits established by the particular law of his own independent Church, those imposed by the various acts of governmental power and the offerings on the occasion of the celebration of the Divine Liturgy, the sacraments, sacramentals or any other liturgical celebrations, unless otherwise provided by common law. § 2 . The patriarchs and eparchial bishops of the different independent churches that exercise their power in the same territory must ensure that the councils establish the same norm regarding taxes and offerings.
Can. 1014 . In all churches customarily open to the faithful, the eparchial bishop may order that offerings be collected for specific church projects.

Can. 1015 . Natural or legal persons are not permitted to collect alms except with the permission of the authority to which they are subject and with the written consent of the Hierarch of the place where the alms are collected.

Can. 1016 . § 1 . Offers made for a specific purpose can only be intended for that purpose. § 2 . Unless otherwise provided, offers made to the directors or administrators of any legal entity are presumed to have been made by the legal entity itself. § 3 . These offerings cannot be rejected except for just cause and in matters of greater importance with the permission of the Hierarch; The permission of the same Hierarch is required to be accepted, which carry a burden or modal condition with the signature Can. 1042.
Can. 1017 . The Church receives the prescription according to the cann. 1540 - 1542 norm also for temporal goods.

Can. 1018 . Sacred things, which, of course, are intended for divine worship by dedication or blessing, if they are in the possession of private individuals, may be acquired by private individuals by prescription, but it is not permitted to use them for profane purposes, unless they have lost their dedication or blessing; If they belong to an ecclesiastical legal entity, they can only be acquired by another ecclesiastical legal entity.

Can. 1019 . Real estate, valuable movable things, which of course are of great importance for the sake of art or history or material, rights and actions, personal or real, that belong to the Apostolic See, are prescribed for a period of one hundred years; those that belong to any autonomous Church or eparchy, for a period of fifty years, and those that belong to another legal entity, for a period of thirty years.

Can. 1020 . § 1 . Every authority has the serious obligation to guarantee that temporal goods acquired by the Church are registered in the name of the legal entity to which they belong, observing all the provisions of civil law that safeguard the rights of the Church. § 2 . However, if civil law does not allow temporal property to be registered in the name of a legal entity, each authority shall ensure that, after hearing civil law experts and competent lawyers, the rights of the Church remain intact in the ways valid under civil law. § 3 . These provisions also apply to temporary assets legally owned by a legal entity, the acquisition of which has not yet been documented. § 4 . The immediately higher authority is obliged to enforce these rules.

Can. 1021 . § 1 . In each eparchy there will be, according to the norm of the particular law of its own independent Church, a special institution, which collects goods or offerings for its purpose, so that adequate and fundamentally equal sustenance is adequately provided for all the clerics who render service in favor of the eparchy, unless otherwise provided. § 2 . When prevention and social security, as well as health care for clerics, have not yet been adequately organized, the particular law of each autonomous Church provides for the creation of institutions that put them safe under the supervision of the local Hierarch. § 3 . In each eparchy, to the extent necessary, a common mass should be established in the manner determined by the particular law of the independent Church, by which the eparchial bishops can satisfy their obligations to the other members of the Church and satisfy the various needs of the eparchy, and by which even the richest eparchy can help the poorest. CHAPTER II OF THE ADMINISTRATION OF ECCLESIASTICAL PROPERTY

Can. 1022 . § 1 . It is the responsibility of the eparchial bishop to ensure the administration of all ecclesiastical assets, which are within the limits of the eparchy and are not subject to its administrative power, except for legitimate titles that confer more important rights. § 2 . Taking into account the rights, customs and legitimate circumstances, the Hierarchs, giving appropriate instructions within the limits of the common law and the particular law of their own Church, ensure that the entire administration of ecclesiastical property is properly organized.
Can. 1023 . The administration of ecclesiastical assets corresponds to the legal entity that directly governs them, unless otherwise provided by law.

Can. 1024 . § 1 . Acts that exceed the limits and methods of ordinary administration may not be validly placed in the administrator of ecclesiastical assets, unless consent is granted in writing by the competent authority. § 2 . The acts that exceed the limits and form of ordinary administration will be determined in the statutes; But if the statutes say nothing on this matter, it is up to the authority to which the legal entity is directly subject to determine such acts in consultation with a competent council. § 3 . Except when and to the extent that it is directed to its purpose, the legal entity is not obliged to respond for acts carried out by the administrators invalidly.

Can. 1025 . Before the administrator of ecclesiastical property begins to perform his duties, he must: 1. make a promise to the Hierarch or his delegate that he will faithfully fulfill his duty; 2° sign a detailed inventory, reviewed by the Hierarch, of the ecclesiastical assets entrusted to his administration.

Can. 1026 . One copy of the inventory of ecclesiastical property will be kept in the archive of the legal entity to which they belong, the other in the archive of the eparchial court; Any changes that may occur to the stable assets of the same legal entity will be recorded in both copies.

Can. 1027 . The authorities must ensure that the administrators of ecclesiastical property provide appropriate and valid guarantees under civil law, so that the Church does not suffer any loss from the same administrators who die or cease to hold office.

Can. 1028 . § 1 . Every administrator of ecclesiastical property is obliged to fulfill his duty with the care of a good father of a family. § 2 . From here he must especially: 1° ensure that the ecclesiastical property entrusted to his care does not perish in any way, nor suffer any loss when entering into insurance contracts, to the extent necessary, for this purpose; 2° observe the norms of canon and civil law, as well as those imposed by the founder or the donor or by the competent authority, and above all take care that no damage is caused to the Church due to non-observance of civil law; 3° demand the return of the goods and the product accurately and at the right time and keep the exact figures and spend them according to the founder's design or legitimate norms; 4° ensure that the debt or loan or mortgage to be paid is paid at the appointed time and that the sum of the capital of the debt is returned in a timely manner; 5° invest, with the consent of the Hierarch, the money that is left over from expenses and can be usefully invested in the purposes of the Church or a legal entity; 6° have well-organized receipt and expense books; 7° settle the administration account at the end of each year; 8° organize the documents on which the rights of a legal entity over ecclesiastical property are based and keep them in the archive, and deposit their authentic copies, where appropriate, in the archive of the eparchial court. § 3 . The forecast of income and expenses, which must be formulated annually by the administrators of ecclesiastical assets, is highly recommended; but a particular law can prescribe it and determine more precisely the form in which it must be presented.

Can. 1029 . The administrator of ecclesiastical property will not make donations of movable property that does not belong to the permanent patrimony, except those moderated according to legitimate custom, except for the just cause of piety or charity.

Can. 1030 . The administrator of ecclesiastical property: 1° in the leasing of works, he will also scrupulously observe the civil law relating to work and social life, according to the principles transmitted by the Church; 2° to those who carry out the work according to the conditions, he must give them fair remuneration, so that they can adequately satisfy their needs and those of their people.

Can. 1031 . § 1 . Rejected contrary to custom, the administrator of ecclesiastical property must render an account of the administration every year to his own Hierarch. § 2 . For the temporal goods offered to the Church, the administrator of ecclesiastical goods will render a public account in the manner established by particular law, unless the local Hierarch has determined otherwise for serious reasons.

Can. 1032 . The administrator of ecclesiastical assets cannot initiate or contest a lawsuit on behalf of a legal entity in civil jurisdiction, except with the permission of the corresponding Hierarch.

Can. 1033 . The administrator of ecclesiastical property, who dismissed an office or office at his own discretion, is obliged to make restitution, if as a result of the arbitrary dismissal damage is caused to the Church. CHAPTER III CONTRACTS, ESPECIALLY DISPOSAL

Can. 1034 . What the civil law of the territory where the contract is concluded determines about contracts in kind and in particular, and about payments, the same canon law in matters that are subject to the power of the Church, is observed with the same effects.

Can. 1035 . § 1 . To transfer ecclesiastical assets that constitute a stable legal entity from the legitimate transfer of assets, the following are required: 1. a just cause such as urgent need, obvious utility, piety, charity or pastoral reason; 2° a written evaluation of the matter that must be disposed of by experts; 3° in the cases provided for by law, the consent of the competent authority is granted in writing, without which the sale is null. § 2 . Other precautions prescribed by the competent authority must also be observed to avoid damage to the Church.

Can. 1036 . § 1 . If the value of the ecclesiastical property whose disposal is proposed is contained within the minimum sum and the maximum sum established by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church or by the Apostolic See, the consent is required: 1° of the financial council and the college of eparchial counselors, if it concerns eparchy property; 2° of the eparchial bishop, who in the case needs the consent of the finance council and the college of eparchial counselors, if it concerns assets of a legal person subject to the same eparchial bishop; 3° the authority determined in the type or statutes, if it concerns property of a legal person not subject to the eparchial bishop. § 2 . In Patriarchal Churches, if the value of the property exceeds the maximum sum established by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, but not twice, consent is required: 1° granted by the Patriarch with the consent of the permanent Synod, if it concerns property of an eparchy located within the territory of the Patriarchal Church, unless the particular law of the same Church provides otherwise; 2° given by the eparchial bishop as well as by the Patriarch with the consent of the permanent Synod, if it concerns property of a legal person subject to the eparchial bishop who exercises his authority in the territory of the patriarchal Church; 3° Given by the Patriarch with the consent of the permanent Synod, if it concerns property of a legal person not subject to the eparchial bishop, even if it is of pontifical right, that are within the territory of the Patriarchal Church. § 3 . In Patriarchal Churches, if the value of goods exceeds twice the maximum sum established by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, and if they are valuable things or things donated by the will of the Church, § 2 is preserved, but the Patriarch needs the consent of the same Synod. § 4 . In other cases, the consent of the Apostolic See is required, if the value of the goods exceeds the sum established or approved by the Apostolic See itself and, if they are valuable things or donated by the Church.

Can. 1037 . To dispose of the temporal property of the Patriarchal Church or of the eparchy of the Patriarch, the Patriarch needs: 1° the advice of the permanent Synod, if the value of the property is contained within the minimum and maximum sum established by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church and if it concerns property of the Patriarchal Church; but if it is only the property of the Patriarch's eparchy, Can. 1036 , § 1 , n. 1; 2° with the consent of the permanent Synod, if the value of the property exceeds the maximum sum fixed by the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, but not twice; 3. with the consent of the Synod of Bishops of the Patriarchal Church, if the value of the goods exceeds double the same sum and if they are valuable things or donated by the will of the Church.

Can. 1038 . § 1 .
